This can also refer to someone who's unskillful at something as well." "The reading doesn't follow any of the rules you've run into. It's まずい. Think about how you're going through this really long maze (まず) and how you're promised a really tasty wonderful treat at the end for getting through it (you're a lab rat or something). When you get to the end, there's your treat! What joy! You eat it and... oh man... it is so bad tasting you can't even believe it. Be sure to imagine the terrible taste and the terrible disappointment after going through that difficult maze only to get this... this... terribly unappetizing cheese."

notes: "This word is made up of a single kanji with hiragana attached to it. That hiragana ends with い which means it's an adjective. So, what's the adjective form of the kanji that's in this word? 円 means both ""yen"" and ""round"" but in this case we're looking at the round one (because something isn't going to be ""yenny""). The adjective version of round is round or circular. Just like a yen coin, this ""round"" is a flat round. As in, if you draw a circle on a piece of paper, you could use this word. Same goes with yen, which is why ""yen"" and ""round"" both use the same kanji." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: The reading for the 円 portion of this word is the same as a kanji you're learning in this level: 丸. That kanji means something really similar to this kanji. And guess what? They also share a reading. So, if you know that the reading of 丸 is まる then you'll also know that the reading for this word is まる!"

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は案外いい人かも知れない。
example_sentences.english: He may unexpectedly turn out to be a good person.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたのやり方はずるい。
example_sentences.english: Your method is cunning.

example_sentences.japanese: 夏の日差しがまぶしかったよ。
example_sentences.english: The summer sunlight was dazzling.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は彼の意見に賛成だ。
example_sentences.english: I agree with his opinion.

example_sentences.japanese: この計算は面倒臭いなあ。
example_sentences.english: This calculation is troublesome.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼らはとても愉快な人たちです。
example_sentences.english: They're very pleasant people.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は苦いコーヒーが好きです。
example_sentences.english: I like bitter coffee.

notes: "A person of industry makes a lot of things by hand, so everything they make is artificial, and also means it's man made." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたののうは、ほんとうに人工ののうなんですか？
example_sentences.english: Is your brain really artificial?

example_sentences.japanese: この川は、人工の川です。
example_sentences.english: This river is man-made.

example_sentences.japanese: にわに人工しばをしいてみました。
example_sentences.english: I put artificial turf in the garden.

notes: "した is the past tense form of する (which means ""to do""). So, essentially this word is ""did big."" What is something that ""did big""? It's something that's great or considerable." "The reading for the 大 part is actually the on'yomi reading you learned when learning its kanji. So, as long as you remember that (and remember to use that reading), you can read this word as well. 大した = たいした."

example_sentences.japanese: それは大したことはない。
example_sentences.english: It’s not a big deal.

example_sentences.japanese: まったく大した女だよ。
example_sentences.english: She is such a great woman.

example_sentences.japanese: マクドナルドのしゃちょうになれれば大したものだ。
example_sentences.english: Being the president of McDonald’s would be a big deal.

notes: "This word uses white and person ... put those together and you have a white person, aka a caucasian person." As a jukugo word, it follows all the rules and uses the on'yomi readings from the kanji (both of which you know from learning the kanji).

example_sentences.japanese: 白人だんせいとけっこんしました。
example_sentences.english: I married a white man.

example_sentences.japanese: わたしはケニア出しんのこく人ですが、アメリカの白人かぞくにそだてられました。
example_sentences.english: I am black and from Kenya, but I was raised by a white family in America.

example_sentences.japanese: おおくの白人たちは、日本のなつが大のにが手だ。
example_sentences.english: Many caucasians hate summer in Japan.

english: Good At, Skillful, Skilled At, Skilled
notes: "Think of someone holding out their hand. This is average. Things rated below the hand are things you're bad at. Things rated above the hand are things you're good at." "Both of these kanji use on'yomi reading, though 手 uses an on'yomi reading you didn't learn with the kanji. It's a rare reading, so it wasn't included (and we just have to deal with exceptions like this as we go along). To remember the reading for this word, here's a mnemonic:What are you good at? You're really good at taking Jourm (じょう) to the zoo (ず). No one else can take Jourm to the zoo, he gets mad and throws them into the animal enclosures. But you? Jourm trusts you."

example_sentences.japanese: さとうさんは、うたを上手にうたいます。
example_sentences.english: Satou is good at singing.

example_sentences.japanese: オリーブオイルのつかいかたが上手な王子をしっていますか。
example_sentences.english: Do you know any princes who are good at using olive oil?

example_sentences.japanese: わたしはへんがおをつくるのが上手です。
example_sentences.english: I’m good at making funny faces.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it uses the kun'yomi reading. You haven't learned this reading yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you:Imagine hearing someone to your left saying, ""Hi Da'ri!"" (ひだり) which is supposed to be ""Hi There,"" or ""Hi Dearie."" You turn left and there's no one there. You hear it again, ""Hi Da'ri!"" Keep turning to the left until you find the person saying hi to you."

example_sentences.japanese: わたしは、左ききです。
example_sentences.english: I’m left-handed.

example_sentences.japanese: 左の山のなまえはなんですか？
example_sentences.english: What's the name of the mountain on the left?

example_sentences.japanese: あのむすめが左みみのピアスをあけたときのことがわすれられない。
example_sentences.english: I will never forget the time that girl got her left ear pierced.

notes: "Person person, why, that's more than one person. It's people! It's everybody!" "The reading is the vocab word 人 twice, with the second one getting rendaku'd, turning it into びと."

example_sentences.japanese: なぜ人々はくるまをかうのでしょうか？
example_sentences.english: Why do people buy cars?

example_sentences.japanese: おおくのパプアニューギニアの人々は水中でもいきができるらしい。
example_sentences.english: I heard that many Papuan people can breathe underwater.

example_sentences.japanese: このちいきの人々は、みんないい人ばかりです。
example_sentences.english: The people in the area are all just good natured people.

notes: "If you're in the middle of a bunch of water, then you're most likely underwater. " This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 水中でしか使えない。
example_sentences.english: It can only be used underwater.

example_sentences.japanese: 右をみると、水中のせかいがひろがっていました。
example_sentences.english: When I looked to the right, there was an underwater world in front of me.

example_sentences.japanese: 水中でめをあけることができません。
example_sentences.english: I can’t open my eyes underwater.

english: Unskillful, Unskilled, Bad At, Not Good At, Not Skilled
notes: "Think of someone holding out their hand at shoulder level. Anything above that equals ""skillful."" Everything below that equals ""unskillful. So, in the case of this word, ""below hand"" means ""unskillful.""" "If you're bad at something and you complain about it, then you're just a hater (へた). Don't be a hater."

example_sentences.japanese: ギターはまだ下手ですが、まいばんれんしゅうしています。
example_sentences.english: I’m still bad at the guitar, but I practice every night.

example_sentences.japanese: アメリカ人のまねが下手な人は、フランス人のまねが上手です。
example_sentences.english: The person, who is not good at imitating Americans, is good at imitating French people.

example_sentences.japanese: わたしははをみがくのが下手です。
example_sentences.english: I’m bad at brushing my teeth.

notes: "Normally a single kanji alone like this would mean the same thing as its parent kanji, but in the case of 生 it's a little different (but still related). When you think of something that has life, it's something that's very fresh or raw. Think sashimi or sushi, for example. You want that to be as close as possible to life as you can. That's why you eat it when it's fresh, and that's also when you eat it raw.You'll see this word at the beginning of other words. For example, 生たまご is ""raw egg.""" "This uses one of the kun'yomi readings. To remember this one, though, think this:When you get a raw fish in Japan, you never want to name (なま) it, because you'll probably have to eat it (and that would be traumatizing!). Just imagine yourself actually doing that - how terrible would that be?"

example_sentences.japanese: 生チョコをつくりました。
example_sentences.english: I made ganache.

example_sentences.japanese: 生のやさいはにが手です。
example_sentences.english: I don't like raw veggies.

example_sentences.japanese: 生ビール一ちょう、下さーい。
example_sentences.english: Give me a draft beer!

notes: "Think back to the old old olden days. Back when decisions were made with swords. A big cut is going to be important. Just imagine a couple samurai squaring off, then charging, then making one big cut. It's the most important thing they'll do in their lives (if they live!)." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: これは、メアリーが大切にしている人ぎょうです。
example_sentences.english: This is the doll that Mary treats with a great deal of care.

example_sentences.japanese: そばにいてくれる友人やこい人、かぞくを大切にした方がいいですよ。
example_sentences.english: You should cherish your friends, partner, and family who stand by you.

example_sentences.japanese: 大切なしょるいときくと、いつも中みをみたくなる。
example_sentences.english: Whenever I hear that a document is very important, I always want to look at what’s inside.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it should use the kun'yomi reading. When learning the kanji, you didn't learn that reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you with this word:There's something inside and you wanna get to what's within. Look inside. Ooh, cheese (うち)! Your favorite. Ooh cheese, how I love you."

example_sentences.japanese: はこの内がわをピンクいろにぬってください。
example_sentences.english: Please paint the inside of the box pink.

example_sentences.japanese: てきは内にあり。
example_sentences.english: There is an enemy within.

example_sentences.japanese: 内にひめたおもいを、日きにつづった。
example_sentences.english: The thoughts I hide inside myself were spelled out in my diary.

notes:
"The city stand is municipal in nature. Municipal means ""of or relating to a city or its governing body"", and this vocabulary means just that. Or just city. City is fine too." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

"The place where I stand is my own private area. Think of the ""circle of personal space."" This is where you stand plus an arm's length. This area is very private to you. Who knows what you do in your own private area." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: そぼは市立びょういんに入いんしています。
example_sentences.english: My grandmother is hospitalized at the municipal hospital.

example_sentences.japanese: 市立としょかんまでのみちをおしえてください。
example_sentences.english: Please tell me the direction to the municipal library.

example_sentences.japanese: 大さか市立大がくのまえでさか立ちをした。
example_sentences.english: I stood on my head in front of Osaka City University.

example_sentences.japanese: 私立のようちえんはクリスマスの日はお休みだよ。
example_sentences.english: The private kindergartens are closed on the Christmas Day.

example_sentences.japanese: ここを出て、前の通りを左の方へ三つ目の交さ点まで歩くと、その私立病院に着きますよ。
example_sentences.english: Go out of here and walk left along the street until you come to the third intersection and you'll get to the private hospital.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチがカフェでこっそり会っていた男の人は、私立探偵だったということが判明しました。
example_sentences.english: I found out that the guy Koichi secretly met at the cafe was a private detective.

notes: "The combination of kanji doesn't make perfect sense, but it's alright. Take something that's middle old and you have something that's used or secondhand. It's not 100% old yet... it's still in the middle, meaning you can give it to someone else to use, like your younger siblings." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 中古ですが、ベンツをかいました。
example_sentences.english: It’s used, but I bought a Benz.

example_sentences.japanese: このあたりは、中古ショップがじゅうじつしています。
example_sentences.english: There are a lot of secondhand stores in this area.

example_sentences.japanese: 中古のかぐのような人とはけっこんしたくない。
example_sentences.english: I don’t want to get married to someone who is like a piece of used furniture.

english: Bold Letter, Bold, Bold Character, Bold Text, Boldface
notes: "What do you think a fat letter is? If I were to guess, I'd say a bold letter." "The reading for this one is a bit odd. The 太 uses the ふと from ふとい (kun'yomi) and the 字 is just the normal on'yomi reading for ""letter."" You have to remember this weird mismatched reading pair on your own, I'm afraid. Perhaps if you think about how fat letters don't really fit with the rest of the text, kind of like how the readings of both kanji also don't fit in it will help?"

example_sentences.japanese: この字は太字にしてください。
example_sentences.english: Make this character bold, please.

example_sentences.japanese: マンションのエレベーターにのったら、でんこうけいじばんに赤い太字で「じしんです今すぐ外に出てください｣とかひょうじが出てきて、マジびびったよ。
example_sentences.english: "When I got on the elevator in my apartment, the bold, red message appeared saying ""Earthquake! Get out of this elevator right now,"" on the electric bulletin board so I got really scared."

example_sentences.japanese: 太字にすることで、その言葉を強調しましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let’s put this in bold to add more emphasis.

notes: "You have a flat energy. What kind of energy would be a flat one? Probably a cool or calm one. You'd also tell people about this flat energy by saying you are all right or just okay." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: よく平気でいられますね。
example_sentences.english: How come you’re always so calm?

example_sentences.japanese: 王女はペットの子犬をなくしても平気な人です。
example_sentences.english: The princess is a type of person who wouldn't get upset even if she lost her pet puppy.

example_sentences.japanese: 夫が会社を首になったが、意外と平気だ。
example_sentences.english: My husband was fired, but I’m surprisingly calm.

notes: "The middle of the central... that is really, really in the center if you ask me (and is very central as well). This is one of those ""overdid it on the meaning"" words." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 中央に立っているのが、田中さんのおねえさんです。
example_sentences.english: That’s Tanaka’s older sister standing in the center.

example_sentences.japanese: 大さかえきの、中央かいさつ口でまっています。
example_sentences.english: I’m waiting for you at the central ticket gate of Osaka station.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の頭の中央部分には小さな凹みがある。
example_sentences.english: I have a little dent in the center of my head.

notes: "What is the origin of your energy? It is your spirit and health (though this vocab word also means energy as well)." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: お父さんは、元気ですか。
example_sentences.english: How is your father?

example_sentences.japanese: かなちゃんは、元気いっぱいですね。
example_sentences.english: Kana is full of energy.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は元気そうに見えたが、実はひどい下りだったらしい。
example_sentences.english: He seemed fine but apparently he had a bad diarrhea.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same with a little hiragana sticking out. Because the hiragana doesn't really indicate what it is, it's okay to assume that they share meanings as well. "Since this word is made up of a kanji plus some hiragana attached, it should use the kun'yomi reading. When learning the kanji, you didn't learn that reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you with this word: Something is very, very flat. Perhaps someone who doesn't eat much, like a model? Which model? Let's imagine it's Tyra (たいら) Banks."

example_sentences.japanese: パソコンを、どこか平らなところにおいてください。
example_sentences.english: Put your PC somewhere flat, please.

example_sentences.japanese: その女の子は赤のビー玉を八つ平らなところにおいた。
example_sentences.english: That girl put eight red marbles in a flat place.

example_sentences.japanese: 平らで細長いパスタの名前覚えてない？
example_sentences.english: Do you remember the name of the pasta that is thin, long and flat?

english: Head Of Household, Husband, Head Of A Household, Head Of The Household, Landlord, Master
notes: "The master person isn't just a master. You have to think back to when they were making these kanji. Who was the master? It was the head of household. This head of household probably told servants what to do and was all bossy and stuff. He was the master person. Also, this often means husband. Because, I guess the head of household back in the day was the husband. Those sexist ancient people!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: きのう、ご主人とどこかへいきましたか？
example_sentences.english: Did you and your husband go somewhere yesterday?

example_sentences.japanese: ご主人さま、それは少しかいすぎではないでしょうか。
example_sentences.english: I'm afraid you bought too many of them, master.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の主人は何の信念も無い政治家なんです。
example_sentences.english: My husband is a politician who doesn’t have any conviction.

notes: "When you have something that's not correct, you have no justice. In fact, you have injustice. Just imagine yourself being put in an unjust situation, and think about how not correct it is." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 不正をはたらいたのはだれですか。
example_sentences.english: Who did something dishonest?

example_sentences.japanese: 中ごくからの不正アクセスにより、トーフグのSNSアカウントがぜんぶのっとられてしまった。
example_sentences.english: There was unauthorized access from China and all of Tofugu's social media accounts were hacked.

example_sentences.japanese: 俺の叔母は、いつも自分が今までにした不正やごまかしについて話をする。
example_sentences.english: My aunt always talks about her personal acts of injustice and deception.

english: Inside The Car, In The Car, In A Car, Inside A Car, Within The Car, Within A Car
notes:
"The car inside is simply that, inside the car." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

"When you're doing something inside the company you're doing it within the company or in-house. For example, we do our kanji in-house. It gives it that artisan flavor." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ちょっと車内でまっていてください。
example_sentences.english: Please wait in the car for a bit.

example_sentences.japanese: シアトル市のバスの車内にスタバのコップをもったきょどうふしんな外人がいたとおもったら、ただのドバイのイケメン王子さまだった。
example_sentences.english: There was a fidgety-looking man with a Starbuck's cup on a bus in Seattle, but it was actually a handsome prince from Dubai.

example_sentences.japanese: 誰かが車内にベーコンをいくつか忘れていったようだ。
example_sentences.english: It seems like somebody left some bacon in the car.

example_sentences.japanese: つぎの日よう日に、社内のバスケットボール大会があります。
example_sentences.english: Next Sunday there will be an in house basketball tournament.

example_sentences.japanese: 花さんは、社内けっこんをしてたいしょくしました。
example_sentences.english: Hana left the company after she married a man who worked in the same company.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近、社内で変なことが流行っている。従業員が、会社の冷蔵庫の中の食べ物に名前をつけるのだ。今日は、俺は、「鈴木」と名付けられたオニギリを食べた。
example_sentences.english: "Recently, there is a strange new trend in our company. Workers put names on food in the company fridge. Today, I had a rice ball named ""Suzuki."""

notes: "A treasure stone is a very valuable stone. What kind of stones are considered treasures? How about a jewel?" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: あの赤い宝石のゆびわは、だれかのわすれものです。
example_sentences.english: That ring with the red jewel is somebody's lost property.

example_sentences.japanese: あの大ふごうは、メイドに宝石があしらわれたそうじどうぐをつかわせている。
example_sentences.english: That billionaire has his maids use cleaning tools decorated with jewels.

example_sentences.japanese: お姫様は美しい宝石のついた腕輪を時計回りに回しました。
example_sentences.english: The princess turned the beautiful jeweled bracelet clockwise.

notes: "You have only one book energy. No other books cross your mind. Only this one book. Why? Because you have such a one track mind." "The reading is based off the on'yomi readings for everything, though every reading is slightly altered. いち getting shortened to いっ, ほん changing to ぽん, and き gets changed to ぎ. They're based off the readings you know already, though, so making this shift shouldn't be too hard... that is, unless you have an 一本気, ammiright?"

example_sentences.japanese: かれは、とても一本気なせいかくです。
example_sentences.english: He has a really single-minded personality.

example_sentences.japanese: モテないだん子には、じゅんじょうで一本気なおとこがおおい気がする。
example_sentences.english: I feel that many men who are not popular among girls are naive and single-minded.

example_sentences.japanese: 俺の親友は、とても一本気な男で、90歳になった今でも初恋の女を思い続けている。
example_sentences.english: My best friend has a one-track mind; he’s 90 years old and still has feelings for his first love.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it should use the kun'yomi reading. When learning the kanji, you didn't learn that reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you with this word: You need to go for a drive to the public gardens, but you aren't going to get your normal car, you're going to get your other car. Your hoe car (ほか)! It's a car made entirely out of garden hoes. You can drive it and hoe with it at the same time! Your other car can't do that!"

example_sentences.japanese: 他にしつもんはありませんか。
example_sentences.english: Any other questions?

example_sentences.japanese: クラスの他のがく生はぜんぜん大したことのないように見えた。
example_sentences.english: It looked like the other students in the class weren't great.

example_sentences.japanese: この卵をあいつの家に投げるのは、他の日にしようぜ。
example_sentences.english: Let’s throw these eggs at his house some other day.

notes: "If a person has a lot of energy then they're very charismatic and fun! What's another feature of charismatic / fun people? They are most likely popular as well." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: このビールはとても人気があります。
example_sentences.english: This beer is very popular.

example_sentences.japanese: あのどう人しの人気のひみつをさぐっている。
example_sentences.english: I am probing into why that doujinshi is so popular.

example_sentences.japanese: 私がこの辺りで一番人気の高いベリー採集者であります。」と熊が言った。
example_sentences.english: """I am the most popular berry collector around here,"" said the bear."

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it should use the kun'yomi reading. When learning the kanji, you didn't learn that reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you with this word: When I think about the word ""previous"" I think of the beginning of a TV show where they say ""previously on..."" Let's go with that.Previously on Lost (or some other show), everyone gets stuck inside of a sack (さき). Imagine all the characters in the TV show writhing around inside of a sack, trying to get out.You can differentiate this from 先ず (まず) because it doesn't have a hiragana add on. It's plain. It's boring. It's just a sack (and also means the same thing as the kanji it comes from because it's a single kanji with nothing attached, which gets you to previous, which gets you to さき)."

example_sentences.japanese: 分かるもんだいから先にときましょう。
example_sentences.english: You should start with the problems you can solve.

example_sentences.japanese: この先のみちをまっすぐいって川をこえると、北アメリカに入ります。
example_sentences.english: If you go straight up this street and over the river, you will enter North America.

example_sentences.japanese: 申し訳ないけど、今日は先に元彼とした約束があるので、あなたとは会えません。
example_sentences.english: I’m sorry, but I have a prior engagement with my ex-boyfriend today, so I can’t meet up with you.

notes: "What is book energy? It is energy you put into reading - it is your studies! In order to have book energy, though, you have to be very serious." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: いつになったら、本気を出すんですか。
example_sentences.english: How soon before you make a serious effort?

example_sentences.japanese: ついにコウイチが本気を出してきた。
example_sentences.english: Koichi is finally getting serious.

example_sentences.japanese: 私があの男の頭の毛をむしったなんて、本気で思ってないよね？少しは私を信用してよ。
example_sentences.english: You didn’t seriously think I pulled that guy’s hair out, did you? Give me some credit.

notes:
"A name written in letters is the surname. Back in the day your surname was the important name (it's your family name after all, and family was king back in the day). This is the name you'd write out in kanji... aka in letters. So, that's why this combination of kanji means ""surname.""" "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Note that the 名 portion is the alternate reading, so adjust your thinking accordingly so you can get to みょう. Just imagine someone saying ""more"" with a funny accent. They say ""myou"" instead of ""more"". Imagine them saying they have myou people in their family than yours. Their surname is spread amongst myou people than yours."

"A seedling letter is the very first letter you learn when you're little. What's the first thing you learn to spell when you're little? Your surname! You need to know who your family is, otherwise if you get lost or something happens, you won't know how to get home! Or even who you are!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: さくらさんの名字は何といいますか。
example_sentences.english: What is Sakura’s last name?

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチの名字をおしえてくれたら、お礼にてつ人二十八号のフィギュアをあげるよ。
example_sentences.english: If you tell me Koichi's surname, I will give you a figure of Tetsujin 28 in return.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の名字はあなたには絶対教えません。
example_sentences.english: I will never tell you my family name.

example_sentences.japanese: その苗字、初めて聞きました。
example_sentences.english: That was the first time I’d heard that surname.

notes: "If you often think about studying old things, it's called archeology. All archeology involves thinking about old things, at least a little bit." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: わたしは、日本の考古学にきょうみがあります。
example_sentences.english: I’m interested in Japanese archeology.

example_sentences.japanese: 今月末でこの考古学のしごとをやめるんです。
example_sentences.english: I'm going to quit this archeology job at the end of the month.

example_sentences.japanese: この大学では、考古学を学べます。
example_sentences.english: You can study archeology at this university.

notes: "What do you call cow meat? You call it beef (what's for dinner?)." Both readings for both kanji are the readings you learned with the kanji so you should be able to read this.

example_sentences.japanese: いえのちかくのえきででんしゃをおりて、スーパーに牛肉をかいに行きました。
example_sentences.english: I got off the train at a station near my home and went to the grocery store to buy beef.

example_sentences.japanese: 去年、えいこくさん牛肉のゆ入がさいかいされました。
example_sentences.english: Last year, the import of UK beef was resumed.

example_sentences.japanese: 牛肉はありえないくらい生焼けだ。この牛肉のせいで今夜はキッチンの悪夢を見ることになりそうだ。
example_sentences.english: The beef is so undercooked. I may have a kitchen nightmare tonight because of this.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it should use the kun'yomi reading. When learning the kanji, you didn't learn that reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you with this word: You have your body. It's nice - looking good! What would really mess up your body? It would be a car raider (からだ). I'm talking about a dude who is a raider of some kind driving a car. If he runs into your body, you're done for, so watch out for the car raider. Of course, this mnemonic is only meant to get you close to the reading. Hopefully it is close enough to get you to the actual reading, からだ."

example_sentences.japanese: おふろに入ると、はじめに体をあらいます。
example_sentences.english: When I take a bath, I wash my body first.

example_sentences.japanese: ジャマルって何でそんなに体がやわらかいの？
example_sentences.english: Jamal, why is your body so flexible?

example_sentences.japanese: なぜだか、体中がかゆいんだ。
example_sentences.english: My entire body is so itchy for some reason.

notes: "From foreign lands it has come. How would you describe that item? Simply by calling it imported or foreign. This word is also used in hospitals for outpatient clinic. That's pretty good to know if you plan on going to the hospital to get checkups in Japan." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 外来の言ばは、カタカナでかきます。
example_sentences.english: Imported words are written with katakana.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日外来に来ていたかんじゃさんが、来なくなったので心ぱいしています。
example_sentences.english: I'm worried because the patient who would come to the outpatient clinic every day stopped coming.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本のものと全然違うので、私はとても外来品に興味がある。
example_sentences.english: I’m really interested in foreign things because they’re so different from what’s in Japan.

english: Internal, Within The Body, Inside The Body
notes: "Something that's inside your body... hmm, could be a lot of things, but we can generalize and just say it's internal." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ちが、体内でどんなはたらきをしているのかしっていますか。
example_sentences.english: Do you know what function blood has within the body?

example_sentences.japanese: カボチャに多くふくまれるβカロテンは体内でビタミンAにかわります。
example_sentences.english: The kabocha squash is high in beta-carotene and it's converted into vitamin A in the body.

example_sentences.japanese: 人間の体か吸血鬼の体かにかかわらず、血液は体内を循環する。
example_sentences.english: Blood circulates through the body regardless of whether it’s the body of a human or the body of a vampire.

notes: "The skin on the meat is kind of like the outer shell. It's not very nice, and people who eat only meat skin tend to use sarcasm and irony. That being said, Japanese people don't really understand sarcasm. So, maybe that's why ""meat skin"" means ""sarcasm."" Is this ironic? Now I'm not even sure." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: まったく皮肉なものですね。
example_sentences.english: That’s really ironic, isn’t it?

example_sentences.japanese: あの肉やさんは、大した皮肉やだよ。
example_sentences.english: That butcher is a such a sarcastic person.

example_sentences.japanese: 「Ironic」という曲の中に、うまい皮肉はひとつも見当たらなかった。
example_sentences.english: "Not one thing in the song ""Ironic"" is a proper example of irony."

english: Large Voice, Loud Voice, Big Voice
notes: "A large voice is probably pretty large. Maybe even annoying, too. That's why this is a large voice or a loud voice." "The reading for 声 is ごえ (rendaku'd version of the reading you know: こえ). The reading for 大 is the kun'yomi reading, like with the word 大きい (おおきい). Just imagine a loud voice saying ""おお！."""

example_sentences.japanese: そんな大声を出さないでください。
example_sentences.english: Please don’t use such a loud voice.

example_sentences.japanese: おもわず大声を出してわらってしまった。
example_sentences.english: I couldn't help laughing out loud.

example_sentences.japanese: クリスティーナは大声の持ち主で、残念なことにそれを使うのを全くはばからない。
example_sentences.english: Christina has a loud voice, and unfortunately, she’s not afraid to use it.

notes: "This word is so simple. North + West = Northwest." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ひこうきは、北西にむかっています。
example_sentences.english: The airplane is heading northwest.

example_sentences.japanese: ポートランドから車で一じかん半ほど北西の方にいくと、シーサイドというまちにつきます。
example_sentences.english: If you drive about an hour and a half northwest from Portland, you will arrive at a city called Seaside.

example_sentences.japanese: ここから北西の方角のどこかに、パンストを落とした。
example_sentences.english: I lost my pantyhose somewhere northwest of here.

notes: "You have your self part. Part of your self is you. This is oneself. This is myself. Wait, who is this part of me? You're not sure... wait, no, it's myself. Is it? Be a little psychotic for a moment as you try to remember this vocab word." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ちゃんと自分でしゅくだいをしました。
example_sentences.english: I finished the homework perfectly all by myself.

example_sentences.japanese: 自分に自しんがないとえらべない色だよね。
example_sentences.english: That's the color you can only choose if you are confident with yourself, isn't it?

example_sentences.japanese: もちろん私は自分と話しますよ。だって、時には専門家の意見が必要ですもの。
example_sentences.english: Of course I talk to myself. Sometimes I need expert advice.

english: Sky Blue, Light Blue, Light Blue Color, Sky Blue Color
notes: "You'd think that water color would have something to do with watercolors, but it doesn't. No, it has to do with the color of water, which, ironically, is sky blue in English. Light blue works as well." "The reading for this word consists of the kun'yomi reading of 水 and the kun'yomi reading of 色. For 水 you'll know this reading via your vocab studies. For 色 it just so happens to be the reading you learned with the kanji."

example_sentences.japanese: あの水色のバッグがほしいんですが。
example_sentences.english: I want that light blue bag.

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグのTシャツは、さわやかな水色です。
example_sentences.english: Tofugu T-shirt is breezy sky blue.

example_sentences.japanese: どうして今日の空は水色なんだろう？
example_sentences.english: Why is the sky light blue today?

notes:
"What shape has four angles? The most common one is a square." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings for the kanji. You've learned them both already, so you should be able to read this word!

"You look at things and memorize them via your sight, using your sense of sight." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: じゃがいもを、四角に切ってください。
example_sentences.english: Cut the potatoes into squares, please.

example_sentences.japanese: ツイッターのアイコンの形を今の丸から四角にもどしてほしい。
example_sentences.english: I want the twitter icon to go back from the current round shape to the square one.

example_sentences.japanese: どうしてほとんどの窓は真四角か長四角なんだろう。イタリア型の窓とかも作ったらいいのに。
example_sentences.english: Why are most windows either squares or rectangles? They should start making windows shaped like Italy.

example_sentences.japanese: 視覚障害のある社員を差別したとの理由から、上司が解雇された。
example_sentences.english: My superior was fired for discrimination against a visually disabled worker.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. The reading for this word is the same as the reading you learned with the kanji. What? Yeah, that's what.

example_sentences.japanese: 何と言いますか。
example_sentences.english: What would you say?

example_sentences.japanese: あなた、何さまのつもりですか。
example_sentences.english: Who do you think you are?

example_sentences.japanese: 僕達がタイのホテルで飲んだ飲み物の名前は何？
example_sentences.english: What was the name of that drink we had at the hotel in Thailand?

english: Whole Life, Entire Life, A Lifetime, All Through Life, One Existence, A Generation, An Age
notes: "One life is all you get. It's your whole life." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You didn't learn this reading for 生 though, so here's a mnemonic to help you:Who has been in charge of you your whole life? The shogun (しょう). He owns everyone and that's how it will stay for your entire life."

example_sentences.japanese: このゆびわは、一生、大切にします。
example_sentences.english: I’ve taken care of this ring my whole life.

example_sentences.japanese: わたしの父は、しぬまで一生どくしんでした。
example_sentences.english: My father remained single all his life.

example_sentences.japanese: 一生かけて償います。
example_sentences.english: I’ll make up for it with my life.

notes: This has a little hiragana attached to it but nothing that suggests it's a verb or an adjective. That means you can assume this word has the same meaning as its parent kanji. "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: You have to remember the すべ part, which is an admittedly difficult sound to remember. You have to think of the concept of all or entire. When you think of that concept, think of someone's entire fortune. All their money. You want to get all of Beth's money, so you sue beth (すべ) for all she has."

example_sentences.japanese: 全て上手く行きました。
example_sentences.english: It all went smoothly.

example_sentences.japanese: 申しわけございませんが、げんざい全てのおせきがうまっているじょうきょうでして...。
example_sentences.english: I am sorry, but all the seats are fully occupied at the moment, so...

example_sentences.japanese: 僕が先だよ。ウィキペディアが僕の宿題を全て真似したんだ。
example_sentences.english: I was the first to do it. Wikipedia copied my entire homework assignment afterwards.

english: America, United States, United States Of America, Usa
notes: "America is the country of rice. I guess this is from all those rolling plains and such we have. Another way to say America in Japanese is アメリカ, but this is another more formal (and older) way. ""Rice Country"" aka America." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 米国の大とうりょうの名まえを知っていますか。
example_sentences.english: Do you know the name of the president of the United States?

example_sentences.japanese: 米国には元々何もきたいなんてしてなかったよ。
example_sentences.english: I never expected anything from America anyways.

example_sentences.japanese: 多くの人は、単にマクドナルドのスーパーサイズコンボのために米国に移住する。
example_sentences.english: Many people immigrate to America solely for the super-size combos at McDonald’s.

notes: "Here you have both directions / ways. Every time you have to choose between something it's like having to choose between two ways. That's why this word is simply both. Close to the kanji is the meaning both sides, as well. Learn either for 両方, they're pretty similar." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 姉も妹も、両方とも大さかにすんでいます。
example_sentences.english: My older and younger sisters both live in Osaka.

example_sentences.japanese: じかんはあるんだから、両方やってみたら？
example_sentences.english: You've got time, so why don't you try it both ways?

example_sentences.japanese: ダメだよ！両方とも僕のだよ。
example_sentences.english: Nope. They’re both mine.

notes: "Don't use one hand when you can use both hands. This is simply both plus hand put together." This word uses the readings you learned with both kanji. No problemo for a kanji master such as yourself.

example_sentences.japanese: 両手を上げて、バンザイをしました。
example_sentences.english: They raised both hands and shouted banzai.

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトは両手に花ですね。
example_sentences.english: Viet is between two beautiful women.

example_sentences.japanese: バランスの良い食事とは、両手にチョコレートクッキーを持つことです。
example_sentences.english: A balanced diet is a chocolate cookie in both hands.

notes: "What is the color of tea? You'd think it would be green, assuming it's Japanese... but this word came from China. What color is Chinese tea? It tends to be more brown. Think Oolong tea, for example." The readings for both kanji are the readings you learned with the kanji, meaning you should be able to read this already.

example_sentences.japanese: ★に入るばんごうを、茶色にぬります。
example_sentences.english: Please color the number that best matches the ★ with brown.

example_sentences.japanese: 明るい茶色にカラーリングしてください。
example_sentences.english: I'd like to dye my hair light brown, please.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の白いTシャツ全ての脇のところに、茶色のシミがある。
example_sentences.english: All of my white t-shirts have brown armpit stains on them.

notes: "The way you say things could be translated as your accent... but this is much bigger. This is an entire ""way"" of speaking. This is a dialect. You can even think of the 方 as being ""direction"" where you go in different directions in a country and discover different dialects, if that way of thinking helps." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 方言のじしょを作っています。
example_sentences.english: I’m making a dialect dictionary.

example_sentences.japanese: ああっもうっ！かれしの方言がうつっちゃってるずら。
example_sentences.english: Damn! My boyfriend's dialect has rubbed off on me.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の国の東側出身の人達は変わった方言で喋るので、彼らが何を言っているのか全く分かりません。
example_sentences.english: People from the eastern part of my country use such an odd dialect that they are impossible to understand.

hiragana: はやくち, はやぐち
english: Fast Talker, Fast Talking, Fast Speaker, Fast Speaking, Quick Talker
notes: "When you have a fast mouth, you're probably a fast talker, right motormouth?" "Remember how body parts often change even jukugo words to kun'yomi readings? That's what happened here too. Both readings are kun'yomi, making this one はやくち. Alternatively, you can read this as はやぐち as well."

example_sentences.japanese: わたしの兄は、とても早口です。
example_sentences.english: My older brother is a really fast talker.

example_sentences.japanese: お前のことが一ばん大すきだよって、何でそんなに早口で言ったの？
example_sentences.english: Why did you say that you love me the most so quickly?

example_sentences.japanese: こんなに早口の赤ん坊なんて見たことないよ。
example_sentences.english: I’ve never seen such a fast talking baby before.

notes: "An outside country is one outside of your own country. That is a foreign country." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: わたしたちはまだ外国に行ったことがありません。
example_sentences.english: We haven’t gone to other countries yet.

example_sentences.japanese: 外国へでんわをするのはこれがはじめてです。
example_sentences.english: This is my first time making an overseas call.

example_sentences.japanese: もし外国にいるなら、有名人になっても構わない。
example_sentences.english: I wouldn’t mind being a celebrity if I was in a foreign country.

english: Full Effort, Every Effort, Best Effort, Full Power
notes: "When you put all your power into something, you're putting your full effort into it. Hopefully that's what you put into your kanji learning as well!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: えきまで、全力で走りました。
example_sentences.english: I ran with all my might to the station.

example_sentences.japanese: その中国人の女は、王子が自分とけっこんしてくれるよう全力でせっとくしたが、しっぱいにおわった。
example_sentences.english: That Chinese woman tried her best to persuade the prince to marry her, but she failed.

example_sentences.japanese: そのゾンビは、死から蘇ろうと全力を尽くしていた。
example_sentences.english: That zombie is using up all its strength trying to come back from the dead.

notes: "You have correct and fix. When you're always fixing things to make them correct (for example, someone's lies!) you are a very honest person." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 川田さんは、とても正直な人です。
example_sentences.english: Kawata is a very honest person.

example_sentences.japanese: かれの正直なところがすきなんです。
example_sentences.english: I like his honesty.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕は水中で息をしている火星からきた王子だし、他の人の模範となる必要があるので、いつも正直でいようと心がけています。
example_sentences.english: I try to be honest all the time because I’m an underwater-breathing Martian prince and I need to set an example for people.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "If you're lucky, you already know this (very) common word's reading. It's the word for ""I,"" probably one of the first things you'd learn in Japanese. The reading for this is わたし. If you don't know that already, just think: ""What, a し?"" referring to the reading of the kanji, which is し."

example_sentences.japanese: メーリングリストから私を外してください。
example_sentences.english: Please remove me from your email list.

example_sentences.japanese: 私がえいぎょう部のせきにん者です。
example_sentences.english: I'm the director of the sales division.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日の夜、バーデビューしちゃった。私もちょっとずつ大人の階段登ってるって感じ？
example_sentences.english: I went to a bar for the first time last night. I feel like I’m slowly becoming an adult.

notes: "A country king is still a king, just of a bigger area." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: あの国王は、とてもよくばりです。
example_sentences.english: That king is very greedy.

example_sentences.japanese: わたしは、国王のことをじょじょにりかいしてきました。
example_sentences.english: I'm starting to understand the king.

example_sentences.japanese: 18歳という若さで国王になった。
example_sentences.english: I became the king as a youth of 18.

notes: "This is heaven country. Where is that? Probably just in heaven (or if you want to be fancy, the kingdom of heaven)." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. The 国 is changed to the reading ごく, though because of rendaku. Even heaven changes a little bit."

example_sentences.japanese: ポチはきっと天国にいるんだよ。
example_sentences.english: Poochie is definitely in heaven.

example_sentences.japanese: 天国がこんなとこだったなんて、本当にがっかりです。
example_sentences.english: I am so disappointed to learn the Kingdom of Heaven is that kind of place.

example_sentences.japanese: タバコを天国で吸いましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let’s smoke cigarettes in Heaven.

notes: "The water star is the planet Mercury. That's where we hid all of our secret moon water. Mercury looks enough like our moon, so we put it there so no one could find it." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 水星には大気がありません。
example_sentences.english: Mercury does not have an atmosphere.

example_sentences.japanese: こんなはずじゃなかったんですが、もう十年も水星でホームレスをしています。
example_sentences.english: This isn't what I asked for, but I've been homeless for 10 years on Mercury.

example_sentences.japanese: 水星は、日の出直前、または日没直後しか見ることができない。
example_sentences.english: I can only see Mercury just before sunrise and right after sunset.

notes: "The middle of the east is more simply known as the middle east." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: けさ、テレビで中東のニュースを見ました。
example_sentences.english: I watched the news on the Middle East on TV this morning.

example_sentences.japanese: きんきゅうじたいで中東に行かなくてはいけなかったんだから、けっこんしきに来れなかったのは仕方がないよ。
example_sentences.english: You can't help it that you couldn't make it to the wedding because you had to go to the Middle East for an emergency.

example_sentences.japanese: 中東で一番楽しまれているゲームは何ですか？
example_sentences.english: What is the most played game in the Middle East?

notes: "Death and deceased. That's a lot of death. This is mortality." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: やさいをたくさん食べると、死亡リスクがへるそうです。
example_sentences.english: I heard that when you eat a lot of vegetables you can lower your risk of mortality.

example_sentences.japanese: 山田さんの弟さんの死亡のげんいんはなんですか？
example_sentences.english: What is the cause of Mr. Yamada's younger brother's death?

example_sentences.japanese: チーズバーガーの発明により、全先進国の死亡率が三倍に跳ね上がった。
example_sentences.english: Since the invention of the cheeseburger, mortality rates in all first-world nations have tripled.

notes: "When something involves all the country you know it's nationwide or national." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 全国でインフルエンザがはやっています。
example_sentences.english: The flu is spreading nationwide.

example_sentences.japanese: リンゴのしゅうかくりょうが全国で一ばん多いけんはどこですか？
example_sentences.english: Which prefecture is the largest producer of apples nationwide?

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は全国規模のサイバーいじめのスキャンダルに関与していた。
example_sentences.english: He was involved in a nationwide cyber bullying scandal.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it should use the kun'yomi reading. When learning the kanji, you didn't learn that reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you with this word: Someone yells out ""NEXT!"" because the first thing didn't work on you. That was a single guillotine. Now they are going to try two guillotines (つぎ) and see how that works on your thick neck. NEXXXXT!"

example_sentences.japanese: 次のでん車にのりましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let’s catch the next train.

example_sentences.japanese: 次のよていは、決まり次だいお知らせします。
example_sentences.english: I'll let you know once we decide on the next plan.

example_sentences.japanese: このバスツアーの次の目的地は、マイケル・ジャクソンの家です。
example_sentences.english: The next destination on this bus tour is Michael Jackson’s house.

notes: "When you're years above someone else, you are older than that person." The reading for this one is an exception, because it uses kun'yomi readings even though it is a jukugo kanji. You already know the separate kun'yomi readings from the vocabulary of the last level, but you will have to remember to actually use this knowledge when this word comes up.

example_sentences.japanese: 年上の人と、デートするのははじめてです。
example_sentences.english: This is my first date with an older person.

example_sentences.japanese: 人生はよそく不かのうだ。お前が年上のび人とけっこんするかのうせいだってゼロパーセントではない。
example_sentences.english: Life is unpredictable. It's not a zero percent chance that you will get married with a beautiful older woman.

example_sentences.japanese: お父さんが、お母さんのお母さんはピラミッドよりも年上だと言うんだよ。
example_sentences.english: My dad says that my mom’s mom is older than the pyramids.

notes: "The outside of the sea is someplace overseas. It can also be foreign or abroad if those words are easier to remember for you." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: しょう来は、海外ではたらきたいです。
example_sentences.english: I want to work overseas in the future.

example_sentences.japanese: ほけんぎょうかいに八年つとめた後、アメリカへ海外りゅう学しました。
example_sentences.english: After having worked in the insurance industry for eight years, I went to America to study abroad.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はどこか海外で住みたいと思っているが、旅行は嫌いだ。
example_sentences.english: I want to live somewhere overseas, but I hate traveling.

notes: "Something is flat and relaxed. That is you. What words does that describe? To me, that would be peace and tranquility. Just imagine something that is flat and relaxed, like a field of grass with happy people in it. It's so peaceful! It's so tranquil!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 平安じだいはいつですか。
example_sentences.english: When was the Heian period?

example_sentences.japanese: 平安をみだす人がいないワニカニフォーラムは、わたしの心に平安をあたえてくれる。
example_sentences.english: The WaniKani forums don't have any trolls, so it gives me peace of mind.

example_sentences.japanese: ブリティッシュコロンビアの古の森を歩く時、心に平安を感じる。
example_sentences.english: Walking through the old growth forests in British Columbia was so peaceful.

notes: "When you are all relaxed you are finally in safety." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ここまで来れば、安全です。
example_sentences.english: If I come here, I’m safe.

example_sentences.japanese: ゆっくりでかまいませんので、安全うんてんでおねがいします。
example_sentences.english: I don't mind if we're a little slow, so just please drive safely.

example_sentences.japanese: 安全第一が私のモットーです。
example_sentences.english: My motto is safety first.

notes: "The South East is the Southeast." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 車は、南東に向かってすすみました。
example_sentences.english: The car continued heading southeast.

example_sentences.japanese: てっきり今日は日が南東にしずむもんだとおもっていたよ。
example_sentences.english: I totally thought the sun would set in the southeast today.

example_sentences.japanese: 南東の方角に、流れ星を見た。
example_sentences.english: I saw a shooting star in the southeast.

notes: "You've seen that 代わる means ""to substitute for"" or ""to replace."" This is the noun version of that (no う sound on the end). So, what is the noun version of those verb words? It would be substitute or replacement." "You should be able to figure out the reading from learning 代わる in the previous level."

example_sentences.japanese: 代わりの先生をさがしています。
example_sentences.english: We’re looking for a substitute teacher.

example_sentences.japanese: この世のどこにも、かれの代わりはいないんです。
example_sentences.english: There is no replacement for him anywhere in the world.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語を教わる代わりに、英語を教えることができますよ。
example_sentences.english: I can teach you English and in exchange you can teach me Japanese.

notes: "If you're in the middle of the ground, then you're most likely underground. Are you a moleperson? That's pretty cool." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 地中は、冬にはあたたかく、なつはつめたいです。
example_sentences.english: Underground it’s warm in the winter and cold in the summer.

example_sentences.japanese: 多くのみずうみは、地中の水ろでつながっています。
example_sentences.english: Many of the lakes are connected by subterranean channels.

example_sentences.japanese: 地中の温度を測るにはどうすればいいですか。
example_sentences.english: What do I need to do to gauge the temperature underground?

notes: "Below the ground is underground." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: このたてものの地下に、トイレがあります。
example_sentences.english: There is a restroom in the basement of this building.

example_sentences.japanese: デパ地下でたくさんし食をしました。
example_sentences.english: I ate a lot of food samples at the food section of the department store basement.

example_sentences.japanese: ヨハネの黙示録がもうすぐ実現されるから、私は地下室を建設しているのだよ。
example_sentences.english: The Apocalypse is coming soon so I’m building an underground cellar.

notes: "When you're not relaxed how do you feel? Uneasiness is what you'd feel." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ごうかくしているか不安です。
example_sentences.english: I’m anxious about passing.

example_sentences.japanese: 出さんを目前に不安な気もちでいっぱいです。
example_sentences.english: I'm so nervous about the impending childbirth.

example_sentences.japanese: あの殺人事件を目撃してからというもの、不安を取り除くことができない。
example_sentences.english: Since I witnessed the murder, I haven't been able to rid myself of these feelings of anxiety.

notes: "A sheep's fur is wool." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: クリスマスプレゼントに、羊毛のブランケットをもらいました。
example_sentences.english: I got a wool blanket as a Christmas present.

example_sentences.japanese: この羊毛フェルトの人形に出会えて本当によかった。
example_sentences.english: I'm so happy to have come across this wool felt doll.

example_sentences.japanese: 羊毛の手袋は、枕の詰め物に適している。
example_sentences.english: Woolen mittens are great for stuffing pillows.

notes: "When you have someone who has years below your own, this person is younger than you." "The reading for this one is kind of strange. It is the kun'yomi reading for both of the kanji. You know the kun'yomi readings from earlier, back when you learned the vocab 年 and 下."

example_sentences.japanese: もり田さんには、年下のかの女がいます。
example_sentences.english: Morita has a younger girlfriend.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチはアーノルドシュワルツネッガーより三十八才年下だ。
example_sentences.english: Koichi is 38 years younger than Arnold Schwarzenegger.

example_sentences.japanese: あの子は年下なのにとても大人びている。
example_sentences.english: Even though that kid is younger, he’s really mature.

notes: "この means ""this"" so この辺 just means this area." "The reading for the kanji portion is just what you've already learned with the kanji 辺 so this shouldn't be a difficult one to read for you."

example_sentences.japanese: この辺は、人が少ないのでしずかです。
example_sentences.english: There aren’t many people around here, so it’s quiet.

example_sentences.japanese: この辺に、スタバはありますか？
example_sentences.english: Is there Starbucks around here?

example_sentences.japanese: この辺では、言葉に気をつけた方がいいぜ。町のこちら側に住んでいるやつらは、口笛を吹いただけでも顔に唾をぶっかけてきやがるからな。
example_sentences.english: You have to be careful about what you say around here. People on this side of town will spit in your face just for whistling.

notes: "A black person is simply a black person, kind of like how a 白人 is a ""white person,"" but a different  color." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: なぜ未だに黒人をさべつする人がいるのか、りかいできません。
example_sentences.english: I can’t understand how there are still people who discriminate against black people.

example_sentences.japanese: おれは黒人であいつは白人だけど、それがどうしたの？
example_sentences.english: I'm black, he's white. What's wrong with that?

example_sentences.japanese: ピーナッツバターは、ジョージ・ワシントン・カーヴァーという名の黒人によって発明された。
example_sentences.english: Peanut butter was invented by a black person named George Washington Carver.

english: Frantic, Desperate, Certain Death, Sure Death
notes:
"Your future consists of certain death. How would you feel in this situation? Probably very frantic and desperate. Another translation for this word is simply certain death, though I'd rather you learn one of the first two before this one if you can." "The readings are the on'yomi readings, though 必 (ひつ) gets shortened to ひっ. In your desperate situation just imagine that you're trying to get out of it, and to do so you move the つ only to find a smaller っ blocking your way. It is certain death."

"If it's certain that you will attain it, then it is inevitable. It is a foregone conclusion." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 必死にがんばっても、どうにもならないこともある。
example_sentences.english: Even if I try desperately, it might still be futile.

example_sentences.japanese: わたしのそ父は、必死のかくごでせんじょうに向かったそうです。
example_sentences.english: I heard that my grandfather went to the war front prepared to die.

example_sentences.japanese: 「隊長、私はどうしても火星に戻る必要があるんです。アイフォンを忘れてしまったのです。」彼は必死に頼んだ。
example_sentences.english: """Captain, I really need to return to Mars. I left my iPhone there,"" he said desperately."

example_sentences.japanese: 子どもへの性教育はある時期では必至になると思うんですが、日本はそうした教育については通常どのように行われるんですか。
example_sentences.english: I think it’s necessary to teach kids sex education at some point, but how do people usually teach those things in Japan?

notes: "When you have self reason, you are able to think for yourself. When you can think for yourself, you have freedom. Very philosophical this vocab is." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 一人ぐらしをはじめて、自由なじかんができました。
example_sentences.english: I started living by myself and I have some free time to spare.

example_sentences.japanese: 自由になるための道のりはまだまだとおいですが、ぜったいにあきらめません。
example_sentences.english: To obtain freedom, we still have a long way to go, but we will never give up.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本のサラリーマンが自由に使えるお金は、毎月平均たった三万五千円だ。
example_sentences.english: The money Japanese salarymen can use freely every month is, on average, usually only 35,000 yen.

notes: "When something is made with hand, it is handmade." "The readings for these kanji are the kun'yomi readings. Just think of this word as two separate words put together (手 and 作る). The る in 作る gets changed to り because it's an adjective, and the つ in つくり gets changed to づ because of the way the words are combined with each other. You should know most of the reading that is in this word, though it will probably take a little bit of thinking to sort out the little changes in those readings."

example_sentences.japanese: このテーブルは、林さんの手作りです。
example_sentences.english: This table was handmade by Hayashi.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日手作りのバランスのいい食じをとるようにしています。
example_sentences.english: I try to have a homemade, well-balanced diet every day.

example_sentences.japanese: 手作りのプレゼントは、どれだけ暇な時間があるかってことがバレてしまうので、結構怖い。
example_sentences.english: Handmade presents are pretty scary because they reveal that you have too much free time.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it should use the kun'yomi reading. When learning the kanji, you didn't learn that reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you with this word: You visit your friend's home. However, this home isn't any normal home. They live at the video game company EA (いえ). Imagine yourself going to your friend's home from school every day. You go to EA, settle in, and play some video games. What a great home that would be to visit.There's another reading as well, though, and it's うち. This reading is used for your own home. For someone else's home you'd use いえ, though."

example_sentences.japanese: みなさん、家にあそびに来てください。
example_sentences.english: Everyone, please stop by my house.

example_sentences.japanese: いいかげん、家をかた付けた方がいいよ。
example_sentences.english: You really need to clean your house.

example_sentences.japanese: 家とは、みんなの心と食べ物がある場所です。
example_sentences.english: Home is where the heart is. And the food.

notes: "A hand paper being a letter seems kind of strange, but think of it this way: Paper that you can fit in your hand? That's good for a letter. Also, you could write a letter on your hand if you want, though it would hurt a lot to chop off your hand and send it (imagine doing this)." "The reading is double kun'yomi (body parts tend to make kanji in words change to a kun'yomi reading). Both kanji in this word had you learn that reading right from the start, though, so you should be able to read this word. Just watch out for the rendaku making it がみ, not かみ."

example_sentences.japanese: 外国に手紙を出しました。
example_sentences.english: I sent a letter to a foreign country.

example_sentences.japanese: その金正日からの手紙、ネットオークションに出しちゃえば？きっとだれかしらかうと思うよ。
example_sentences.english: Why don't you put up the letter from Kim Jong Il for online auction? I think somebody would buy it.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はコカコーラ宛に、心のこもった手紙を書いて、どうして彼らの製品にたくさん砂糖が入っているのかについて尋ねたいと思います。
example_sentences.english: I’m going to write a very heated letter to Coca-Cola and ask why there is so much sugar in their products.

notes: "A small voice is so small that you can hardly hear it. It's a low voice or a whisper." "The readings for this word are both kun'yomi readings. You've learned both of these readings by now so you should be able to read this on your own. Just watch out because, like in 大声, the こえ becomes ごえ thanks to our old friend rendaku."

example_sentences.japanese: 二人とも、どうして小声ではなしているの？
example_sentences.english: Why are they both whispering?

example_sentences.japanese: 「ビエトに学ランをきてもらいたいんだ。に合うと思うんだよね。」と、わたしのもうそうの中でコウイチがビエトに小声で言った。
example_sentences.english: """I want you to try on a school uniform. I think you'll look good in it."" Koichi whispered to Viet in my fantasy."

example_sentences.japanese: 男は、小声で話し始めた。
example_sentences.english: The man started speaking in a low voice.

notes: "The same time? Okay, let's say what we think this word means at the same time. Whoops, I just said it, sorry." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生が教室に入ってきたと同時に、しぎょうのチャイムがなりました。
example_sentences.english: At the same time teacher came in the classroom, the bell rang.

example_sentences.japanese: でん子レンジとトースターを同時につかったから、ブレーカーがおちちゃったんだ。
example_sentences.english: I was using the microwave and the toaster at the same time, and the circuit breaker tripped.

example_sentences.japanese: 「今日はよくできましたね。それではまた来週同じ時間に。」と、コスプレのプロとアニメオタクが同時に言った。
example_sentences.english: """Good lesson today. I’ll see you this time next week,"" the professional cosplayer and the anime nerd said at the same time."

notes: "You have strong power. This is your strength." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: このボンドは、かなり強力なので気をつけてください。
example_sentences.english: This glue is pretty strong, so please be careful.

example_sentences.japanese: 強力なミニウォーターポンプの作り方をおしえてもらいました。
example_sentences.english: I was taught how to make a powerful, mini water pump.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女を見つめると、まるで十人力ぐらい強力になったように感じる。
example_sentences.english: When I look at her, I feel as though I have the strength of ten men.

hiragana: さんかくけい, さんかっけい
notes: "You already learned that 三角 means ""triangle."" Well this means triangle too, but it's the mathematical term. You should use it in math class." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: どうすれば、三角形のオニギリをにぎれるんですか？
example_sentences.english: How do you make onigiri into a triangle?

example_sentences.japanese: 夏の夜空には、天の川をはさんでことざとわしざと白鳥ざの一とう星をむすんだ大三角形が広がります。
example_sentences.english: A big triangle, consisting of three magnitude stars from Lyra, Aquila, and Cygnus, stretches out in the summer night sky.

example_sentences.japanese: そこには、三角形の公園があります。
example_sentences.english: There is a triangle park there.

notes: "You already know 人気 which means ""popular."" And you also know that 不 means ""not."" So what do you get when you combine the two? Something that's not popular or unpopular." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 今年、もっとも不人気だったアニメは何だと思いますか。
example_sentences.english: What do you think is the most unpopular anime this year?

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチたいマイケルのすもうのし合は、Youtubeで見るとはく力に欠けるので不人気です。
example_sentences.english: The Koichi vs Michael sumo match is unpopular because it lacks the intensity when you watch it on YouTube.

example_sentences.japanese: 「お前の母ちゃんに言ってやる」が口癖だったため、彼はクラスメートに不人気だった。
example_sentences.english: "He was unpopular among his classmates because his favorite phrase was, ""I’m gonna tell your mom."""

notes: "The yellow color is just the color yellow." The readings are the same as the readings you learned with the kanji meaning you should be able to read this word right off the bat.

example_sentences.japanese: 黄色かみどり色のペンはありますか？
example_sentences.english: Are there yellow or green pens?

example_sentences.japanese: アメリカのカラスは、美しい黄色の羽をもっていることで有名です。
example_sentences.english: An American crow is well known for the beauty of its yellow wings.

example_sentences.japanese: もし尿のいろが透明から黄色に変わってしまったら、もっと水を飲んだ方が良いという合図です。
example_sentences.english: If your urine changes from clear to yellow, you should drink more water.

notes: "Remember 地下, which is ""below ground."" Well, this is ground and above combined together, so I bet you can guess that this means above ground. But usually things above ground don't float (unless you're in space), so it's really on the ground." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 木のはが地上におちた。
example_sentences.english: The leaves fell to the ground.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは地上1kmの所に、ひみつき地をもっている。
example_sentences.english: Koichi has a Secret Base 1km above ground.

example_sentences.japanese: 東京タワーは、地上から見上げると物凄い迫力がありますね。
example_sentences.english: When you look at Tokyo Tower from the ground it feels tremendously powerful.

english: Body And Mind, Mind And Body
notes: "Technically this kanji is heart and somebody, but think about it this way. Where does everything come from inside somebody? The heart! It keeps things going by pumping blood, providing the foundation for both a good mind and body." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: かれは、心身ともに、つかれきっていたんだと思います。
example_sentences.english: I think his body and mind were both worn out.

example_sentences.japanese: 取りえは、心身ともにけん全であることだけです。
example_sentences.english: My only strength is being of sound mind and body.

example_sentences.japanese: ヨガは、心身共にとても健康にしてくれる。
example_sentences.english: Yoga is excellent for the health of your body and mind.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "The reading is the same as the kanji you learned, too, making this one an ease to learn!"

example_sentences.japanese: あんたはそうやって楽することばっかり考えて！
example_sentences.english: You only think about taking the easy way out!

example_sentences.japanese: このいすめっちゃ楽だわー。
example_sentences.english: This chair is very comfortable!

example_sentences.japanese: 私は愛犬トトと一緒にいる時が一番楽です。
example_sentences.english: I am most at ease when I am with my dog, Toto.

english: Last Time, Recently, Lately, Previous, Previously
notes: "この means ""this."" And, you know what the word 前 means (front/before). So ""this before"" has to do with something that happened previously. That's why this word means last time, recently, and lately." "The reading for 前 is the kun'yomi, like the reading for the vocabulary word 前. So long as you know that word, you'll be able to read this one too. The reason it's not on'yomi is because it's like two words put together. The word この and the word 前."

example_sentences.japanese: そういえば、この前、しょうてんがいでさくら子ちゃんとバッタリ会ったよ。
example_sentences.english: That reminds me, last time I was at the shopping district I ran into Sakurako.

example_sentences.japanese: この前、日本ごの曲のCDを買ったんだよね。
example_sentences.english: I recently bought a Japanese music CD.

example_sentences.japanese: この前、思わずノートをとるぐらい完璧な日没を見たのはいつだったかな？
example_sentences.english: When was the last time I saw a sunset so perfect that I had to take note of it?

english: Natural, Reasonable, Obvious, Usual, Common, Ordinary
notes: "You've seen how 当たり means success. If you've experienced success before, everything after that seems to be pretty obvious." The readings for this word are both kun'yomi readings. You've learned both of these readings by now so you should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: こんな当たり前のこと、どうして分からないの？
example_sentences.english: This is normal stuff, why can’t you get that?

example_sentences.japanese: でも、これが当たり前のことだとは思わないでくださいね。
example_sentences.english: Don't take it for granted though.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日のような当たり前の日をすごせることに、かんしゃしなきゃいけませんよね。
example_sentences.english: Shouldn't we be thankful we're able to have an ordinary day like today.

english: Pending, Unsettled, Undecided, Not Yet Decided
notes: "Something that is not yet decided... it is pending... it is unsettled." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: しょうさいは未決です。
example_sentences.english: The details are undecided.

example_sentences.japanese: 未決しょるいは、コウイチのデスクの上の赤いトレイに入れてください。
example_sentences.english: Please put the pending documents in the red tray on Koichi's desk.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女の裁判はもう十三年近くも未決となっています。そんなに待たなくてはいけないなんて、とても不公平です。
example_sentences.english: Her court case has been pending for nearly 13 years. It’s so unfair to have to wait that long.

notes: "Someone who does study for a living. That is a scholar." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: かれのお父さんは、立ぱな学者です。
example_sentences.english: His father is a splendid scholar.

example_sentences.japanese: あの学者はけいれきさしょうをしています。
example_sentences.english: That scholar is a resume faker.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は世界でも有名なハロー・キティ学者です。
example_sentences.english: I am a world renowned scholar of Hello Kitty.

notes: "Somebody's body. This refers to the very general word the body. As in, ""the human body"" or something like that. This can also refer to health as well." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日は、学校で身体そくていがあります。
example_sentences.english: There will be body measurements tomorrow at school.

example_sentences.japanese: この図しょかんには、身体しょうがいしゃがつかえるトイレはありますか？
example_sentences.english: Is there a handicap accessible restroom in this library?

example_sentences.japanese: 空こうで、まやくをかくしもっていないか、身体けんさをされました。
example_sentences.english: At the airport, they searched me for hidden drugs.

notes: "The all of somebody is someone's whole body." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: わたし、全身毛むくじゃらのワイルドな男せいがすきなんです。
example_sentences.english: I love men whose entire bodies are covered in wild, thick hair.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは全身にタトゥーを入れようと思っているみたいなんだけど、どう思う？
example_sentences.english: Apparently Koichi is looking to get his whole body tattooed. What do you guys think?

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日七ヶ月ぶりにランニングしたから、今日は全身筋肉痛だよ。
example_sentences.english: I went running for the first time in seven months yesterday and now my whole body hurts.

notes: "The お is added to elevate someone in front of you. But it's done in a sarcastic way, so this word means you. That's right, plain old ""you."" This ""you"" is usually used casually, between men." "The reading for 前 is the kun'yomi, like the reading for the vocabulary word 前. So long as you know that word, you'll be able to read this one too. "

example_sentences.japanese: 一生お前といっしょに生きていきたいんだ。
example_sentences.english: I want to live my whole life with you.

example_sentences.japanese: 女のことお前ってよぶ男本当にきらいだわ。
example_sentences.english: "I really hate men who call women ""you."""

example_sentences.japanese: お前の作る餃子は本当に美味しいな。
example_sentences.english: The gyoza you make is really tasty.

notes: "The degree of the angle shows what the angle is. 90 degrees? 160 degrees? They're all still angles when you come down to it." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: べつの角度から、もう一度見てみましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let’s try looking again from a different angle.

example_sentences.japanese: ピサのしゃとうはたしかにへんな角度で立っている。
example_sentences.english: The Leaning Tower of Pisa sure stands at an odd angle.

example_sentences.japanese: もしマイリー・サイラスが一番好きな歌を歌っているのをこの角度から見ることができたら、俺の夢を叶えてくれたってことで神様の存在を信じると思う。
example_sentences.english: If I can see Miley Cyrus singing my favorite song from this angle, I will believe in God because it would mean that He made my dream come true.

english: Black And White, White And Black
notes: "Something is both white and black. It is black and white (you can also say white and black if you prefer)." "The readings are kun'yomi, but you should have seen both 白 and 黒い separately as vocabulary by now. It's the same readings here, so you can apply that knowledge and read this word!"

example_sentences.japanese: 白黒ハッキリさせようぜ。
example_sentences.english: Let’s make it clearly black and white.

example_sentences.japanese: この白黒の写しん、すてきですね。
example_sentences.english: This black and white photo is very lovely.

example_sentences.japanese: カナエちゃんがいつもオシャレな服装をしているってことは認めるけどさ、今日の白黒のドレスはちょっとなんかパンダみたいじゃない？
example_sentences.english: I agree that Kanae always wears very chic clothes, but today that black and white dress just makes her look like a panda, doesn’t it?

english: Discomfort, Inconvenience, Disability, Impairment, Poverty, Destitution
