example_sentences.japanese: 天然ボケで、一緒にいていつも楽しいなって思うんだ。俺、お前のこと大好きだよ。
example_sentences.english: You’re kind of goofy and that makes you fun to hang out with. I really like you.

notes: "An image is reflecting on the mirror. You're looking at the mirror, confused. Don't worry, it is only a reflection, an image. It's not real." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: YouTubeでマイケルの映像を四千四百四十四回見ると、のろいにかかるらしいよ。
example_sentences.english: I heard that if you watch Michael's image on YouTube 4444 times, you'll be cursed.

example_sentences.japanese: 映画リングを見てからというもの、古い戸からさだ子が出てくる映像が頭からはなれない。
example_sentences.english: Since I watched Ringu, I can't get the reflection of Sadako coming out of that old well out of my head.

example_sentences.japanese: あの新しい日本映画見た？映画自体はいまいちだったんだけど、映像が物凄く美しかったよ。
example_sentences.english: Did you see that new Japanese movie? The movie itself wasn’t very good, but the shots they captured were beautiful.

notes: "The right side of your body is the side you profit most from. So, you use it a lot more. That's because you're right handed." "Both kanji use the kun'yomi vocab readings. So, think to the words 右 and 利く to learn how to read this one. It probably reads like this because it's two separate words come together (right + handed) rather than one word."

example_sentences.japanese: わたしの息子は右利きではありません。
example_sentences.english: My son is not right-handed.

example_sentences.japanese: ぼくは左利きなのに、お母さんが間ちがえて右利きのグローブを買っちゃったんだ。
example_sentences.english: Although I am left-handed, my mom bought a right-handed baseball glove by mistake.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女のこと、すごく好きだったんだけど、右利きだって分かってから冷めちゃったんだよね。どうしてかは分からないけど。
example_sentences.english: I really liked her but I was turned off when I found out that she was right handed. I don’t know why.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. The reading is the same as the kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: けっこん指わは、銀か金、どちらにする？
example_sentences.english: For your wedding ring which would you prefer: silver or gold?

example_sentences.japanese: いくつになっても銀せいひんがすきです。
example_sentences.english: No matter how old I get, I still like silver things.

example_sentences.japanese: 赤信号で、銀の軽トラが私の横に止まった。
example_sentences.english: At the red light a silver pick-up truck pulled up alongside me.

notes: "The silver color is just silver (the color)." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 初めにお伝えしていたように、これを銀色にぬり直してください。
example_sentences.english: Please repaint this silver like I told you the first time.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチの銀色のヒゲをわたしに売ってくれませんか？
example_sentences.english: Could you sell Koichi's silver mustache to me, please?

example_sentences.japanese: 私のダンスの相手は、あの銀色のコスチュームを着たフグって男よ。
example_sentences.english: My dance partner is that guy in the silver costume. His name is Fugu.

notes: "This is a weird word, sorry ahead of time. You have the formal name title plus another formal name title (thanks to the 々). When you have several different kinds of formal name titles you have all kinds of fancy people that you're talking to. Each one of them is different. There are many various people!" "The reading is just the reading you learned with the kanji. The second one is ざま however, which plays right into the ""various"" meaning of the word. There's even various ways to read さま in this word!"

example_sentences.japanese: わたしの大学は大きくて有名なので、様々な国からりゅう学生が集まっています。
example_sentences.english: My university is big and famous, so foreign exchange students come here from many different countries.

example_sentences.japanese: その発言に対しては様々な受けとり方ができると思います。
example_sentences.english: I think there are various ways to interpret that remark.

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグの社員は、どこの出身かによって、肌の色も体型も大きさも様々で、みんなそれぞれユニークな個性をもっています。
example_sentences.english: Tofugu workers vary in size, shape, and color, depending on where they come from. They all have unique characteristics.

notes: "This is a strange word, I'm afraid. You'll have to bear with it. This, when added onto a word, is like adding an ""-al"" to a word (or a -like to a word). For example, add it onto 日本 (Japan) and you have ""Japanese-like,"" which comes out to ""Very Japanese."" It's a weird sort of modifying word that really depends on each situation it's in, though -al and -like often do a decent job. For now, just know this word means these things. We'll start applying it to various words in the future, slowly but surely." The reading is the same as the one you learned with the kanji, probably because this is usually added onto other words, making it behave like a jukugo.

example_sentences.japanese: 自分的には上手にアメリカ的なスピーチができたと思ってたんだけどな。
example_sentences.english: I personally thought I was able to give an American-style speech pretty well.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチの神ぴ的なえみが、こ人的にめっちゃツボなんだよね。
example_sentences.english: I just personally love Koichi's mysterious smile.

example_sentences.japanese: Tofugu的秘密計画って一体何ですか？もう少し具体的におっしゃって頂けませんか？
example_sentences.english: What do you mean by a Tofugu-like secret plan? Do you think you could be more specific?

notes: "Something that can move by its self is something that's automatic." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ボーナスで、全自動のフロントロードしきのせんたくきを買う予定です。
example_sentences.english: I'm planning to buy a fully-automatic front loading washing machine with my bonus.

example_sentences.japanese: スマホでとった写しんは、全て自動でクラウドにアップロードしてほぞんされるようにせっ定しています。
example_sentences.english: I set up my smartphone to automatically upload every single photo to the cloud.

example_sentences.japanese: Tofuguの方針で、許可無くコウイチのベーコンを食べた社員は、自動的に退職処分となる。
example_sentences.english: It’s Tofugu policy that workers caught eating Koichi’s bacon without permission are automatically fired.

english: Bad Feeling, Feeling Bad, Feeling Terrible, Unpleasant, Gross
notes: "The 気持ち (feeling) is bad. So, you can imagine how you feel isn't good, it's a bad feeling. You're feeling terrible, in fact." "The readings come from the words 気持ち and 悪い. Hopefully you've seen both and can combine them together to know the reading automatically. No bad feelings with this word, right?"

example_sentences.japanese: 二日よいで、頭はガンガンするし、めっちゃ気持ち悪いし、最悪だよ。
example_sentences.english: I'm hungover, I have a bad headache, and I feel terrible. This is awful.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは気持ち悪いネコなで声で、ビエトをよんだ。
example_sentences.english: Koichi called out to Viet with his sickly sweet voice.

example_sentences.japanese: ちょっと、そんな風に腕を曲げるのやめてくれない？めちゃくちゃ気持ち悪いんだけど。
example_sentences.english: Stop bending your arms like that. It’s seriously weirding me out.

notes: "When something is all perfect it is complete. Not only that, but it's perfect (because it's ALL perfect, not just partially so)." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグは日々少しずつ完全のいきに近づいている。
example_sentences.english: Tofugu is approaching perfection little by little every day.

example_sentences.japanese: 残念ながら、コウイチには完全なアリバイがあります。
example_sentences.english: Unfortunately, Koichi has a perfect alibi.

example_sentences.japanese: ああ、もう！お前のせいで完全に気が散っちゃったじゃないか！話したいことって何なんだよ。オフィスで飼う犬だっけか？
example_sentences.english: Oh jeez! Now you’ve completely distracted me. What was it that you wanted to talk about... office dog, was it?

notes: "Something that's outside the example doesn't follow the rules. It's not what it's supposed to be (the example), it is the exception." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: このレストランの料理は例外なくどれも美味しいです。
example_sentences.english: All the dishes at this restaurant are delicious without exception.

example_sentences.japanese: きわめて例外のケースをのぞいて、この病院がその手術に成功したのをほとんど見たことがありません。
example_sentences.english: Except for a few exceptional cases, I haven't actually seen this hospital successfully complete the procedure.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチはいつも朝遅くまで寝ていますが、金曜日はスーツを着なくてはいけないので例外です。
example_sentences.english: Koichi usually sleeps in, but Friday is an exception because he has to wear a suit.

notes: "The beauty art is not just any art. It's the best art. It's fine art." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 大学で美術のクラスをとっています。
example_sentences.english: I am taking a fine arts class at college.

example_sentences.japanese: き業のリーダーには美術のセンスも必要とされるが、コウイチにはそんなセンスは全くない。
example_sentences.english: Leaders of companies need to have a sense for fine art, but Koichi doesn't have anything like that.

example_sentences.japanese: アヤは、人間の剥製という美しい美術作品が並べられたアジトを「Tofuguの恐ろしい美術館」と名付けた。そして、コウイチとビエトもその剥製の一つにされようとしていた。
example_sentences.english: "Aya named her hideout the ""Tofugu Terrible Art Gallery"" because it was filled with her beautiful artwork-stuffed corpses. Koichi and Viet were to join her collection."

notes: "The origin of your foundation is where you have to work from when learning something new. For example, the 基本 portions of WaniKani are the earlier levels, especially the radicals. They are the foundation you need to learn your kanji and vocab later on." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: この公しきが数学の基本だというダリン君の主ちょうは、基本的に正しいと思います。
example_sentences.english: I think Darin's claim is fundamentally right, and that this formula is basic to mathematics.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは、ビエトからヤクザの対外けいざいせいさくの基本について学んでいます。
example_sentences.english: Koichi is learning the basics of Yakuza external economic policy from Viet.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は日本語の基本中の基本も知らない超初心者です。
example_sentences.english: I’m a super beginner who doesn’t even know the most basic of basics of Japanese.

notes: "A good like is something you like really good, if that makes any sense. This thing is a good and favorable thing." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You've learned them already, so you should be able to read this on your own!

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグと日本せいふは、良好なかんけいをたもっています。
example_sentences.english: Tofugu and the Japanese government have a good relationship.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチ先生は、ムッツリスケベであることは生物学的に良好なことだっておっしゃってましたよ。
example_sentences.english: Dr. Koichi told me that it's biologically favorable to be a dirty-minded person who doesn't talk about it.

example_sentences.japanese: その患者さんの経過は過去六ヶ月間良好で、普段通りの生活を送ることができています。
example_sentences.english: The patient has been doing well for the last six months and has been able to live a normal life.

notes: "You've hopefully seen 消化 by now and know that it means ""digestion."" If you know that, then you can see that the ""digestion"" is not good. When your digestion is not good, what do you have? Indigestion. Excuse me, I have to run to the restroom..." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Knowing 消化 and 不良 will help as well."

example_sentences.japanese: 消化不良のくすりをさがしています。
example_sentences.english: I'm looking for indigestion meds.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチくんにこく白したんだけど、返事が全然はっきりしなかったから、消化不良ですごくモヤモヤしてるんだよね。
example_sentences.english: I asked Koichi out, but his answer was very unclear and it's making me frustrated and giving me indigestion.

example_sentences.japanese: 今、消化不良で苦しんでるの。胸焼けもするし、膨満感もあるし、すごく気持ち悪い。しばらく放っておいてくれない。
example_sentences.english: I am suffering from indigestion. I have heartburn, bloating, and I feel sick to my stomach. Please leave me alone.

notes: "The abilities you originally start out with are instincts. Animals have lots of them because they aren't very good at learning. They have to start out knowing them from the start." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 動物は本能的に火をおそれるが、コウイチは例外だった。
example_sentences.english: Animals have an instinctive fear of fire, but Koichi was an exception.

example_sentences.japanese: いつも、生まれもった本能のおももくままにできるだけしたがうようにしています。
example_sentences.english: I always try to rely on my innate instincts as much as possible.

example_sentences.japanese: 熊は、動物の本能で危険を察知した。
example_sentences.english: The bear sensed danger with its animal instincts.

notes: "You wouldn't put your idea in a diagram ~like format if it wasn't intentional. Doing that takes a lot of work. So you can only make diagram like things on purpose!" "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You haven't learned this reading for 図 yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you:You intentionally stub your toe (と) all the time! If you hurt your toe on purpose you can get out of class and work! It's a really simple injury, but you can't do other stuff while it's hurt, so you always do it on purpose to get out of things."

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは、トーフグ社員の基本給を、意図的に引き上げた。
example_sentences.english: Koichi intentionally raised the base pay for Tofugu employees.

example_sentences.japanese: でもそれちょっと、意図的な作り話っぽくない？
example_sentences.english: But don't you think it sounds a little like an intentionally made-up story?

example_sentences.japanese: 意図的に情報を操作している奴がいる。
example_sentences.english: There’s a guy manipulating the news on purpose.

notes: "A person whose ideas are grounded in evil is a malicious, mean jerk! " "This reading is a combination of the on'yomi readings for 意 and 地, and the kun'yomi reading for 悪. You've learned them all already, so this should be cake!"

example_sentences.japanese: 折角の時間をあんな意地悪なやつのためにむだにするなんてもったいないよ。
example_sentences.english: Don't waste your precious time on such a jerk.

example_sentences.japanese: このようせいは、かわいいけど意地悪です。
example_sentences.english: This fairy is cute but malicious.

example_sentences.japanese: どうして妹に意地悪ばっかりするの！
example_sentences.english: Why are you so mean to my little sister?!

notes: "Something that looks like it was made near the period you're currently in is really modern! But if it looks like it's from a period not near the one you're in... throw it away! It isn't modern enough to touch your hands!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 近代的なデザインが気に入りました。
example_sentences.english: I like the modern design.

example_sentences.japanese: とても近代的な建物ですね。
example_sentences.english: It’s a really modern building, isn’t it?

example_sentences.japanese: 最近のプリクラはちょっと近代的になりすぎていると思う。
example_sentences.english: I think purikura is a bit too modern these days.

notes: "This has the same meaning as the kanji. The little り thrown on there is just a little remainder sticking off the end of the kanji. No need to pay attention to that." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: You're waiting inside. The remainder of your forces are out there, fighting. You don't know who will survive... or if they even will. You have a secret knock (のこ), though, that you use to find out if it's one of the remaining forces outside or the enemy, broken through. You hear a knock. What is it? Is it your men or theirs? Imagine it out, focusing on the knock conversation that happens between you and the remainder."

example_sentences.japanese: 残りの水はどこに行ったの？
example_sentences.english: Where is the leftover water?

example_sentences.japanese: さく夜のコウイチのツイートは、一にぎりの残りのフォロワーさえもおこらせてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: Koichi's tweet last night made even the small remainder of his followers very upset.

example_sentences.japanese: 今夜はデートがあるので、晩御飯は昼御飯の残りを温めて食べてね。ママより。
example_sentences.english: I’m going on a date tonight. You can heat up some leftovers from lunch to eat for dinner. Love, Mom.

english: Sexually Transmitted Disease, Std, Sexually Transmitted Infection, Sti
notes: "A gender sickness is one you catch from *ahem* doing things with those of another or the same gender. You only catch these sicknesses this way, meaning they're sexually transmitted diseases (save yourself some typing and just answer with STD)." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: こまってるんだったら、性病ちりょうのお金、少しだったら都合してあげられるよ。
example_sentences.english: I could lend you some money for the STD treatment, if you're hard up.

example_sentences.japanese: 全く都合の悪い時に性病にかかったもんだよ。
example_sentences.english: I got a sexually transmitted disease at the most inconvenient time.

example_sentences.japanese: 性病を移してくれてどうも有難う。とても嬉しいです。
example_sentences.english: Thank you very much for giving me an STD. It means a lot to me.

notes: "You like the status of what's in front of you. It has an excellent shape and form to it. Imagine something that would be pleasing to you in terms of its shape." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Just be sure to note the かく reading, which gets changed to かっ."

example_sentences.japanese: ずい文変わった格好だね。
example_sentences.english: Your style is pretty unique, eh?

example_sentences.japanese: 格好のいい車ですね。
example_sentences.english: Your car has a nice shape!

example_sentences.japanese: 「何でミカサがエレンのことを好きなのか私には分からないわ。だって、エレンって傲慢だし、思いやりがないし、それに格好良くもないのに。」「恋は盲目っていうじゃない。」
example_sentences.english: """I don’t understand why Mikasa likes Eren. He’s arrogant, he’s inconsiderate, and he isn’t even good-looking."" ""Love is blind."""

notes: "The status of your bones (aka how they're all arranged and put together) equals your skeleton. That bone status is lookin' good on you!" "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Just note that こつ changes to こっ."

example_sentences.japanese: ガッシリした骨格の男性がタイプです。
example_sentences.english: I like a man with a sturdy build.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日は、この記事の骨格をまとめ終えました。
example_sentences.english: Yesterday, I completed an outline for this article.

example_sentences.japanese: コーラが骨格の発育に悪影響を与えるという噂は本当ですか？
example_sentences.english: Is the rumor that cola is detrimental to skeletal development true?

notes: "A hard stubborn person is very stubborn no matter how you look at them. Try to break through that hard stubbornness and all you'll find is more stubborn." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 子どもが頑固でこまっています。
example_sentences.english: I'm having a hard time because my kid's stubborn.

example_sentences.japanese: 頑固なクリステンは、コウイチとビエトは死ぬまでずっと仲良しだと思うと言いはった。
example_sentences.english: Stubborn Kristen insisted that Koichi and Viet would stay friends till the end.

example_sentences.japanese: フグは根っからの頑固者で、自分のやり方にこだわります。
example_sentences.english: Fugu is stubborn to the core and is set in his ways.

notes: "The remainder of your thoughts are very small. You've thought of everything you possibly can to solve this problem. In the end, the remainder of your thoughts is left with one phrase: ""too bad."" There's nothing else to think but the remainder." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: それは残念すぎる。
example_sentences.english: That's so unfortunate.

example_sentences.japanese: 折角のチャンスだったのに、残念です。
example_sentences.english: It was such a rare chance, so it's too bad that I missed it.

example_sentences.japanese: 「このテレビ番組のために私が蜘蛛を食べなくちゃいけないって、本当？」「残念ながらそのようです。」
example_sentences.english: """Is it true that I have to eat spiders on this TV program?"" ""Unfortunately, it is."""

notes: "Things that are targeted as Japanese are more than just Japanese, they are very Japanese. This word may be hard to understand at first, but there are many things the Japanese consider to be Japanese-only. These theories range from reasonable to ridiculous, but either way, you'll see them described as 日本的." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. It will help if you know how to read 日本 as well."

example_sentences.japanese: 日本的なくらしにあこがれています。
example_sentences.english: I yearn for a Japan-style life.

example_sentences.japanese: このアニメはとても日本的ですね。
example_sentences.english: This anime is very Japanese, yeah?

example_sentences.japanese: フグは、サーモンの中に「日本的な優しさ」を見出した。
example_sentences.english: Fugu found a very Japanese gentleness in Salmon.

notes: "Drinking as much as you want is nice and all, but don't get sick. When you see this word, you know you're at an all you can drink place. Tip: Usually there's a time limit, so drink up!" "The reading comes from the word 放題 (ほうだい) and 飲む (のむ). So long as you know those vocab words, you'll be able to read this one as well."

example_sentences.japanese: 食べ放題と飲み放題だったらどっちの方がおとくかな？
example_sentences.english: I wonder which one is a better deal, all you can eat or all you can drink?

example_sentences.japanese: 「カナエ、ちょっと飲み会をき画してくれない？」「おっけー！どんなテーマの飲み会？」「うーんと、ビエトが日本で買ってきたコスプレコレクションのおひろ目会なんだけど。」「分かった。めっちゃ安い飲み放題のい酒屋でもいい？」
example_sentences.english: """Can you plan a drinking party, Kanae?"" ""Okay! What's the theme of the party?"" ""Well, it's for the presentation of Viet's cosplay collection that he bought in Japan."" ""Okay. Can we do it at a super cheap all-you-can-drink Izakaya?"""

example_sentences.japanese: 「じゃあ、あなたは昨夜飲み放題に行っていた訳ですね。他には何かしましたか？」「いや、まあそんなところだよ。」
example_sentences.english: """So, you went to an all you can drink place last night. Anything else?"" ""No, that’s about it."""

notes: "When you eat as much as you want, you are getting an all you can eat deal." "The reading consists of the readings of 食べる and 放題. If you know those you should be able to read this too."

example_sentences.japanese: 一しょに食べ放題に行ったのが、とおい昔のような気がするよ。
example_sentences.english: I feel like my memory of going to the all you can eat restaurant with you is growing distant.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本で、ケーキ食べ放題のカフェに行ってみたんですが、思っていたよりもたくさん食べられました。
example_sentences.english: I went to an all-you-can-eat cake cafe in Japan and I was actually able to eat more than I'd expected.

example_sentences.japanese: よし、今がチャンスだ。さあ、焼き肉食べ放題へ行こう。
example_sentences.english: Ok, the coast is clear. Let’s go get all you can eat yakiniku.

notes: "If you say something is going to clear up, you're usually talking about the weather. That makes it clear weather!" This has the same reading as the kanji you learned, meaning you know the reading!

example_sentences.japanese: 天気予ほうでは、明日も明後日も明々後日も晴れでしょうって言ってたよ。
example_sentences.english: The weather forecast said that it will be clear tomorrow, a day after tomorrow, and two days from now.

example_sentences.japanese: 予ほうは「晴れ後くもり」だし、かさはいらないんじゃない？
example_sentences.english: "The forecast says ""clear weather, with clouds later on,"" so I don't think you need an umbrella."

example_sentences.japanese: 折角の誕生日だし、晴れて良かったですね。
example_sentences.english: It’s a good thing it’s clear out on your birthday, eh?

hiragana: ぶきよう, ぶきっちょ
notes: "You know how 器用 means ""dextrous"" and ""skillful""? Well, this is when you're not those things. When you're not dextrous, you're clumsy and when you're not skillful you're unskillful." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Just keep in mind that the reading of 不 changes from ふ to ぶ. If you're clumsy you'll get a lot of boo-boos (ぶ), get it?"

example_sentences.japanese: 十代は、不器用な私にとって、とても大変な時期でした。
example_sentences.english: My teens were the hardest years for an awkward person like me.

example_sentences.japanese: 不器用な助手が、不器用な手つきで、いつものようにクソ不味いコーヒーをいれてくれた。
example_sentences.english: My clumsy assistant made very disgusting coffee with his clumsy hands, as usual.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の主人は堅苦しくて不器用ですが、正直者です。
example_sentences.english: My husband is strict and clumsy, but he’s an honest person.

notes: "The earth district isn't our solar system or something like that. We're talking about a specific portion of earth, and naming it as a district. So, what is this patch of earth? It's a district, area, or zone." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 来月から、この地区のたん当者が変わるので、あらかじめお知らせさせていただきます。
example_sentences.english: I would like to inform you in advance that the person in charge of this zone will change next month.

example_sentences.japanese: この地区には、りん時ふくしきゅう付金を受きゅうしている人が三十八人います。
example_sentences.english: There are thirty-eight people who receive provisional welfare benefits in this district.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは、近日中に地区検察局に自白内容を収めたビデオテープを送ることを計画しているようですよ。
example_sentences.english: It seems that Koichi is planning to give a videotaped confession to the district attorney’s office soon.

notes:
"When you can't (not) believe in someone, it's because you distrust them. Maybe someone discredited them and now you mistrust everything they say." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

"There are not any shakes or waves or anything fun like that. It is just pure dullness." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: あの変人が不信の目でおれのことを見てくるんだよ。
example_sentences.english: That oddball is giving me a distrusting stare.

example_sentences.japanese: ワニカニユーザーのトーフグへの不信はつのるばかりだった。
example_sentences.english: WaniKani users' distrust of Tofugu just keeps getting stronger.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい日本語学習教材を部分的に公開することは、我々の会社が何か事実を隠蔽しようとしているとの不信を招くかもしれないじゃないですか？
example_sentences.english: Don’t you think that only partial release of the new Japanese learning material may feed suspicion that our company is covering up some facts?

example_sentences.japanese: 私のCDはしばらく売上不振に苦しんでいたが、ラジオで紹介されてから今月は売上げが上昇しています。
example_sentences.english: My CD was suffering from a slump in sales for a little while, but since being introduced on the radio, sales are rising again.

notes: "The English language is the language you're reading right here and now. This is the English language. It is English." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 英語の発音は日本語の発音よりむずかしいと思う。
example_sentences.english: I think English pronunciation is more difficult than Japanese pronunciation.

example_sentences.japanese: もしこのレストランの店員も英語が話せるようだったら、今後わざわざあの店まで行かなくてすむようになるね。
example_sentences.english: If this restaurant's workers turn out to be able to speak English, we won't have to go all the way to the other one any more.

example_sentences.japanese: 「僕たちは皆、英語と数学の授業が嫌いだ。」「ちょっと、一緒にしないでよ。私は両方共好きだし。」
example_sentences.english: """All of us hate our English and Math classes."" ""Hey, speak for yourself. I like both of them."""

notes: "The method of writing is how you write. You can have vocabulary words, but you have to be able to put them together using some kind of method. This method happens to be grammar." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. The ほう changes to ぽう."

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語の文法の本をさがしています。
example_sentences.english: I'm looking for a Japanese grammar book.

example_sentences.japanese: 文法を学べば学ぶほど、文章をかくのが上手になりますよ。
example_sentences.english: The more grammar you learn, the better your writing will become.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の上司、見た目はできる男なのに、いつも間違った文法を使うのが残念すぎるよ。
example_sentences.english: My boss looks like a smart person, so it’s too bad that he always makes grammar mistakes.

notes: "A not law is something that's against the law. It's illegal or unlawful." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトが行っている不法のやみとり引のことを、トーフグの社員はだれも知らない。
example_sentences.english: None of the Tofugu workers know about the illegal black-market transactions that Viet does.

example_sentences.japanese: アメリカにはげん時てんで何人の不法たいざい者がいると思いますか？
example_sentences.english: How many illegal aliens do you think there are in the U.S. at the moment?

example_sentences.japanese: 不法な捜査で得た証拠は法廷では使えませんよ。
example_sentences.english: We can’t use evidence obtained through an unlawful search at the court.

notes: "The sea army are the branch of the military that has boats and does ocean/sea things. What's that? The navy." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 海軍にいた時、おれ的にはお前には十分すぎるぐらいやさしくしてたつもりなんだけどな。
example_sentences.english: By my standards, I was almost too nice to you when we were in the navy.

example_sentences.japanese: この海軍のしきたりでは、本当に悪かったなと思って反せいしている人は、自らすすんでトイレそうじをすることでせい意を見せることになっています。
example_sentences.english: As an institution of this navy, if someone is genuinely sorry about something, they have to volunteer to clean the toilet to show their good faith.

example_sentences.japanese: 電話に出れなくてごめん。信じられないかもしれないけど、実は今海軍の船の上なんだよね。降りたら電話するね。
example_sentences.english: I’m sorry I couldn’t catch your call. Believe it or not, I’m actually on a navy ship right now. I’ll call you when I get off.

notes: "When something has poison it is poisonous and toxic." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ガラガラヘビって有毒なんですか？
example_sentences.english: Are rattle snakes venomous?

example_sentences.japanese: ダリンが道ばたに生えていた有毒キノコを間ちがって食べて、病院にはこばれてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: Darin ate a poisonous fungus growing on the side road by mistake and was sent to a hospital.

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトだけがコウイチのオナラが有毒ガスのような臭いがすることを知っている。
example_sentences.english: Only Viet knows that Koichi’s farts smell like toxic fumes.

notes: "A stubborn height is a shorter, stockier height. It makes a person especially solid, firm, and stout." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 土台はできるだけ頑丈にしておいた方がいいですよ。
example_sentences.english: You should make the foundation as firm as possible.

example_sentences.japanese: この車はとても頑丈にできています。
example_sentences.english: This car is solidly built.

example_sentences.japanese: 眼鏡屋さんで、とても頑丈な眼鏡を作ってもらいました。
example_sentences.english: I had a really solid pair of glasses made by my optician.

notes: "The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. This is more the ""strange"" meaning though, not the ""change"" one. As in, you 変な猫！." The reading is the one you learned with the kanji. How strange! Or not.

example_sentences.japanese: はしらのかげに変な人がいると思ったらただのコウイチだった。
example_sentences.english: I thought there was a strange man behind the pole, but it was just Koichi.

example_sentences.japanese: 同じ仕事をしているのに男性の方が女性よりきゅう料が高いなんてぜっ対に変だよ！
example_sentences.english: It's absolutely absurd that men get higher pay than women despite doing the same work!

example_sentences.japanese: 変だなぁ。僕のメールボックスには、君が送ったと言っているメールがどこにも見当たらないよ。
example_sentences.english: That’s strange. I can’t find the email you say you sent me anywhere in my mailbox.

notes: "With the height of my husband, he's very firm. Try to push him over. Impossible. He's so tall and sturdy due to his height." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. Watch out for the rendaku.

example_sentences.japanese: 私のつまは、あまり体が丈夫ではなく、よく病気になります。
example_sentences.english: My wife isn't very healthy and she gets sick often.

example_sentences.japanese: このいすはとても丈夫なので、すもう取りがすわってもこわれません。
example_sentences.english: This chair is so sturdy that even a sumo wrestler can sit down in it without it breaking.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼が丈夫な男だってことは分かってるけど、暴飲暴食の習慣がちょっと心配なんだよね。
example_sentences.english: I know he’s a sturdy guy, but I’m a little worried about his excessive eating and drinking habits.

notes: "The simple bits of language are the individual words. If you think about it, this is true. First of all, there are a ton of them. Second, they're tiny. They're just little bits of language and the ""word"" for these little bits is word." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語の単語の単語ちょうを作りました。
example_sentences.english: I made a notebook for Japanese vocabulary.

example_sentences.japanese: 単語の意味が分からない時は、じしょを引きます。
example_sentences.english: When I don't know the meaning of a word, I look it up in my dictionary.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語の単語ゲーム作ったんだけど、やってみない？
example_sentences.english: I created a Japanese word game. Do you want to try?

notes: "An automatical (自動 + 的) thing of course isn't ""automatical."" A better way to say it is to cut off the -al and call it automatic." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. It will help to know the reading of 自動 as well."

example_sentences.japanese: それは、ボットによる自動的なツイートですよ。
example_sentences.english: That's an automated tweet by a bot.

example_sentences.japanese: この電車のドアは、自動的には開きません。
example_sentences.english: This train's doors don't open automatically.

example_sentences.japanese: もし誰かがあなたの家に侵入したら、この機械が自動的に警備会社に通報します。
example_sentences.english: If someone breaks into your house this machine will automatically send a message to the security company.

english: Brand New, New Item, New Product
notes: "A new product is something that's brand new or a new item. I like looking around the store for the brand new stuff because it's interesting!" "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Notice though that ひん changes to ぴん. This is because you're buying some brand new pins?"

example_sentences.japanese: 線路に新品のそろばんを落としてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: I dropped my brand new abacus onto the train tracks.

example_sentences.japanese: 新品のジーパンになっとうをこぼしてしまって、テンションめっちゃ下がってます。
example_sentences.english: I spilt some fermented soy beans on my new jeans and that ruined my mood.

example_sentences.japanese: 「新しいパソコンを買ったんだって？」「うーん。新品ではないんだけどね。ビエトのお下がりだよ。」
example_sentences.english: """I heard you bought a new computer."" ""Well, it’s not brand new. It’s a hand-me-down from Viet."""

notes: "When something is ""old rules-like,"" it is not very modern. It is in the past. It is classical." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは写真で古典的なポーズをとるのが好きなようだね。
example_sentences.english: Koichi seems to like taking classical poses in photos.

example_sentences.japanese: こんな古典的なさぎに引っかかってしまって、本当に情けないです。
example_sentences.english: It's super shameful that I was deceived by such a classical fraud.

example_sentences.japanese: あの日本の古典的なスタイルの画家は、私が知っている人の中で、一番好みがうるさいです。どうしてそんなに色々気にするのか理解不能です。
example_sentences.english: That classical-style Japanese painter is the pickiest person I know. I can’t understand why she cares so much.

notes: "Who are all like ""I want to preserve and protect what I have, get out of my business, government!""? That's why people who want to preserve and protect are conservative." "The reading doesn't match up for this word's 守. The reading is しゅ, but you can remember that because the conservatives want to protect and preserve their hoes (ほ) and their shoes (しゅ) from the government. For some reason those get taxed a lot."

example_sentences.japanese: 保守的な学校だったので、学生はみんな校そく通りにせい服を着用するよう要求されました。
example_sentences.english: My school was very conservative, so students were required to wear uniforms in accordance with the school regulations.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本国民は、保守的な国民だと思いますか？
example_sentences.english: Do you think the Japanese are conservative people?

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチはビエトに、年をとるにつれて保守的になる人が多いけど、俺はそうはなりたくない、と言った。
example_sentences.english: Koichi told Viet that people tend to become more conservative as they get older, but he doesn’t want to be like that.

notes: "Things that are below normal products are the cheap knockoffs and bad quality items. These items are incredibly crude in their manufacturing and design. So much vulgarity!" "You haven't seen this reading for 下 yet (sorry there's so many for this kanji!). Those items are so crude that you can't even tell what they're supposed to be. Honestly they all just look like statues of lumpy geckos (げ). That says it's a lamp but it looks more like a gecko looking at the sky. That chair? Definitely a bunch of geckos having a pool party. Are you sure you didn't get this stuff from a weird gecko artist?"

example_sentences.japanese: 私は下品な英語の基本をマスターしました。
example_sentences.english: I've mastered the fundamentals of vulgar English.

example_sentences.japanese: はるか遠くから、下品な笑い声が聞こえてきた。
example_sentences.english: I heard a vulgar laugh from the distance.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたの下品なメールは会社に戻ってからじっくり読ませてもらいます。
example_sentences.english: I’ll carefully read your crude email for you when I get back to the office.

english: "Face Of A Person, Person's Face, Face"
notes: "The face of a face is a face, but more specifically the face of a person. Probably because the most face-like thing you can ever have is a human's face... at least in our eyes (by ""our"" I mean the human race's eyes, because I am totally with you guys on that one)." "The reading for 顔 isn't the one you learned with the kanji. But, we're going to learn that reading right now.The worst thing that can happen to a face is if a face disappears. If it becomes totally gone (がん). A man that is walking up to you with no face, is a man with a gone face. Those men are men who are a part of the gone men (がんめん). Faces, totally gone!"

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグの社員たちは、みんな顔面へんさちが高い。
example_sentences.english: Tofugu workers' facial deviation values are all very high.

example_sentences.japanese: ストレスが原因の顔面神けいつうになやまされています。
example_sentences.english: I'm suffering from facial neuralgia caused by stress.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はアスファルトに顔面を強打した。
example_sentences.english: I hit my face hard on the asphalt.

notes: "The things that are basic (基本) like (的) are your basics and fundamentals. These are like the radicals you learn with your kanji. They're the fundamentals!" "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Knowing how to read the word 基本 will be helpful too."

example_sentences.japanese: 基本的に政治に関心がないんです。
example_sentences.english: Basically, I have no interest in politics.

example_sentences.japanese: 上司に、基本的な事も知らない役立たずだと言われました。
example_sentences.english: I was told by my boss that I don't even know the fundamentals and that I'm useless.

example_sentences.japanese: どのくらい頻繁に自分の超基本的な間違いにびっくりしますか？
example_sentences.english: How often are you surprised by making basic mistakes?

notes: "When you carry happiness with you, you look at the good side of everything and end up having really good luck. Someone who carries happiness will be really lucky in life." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 幸運になるおまじないよ。
example_sentences.english: I’ll get good luck with this good luck charm.

example_sentences.japanese: このフォーチュンクッキーには、だれかの代わりに引っこしの荷ときをしてくれたら、あなたに幸運がおとずれるでしょう、って書いてあるよ。
example_sentences.english: This fortune cookie says that fortune will come to you if you help unpack moving boxes for somebody.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチの名前の意味は、一番幸運な人っていう意味なんじゃないかとすいそくしてるんだけど、どう思う？
example_sentences.english: "I'm guessing that the meaning of Koichi's name is the ""most lucky"" person. What do you think?"

notes: "The ground/earth face is the surface that makes up the ground or the Earth's surface." "The reading for 面 is what you'd expect. 地 on the other hand is じ, which is a bit different (though close sounding) to what you learned previously. Thank the Chinese and their ever changing language for this one. Think of Jesus laying on the ground, telling you how comfortable the ground is. You say ""Jesus, you have to get off the ground, you have a dinner to go to,"" but he doesn't want to leave."

example_sentences.japanese: 海の中じゃなくて地面の中に住めたらいいのに、とフグは言いました。
example_sentences.english: Fugu said that he'd rather live underground than underwater.

example_sentences.japanese: 家の前の庭は草が生えていないので、夏の間は地面がとても熱くなります。
example_sentences.english: Our front yard doesn't have any grass, so the earth's surface gets really hot during summer.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチはフグを優しく撫でてから、地面に降ろしてあげました。
example_sentences.english: Koichi gently stroked Fugu and placed him on the ground.

notes: "With a little luck and happiness you can achieve happiness, though that goes without saying." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 幸福の科学というしゅう教団体について調べてみました。
example_sentences.english: I looked up some information about a religious group called Happy Science.

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグに幸福をもたらすために、コウイチはじゅう業員全員に幸福のフグのおまもりを一万ドルで買わせようとしました。
example_sentences.english: In order to bring happiness to Tofugu, Koichi tried to make all of his employees buy a happiness fugu charm for $10,000 each.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は幸運の星のもとに生まれたため、幸福すぎて毎日涙が止まらないんだよ。
example_sentences.english: She was born under a lucky star and she has so much happiness in her life that she can’t help but cry every day.

notes: "This is the noun version of the kanji 幸. Kanji means happiness and the vocab word means happiness." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: You're seeking true happiness. You visit a great guru who's said to help people find their happiness, but she keeps hitting you on the head while you try to talk to her. You end up with the special happiness chant, ""She Ow! Say (しあわせ) I should say this."" You can never get it out without saying ow, but you're pretty sure happiness is coming."

example_sentences.japanese: 末ながくお幸せにね。
example_sentences.english: I wish you happiness for many years to come.

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトは、うらないしから今年中に幸せがおとずれると言われました。
example_sentences.english: A fortune teller told Viet that happiness will come to him within the year.

example_sentences.japanese: 「私はお金で幸せは買えると思います。何故なら、私は花火を見ていると幸せな気持ちになるからです。もし私が大金持ちだったら、毎日花火を楽しんでずっと幸せな気持ちでいられることができます。」彼女は幸せそうな口調でそう言った。
example_sentences.english: """I think money can buy happiness because watching fireworks makes me happy. If I had a lot of money, I could enjoy fireworks every day and feel happy all the time,"" she said happily."

notes: "You know that 完全 means ""complete"" or ""perfect."" So, a not ""complete"" or ""perfect"" is something that is incomplete or imperfect." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. It also will help if you can read 完全."

example_sentences.japanese: 不完全な形のあいってどんなものですか。
example_sentences.english: What kind of love is imperfect?

example_sentences.japanese: 完全なものよりも不完全なものの方が人情味があってよくない？
example_sentences.english: Aren't incomplete things better than complete things, since they have a humanness about them?

example_sentences.japanese: 勝ち試合が雨で中止になり、Tofuguソフトボールチームのシーズンが不完全に終わった。
example_sentences.english: The Tofugu softball team had an incomplete end to their season when the game they were winning was suspended due to rain.

notes: "When you can not cure something, this is a problem of incurability." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 不治のがんで、よ命三ヶ月だとせん告されました。
example_sentences.english: I was diagnosed with an incurable cancer and I've been given three months to live.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の息子は、不治ののうしっかんと戦っています。
example_sentences.english: My son is fighting an irreversible brain disorder.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは一度不治の病に倒れ、「俺たちは必ず、また会えるよ」とビエトに言い残し亡くなったのですが、言葉通り次の日にはオフィスに出勤し、以前と全く同じように業務をこなしました。
example_sentences.english: "When Koichi fell incurably ill and died, his last words to Viet were, ""We will meet again."" True to his words, he came back to the office the next day and did everything the same as he had before."

notes: "When you are able to guarantee against risk, it's probably because you bought some good insurance! What do you use? The gecko 保険?" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: どうして日本では、女性が保険の外交をすることが多いんですか？
example_sentences.english: Why is it more common for women to do insurance sales in Japan?

example_sentences.japanese: 保険にか入するのに、出生証明書は必要ですか？
example_sentences.english: Do I need a birth certificate to get insurance?

example_sentences.japanese: しまった。また家に健康保険証を忘れてきちゃった。
example_sentences.english: Oh no, I left my health insurance card at home again.

notes: "When you discuss something superfluous you aren't being serious, you're telling a joke." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: つまらない冗談に係わってるひまはないんだよ。
example_sentences.english: I have no time to waste on a stupid joke.

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグはポッドキャストで冗談ばかり言っているが、時々冗談の通じない人からいかりのメールをもらうことがあります。
example_sentences.english: Tofugu likes joking on their podcast, but sometimes they get angry emails from people who don't get the jokes.

example_sentences.japanese: 冗談はヤメてよ！何でフレンチレストランなんて行きたいの？私達の柄じゃないっしょ。飲めればどこでもいいじゃん？違う？
example_sentences.english: Stop joking around. Why do you want to go to a French restaurant? We shouldn’t break our pattern. If we’re just going drinking, anywhere is fine, right?

notes: "The reality is that it's black. Like, so black that it's beyond fake black, it's reality black. This is so black it's pitch black." "The reading for the 真 is the vocab kun'yomi reading. Think of what is pitch black. It's your poor Ma (ま). She is so dark that she sucks in light, like a black hole... wait, she is a black hole, it explains why your Ma is pitch black."

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは真っ黒なニンニクが好きで、よくしたから血が出るまで食べています。
example_sentences.english: Koichi loves pitch black garlic and he often eats it so much that his tongue bleeds.

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトはハワイのビーチで日やけして帰ってきたんですが、まるでこげたトーストのようにものの見事に真っ黒でした。
example_sentences.english: When Viet came back, he was pure black, like a burned toast, because he'd gotten so thoroughly tanned at a Hawaiian beach.

example_sentences.japanese: やばい、超絶に可愛い真っ黒なワンピース見つけちゃったんだけど。
example_sentences.english: OMG, I just came across the cutest pitch black dress.

english: Risky, Unsafe, Dangerous, Danger, Peril, Hazard
notes: "Something that is dangerous and risky is probably pretty risky dangerous, and unsafe." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: まだ危険なじょうきょうだが、回ふくの希望はある。
example_sentences.english: It's still a risky situation, but there is hope for his recovery.

example_sentences.japanese: 駅ではよく、「危険ですから黄色い線の内がわまでお下がりください」というアナウンスが流れています。
example_sentences.english: "In stations, there is often an announcement that says, ""It will be unsafe, so please stay behind the yellow line."""

example_sentences.japanese: 我が社が現在債務不履行の危険性に瀕しているのは真実だが、リスクを覚悟のうえで、信頼に基づいて行動し続けるしかないと思うんだ。
example_sentences.english: That's true that our company is at risk of defaulting on its loan, but I believe that we have to keep taking risks and acting based on our faith.

notes: "Everything on a location's surface is really just a part of the scene before you. This is the kind of scene that would be set in a novel. It's the setting." The reading is a combination of kun'yomi and on'yomi readings. That being said, both readings for both kanji are the readings you learned already, so you should be able to read this.

example_sentences.japanese: つまが荷物をまとめて出ていく場面が自分にかさなりつらくなりました。
example_sentences.english: When I watched the scene where the wife packs up and leaves, I saw myself in her and felt bitter.

example_sentences.japanese: このフレーズは、ビジネスの場面で有効です。
example_sentences.english: This phrase is useful in a business setting.

example_sentences.japanese: 最後の場面で泣いてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: I cried during the last scene.

english: Specialty, Speciality, Area Of Study, Major
notes: "Your specialty gate is the thing you open to let out your specialty. Imagine the thing you're best at (your specialty). Now imagine opening a gate in your chest that lets it out, allowing you to be good at it." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: それは私の専門外です。
example_sentences.english: That's out of my area of study.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の姉は、ペット専門の目医者です。
example_sentences.english: My older sister is a specialty pet eye doctor.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の専門は天文学です。新しい星を発見したいです。
example_sentences.english: My specialty is astronomy. I want to discover new stars.

notes:
"When you do not have happiness, you have unhappiness and misfortune." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

"Not filial piety is when you don't listen to your parents. This is disobedience to parents." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: まるで不幸のどん底のようにいるような顔をしてるけど、大丈夫？
example_sentences.english: You look as if you're in the depths of misfortune. Are you okay?

example_sentences.japanese: 家族に不幸があったので、明日、明後日会社を休ませてください。
example_sentences.english: There was a death in my family. Can I take tomorrow and the day after off?

example_sentences.japanese: 不幸は仲間を好むってよく言うけど、それって私があなたと付き合っている理由をうまく説明しているよね。
example_sentences.english: They say misery loves company, which explains why I’m dating you.

example_sentences.japanese: 自分の家族の不孝になるようなことは、絶対にしたくない。
example_sentences.english: I never want to do anything that would be disrespectful toward my family.

notes: "You only need to hurry to something if it's urgent and it happened all of a sudden. You didn't even have time to prepare." This has the same reading as the kanji you learned, meaning you know the reading!

example_sentences.japanese: あの男は、つまと二人の子を残して急に死んでしまったんだよ。
example_sentences.english: That guy suddenly passed away leaving his wife and two children behind.

example_sentences.japanese: 急な仕事を引き受けちゃったので、今日のおむかえはおそくなります。
example_sentences.english: I took an urgent assignment, so I have to pick my kid up later than usual today.

example_sentences.japanese: 急な依頼ですみません。どうしても断れないお客様からの急ぎの注文だったんです。
example_sentences.english: Sorry for the sudden request. We had to take an urgent order from the customer we cannot refuse.

notes: "The tea supply is down to nothing??? That's absurd! For Americans, I imagine this word would be ""無コーヒー"" instead. Get it?? If you're a caffeine addict this word will make total sense." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: こんなに車がビュンビュン通っていて横だん歩道もないのに、向こう側へわたるなんて、無茶だよ。
example_sentences.english: It's absurd to cross such a busy road without a pedestrian crossing.

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトは無茶なりょうのあわもりを飲んでいました。
example_sentences.english: Viet was drinking excessive amounts of awamori.

example_sentences.japanese: カレーソースでいっぱいのプールで泳ごうなんて、彼も無茶な決定をしたものだ。
example_sentences.english: He made the rash decision to try and swim in a pool filled with curry sauce.

notes: "Someone with ""nothing"" for their name is trying to remain anonymous." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: フグは、無名のまま死にたくないと思っている。
example_sentences.english: Fugu doesn’t want to die in anonymity.

example_sentences.japanese: 若手のアーティストの中には、無名でも良い作品を作る人がたくさんいます。
example_sentences.english: Among young artists, there are many unknowns producing good work.

example_sentences.japanese: アリアナ・グランデは自分の才能を少しも鼻にかけず、無名の新人歌手にも優しく接するらしいので、とても好感がもてます。
example_sentences.english: I heard that Ariana Grande is not a bit stuck up in spite of her talent and is very nice to unknown singers too, so I have a good impression of her.

notes: "Both sides is both sides. Which side? Both sides." The first kanji takes the on'yomi reading and the second takes the kun'yomi reading. Luckily you know both of them already!

example_sentences.japanese: 両側の耳がかゆくてむずむずします。
example_sentences.english: Both of my ears itch immensely.

example_sentences.japanese: 二ひきの犬が、両側から私に鼻をすりつけてきました。
example_sentences.english: Two dogs nuzzled against me from both sides.

example_sentences.japanese: 両側に女の子をはべらせたビエトの写真がパパラッチに売りつけられた。
example_sentences.english: A picture of Viet, with girls on both sides of him, was sold to the paparazzi.

notes: "Rejoice drama isn't so much drama as it is comedy, since it makes you rejoice." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: その映画は悲しすぎて、喜劇というよりは悲劇だ。
example_sentences.english: The movie is too sad. It should be called a tragedy, not a comedy.

example_sentences.japanese: 喜劇王チャップリンのドキュメンタリーを観て自分もお笑いの道を目指そうと思いました。
example_sentences.english: After watching a documentary about Chaplin, the king of comedy, I decided to pursue a career in comedy.

example_sentences.japanese: すごく暑かったので、喜劇を観ながらずっと自分をうちわで扇いでいました。
example_sentences.english: It was so hot that I kept fanning myself while watching the comedy show.

notes: "A thing that is detailed and thin is the details. It will help to remember that 細かい also means detailed, which is probably where this meaning is more coming from. Detailed + Detailed = the details." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: このユーザーは、いつも詳細なフィードバックを送ってくれます。
example_sentences.english: This user often sends us very detailed feedback.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチさんは貧しい家に生まれたと聞いたんですが、もう少し詳細を教えてもらえませんか？
example_sentences.english: Mr. Koichi, I heard you were born poor. Could you give me more details on that?

example_sentences.japanese: 詳細を調べている時間がありません。
example_sentences.english: I don’t have enough time to look up the details.

notes: "Something that is drama al is dramatic." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: ダイエットを始めて三ヶ月で体型が劇的に変化しました。
example_sentences.english: Three months after starting my diet, my body had changed dramatically.

example_sentences.japanese: 劇的とまではいかないけれど、かなりの売り上げがあったことは間違いないようです。
example_sentences.english: While it's not a dramatic increase, it does seem that they received quite a bit of revenue.

example_sentences.japanese: 応援してるチームが劇的なさよならホームランで勝利を納めた時、思わずウルッときてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: I got tears in my eyes when my favorite team won the game with a dramatic home run.

notes: "A normal injustice!  It's a terrible thing that happened, and despite it being normal it's still an emergency." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: この非常ブレーキ、こわれてるかもしれないよ。
example_sentences.english: I think this e-brake might be broken.

example_sentences.japanese: 急に非常ベルが鳴り出して、びっくりしました。何かの非常事たいだったんですか？
example_sentences.english: The emergency alarm suddenly went off and I was surprised. Was it some sort of emergency situation?

example_sentences.japanese: いつでも家に非常食を備えて置くことは良いことです。
example_sentences.english: It’s always good to keep some emergency rations at home.

notes: "This is a single kanji with an い on the end, meaning you know it's probably an adjective. What's the adjective form of void? It's empty or vacant. Just think of what has to happen to make a void in the first place." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: If everything in life seems empty and futile, even cows will be affected. Listen to them say, ""Moo, nah (むな), never mind. What's the point?"" Nothing makes life seem empty like a cow saying ""Moo, nah."""

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日泣いてばかりいるのは虚しい。
example_sentences.english: It's futile to just cry every day.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は何だか虚しい気分です。
example_sentences.english: I feel empty today, for some reason.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日何度も何度も同じことの繰り返しで、虚しくなりませんか。
example_sentences.english: Don't you feel empty doing the same thing every day over and over again?

english: Everyday Life, Normal Life, Daily Life, Ordinary, Regular, Everyday, Usual
notes: "Normal days are what you have in your regular everyday life. This is your normal life." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチの日常の仕事がどんなものなのか知りたいです。
example_sentences.english: I want to know what Koichi's daily work life is like.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の日常はとても平ぼんです。
example_sentences.english: My daily life is very ordinary.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい言語を学ぶ際、まず始めに日常で一般的に使われる実用的な言葉から覚える方が効率的だ。
example_sentences.english: When you learn a new language, it’s more efficient to begin with everyday, practical words at first.

notes: "An illusion that changes your concept of the world is a big fantasy (it's also an illusion). This makes sense, though, right? An illusion is an illusion, sure. But, when it changes your concept of the world, it becomes a total fantasy!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: フグはいくつになっても幻想の世界の住人なんだな。
example_sentences.english: No matter how old Fugu gets, he still lives in a world of illusion.

example_sentences.japanese: 時々、コウイチが自分の息子だというあまい幻想をいだいています。
example_sentences.english: I sometimes cherish the sweet illusion that Koichi is my son.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の兄は、自分が河豚の王だという馬鹿げた幻想を持ち続けている。
example_sentences.english: My older brother maintains the ridiculous fantasy that he is the king of the blowfish.

notes: "When the fee is nothing it is free and without charge!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: コストコで無料のサンプルを食べ歩くのが好きです。
example_sentences.english: I like walking around eating free samples at Costco.

example_sentences.japanese: ワニカニは、レベル四まで無料で利用できます。
example_sentences.english: WaniKani is available for free until level four.

example_sentences.japanese: クリスマス、一人ぼっちで過ごしたくないんだけど、もう予定立てちゃった？もしまだなら、ポール・マッカートニーのチケットが二枚あるんだけど、無料で一枚プレゼントするよ。
example_sentences.english: I don’t want to be alone for Christmas, have you made plans already? If not, I have two Paul McCartney concert tickets and I could give you one for free.

notes:
"When a light shines on how much you've prospered, it's a great honor. You don't feel like you did anything so special, but it's really a privilege for the light to come down on you like this.Don't confuse this with 栄光! With that one, you made things prosper and the light came after, making you look glorious. With this, light is shining on you, and you receive honor from it." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

"Something that is publicly managed is something that is public aka government run. Compare this to 私営 which is private / privately run." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: あべさんにインタビューさせていただけることをとても光栄に思っています。
example_sentences.english: It's truly an honor for us to be able to interview you, Mr. Abe.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチ王と直せつお話ができることは、大変光栄なことなんですよ。
example_sentences.english: You should know that it's indeed a privilege for you to chat with King Koichi in person.

example_sentences.japanese: Tofuguの本社で勤務する機会を頂いたことを、とても光栄に思います。皆さんのお役に立てるよう精一杯頑張りますので、どうぞよろしくお願いいたします。
example_sentences.english: I’m deeply honored to have this opportunity to work at the Tofugu headquarters. I’ll do my best to be of use to you all.

example_sentences.japanese: もし収入がものすごく低いのであれば、安い公営のアパートに住めるかもしれませんよ。
example_sentences.english: If your income is really low, you may be able to live in a cheap public apartment.

notes: "A temporary theory isn't one that's set in stone yet. In fact, it's not really a theory at all, it's more of a hypothesis." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: この土地は、みかんやレモンのようなかんきつるいの果物に向いているんじゃないかという仮説を立てました。
example_sentences.english: I came up with the hypothesis that this soil is very good for citrus fruits like clementines and lemons.

example_sentences.japanese: この仮説の正しさを立証するには、コウイチの力が必要です。
example_sentences.english: We need Koichi's help to prove that this hypothesis is correct.

example_sentences.japanese: 面白いとは思うのですが、もしそれを題材に記事を書きたいのであれば、その仮説を裏付ける資料を見つけてくださいね。
example_sentences.english: I think that’s interesting, but if you want to write an article about that topic you need to find data to prove your hypothesis.

notes: "When you know nothing (Jon Snow), you know nothing. This is ignorance." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 周りの人から、無知なくせに知ったかぶりをするやつだと思われていたらどうしようと心配です。
example_sentences.english: I'm worried people think of me as an ignorant know-it-all.

example_sentences.japanese: 無知が原因で、間ちがいをおかしてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: I made a mistake due to ignorance.

example_sentences.japanese: 無知をさらけ出したからって恥ずかしがることなんか無いよ。あいつらこそ、自分たちの無知を隠していることを恥じるべきさ。
example_sentences.english: You shouldn’t be ashamed of yourself after admitting your ignorance. They should be ashamed of themselves for hiding their own ignorance.

notes: "The inside side is the inside. A little redundant but makes a lot of sense." "The readings are the kun'yomi readings. With 側 you've already learned it. With 内 you'll have to remember the kun'yomi reading of うち. Combine them together and you have うちがわ. Here's a mnemonic to help you remember that pesky うち portion. What is it that's drawn you inside? ""Oo, cheese!"" (うち) Cheese has drawn you inside. You're so excited that you exclaim, ""Oo, cheese!"""

example_sentences.japanese: りそな銀行の内側で待っています。
example_sentences.english: I'll wait for you inside Resona Bank.

example_sentences.japanese: 右の内側のかかとにトゲがささったみたいです。
example_sentences.english: I think I've got a splinter in my inner right heel.

example_sentences.japanese: ゾンビを中に入れないために、金属製のシャッターを下ろして、内側から鍵を掛ける必要があります。
example_sentences.english: We need to lower the metal shutters and lock them from the inside to shut the zombies out.

notes: "The left side is the left side. Simple as that." "The reading for this is vocab kun'yomi readings. Just take the vocab 左 and add it to 側 to have yourself ひだりがわ."

example_sentences.japanese: このエスカレーターでは、みんな左側に立っていますね。
example_sentences.english: Everybody stands on the left side on this escalator I guess.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本は、イギリスと同じで、車は左側通行ですよ。
example_sentences.english: They drive on the left in Japan the same as they do in England.

example_sentences.japanese: 寝る時は、左側を下にして横になる方が好きです。
example_sentences.english: When sleeping, I prefer to lie down on my left side.

notes: "Those love feelings you're having mean you're in love!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の両親は、愛情の深い人たちでした。
example_sentences.english: My parents were deeply affectionate people.

example_sentences.japanese: 愛情の無いけっこんはしたくありません。
example_sentences.english: I don't want to have a loveless marriage.

example_sentences.japanese: 愛情たっぷりのビーフシチューです。
example_sentences.english: It’s beef stew that’s full of love.

notes: "Something that's used for medicine is medicinal." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: にきびが気になるので、薬用の石けんで顔をあらうようにしています。
example_sentences.english: I worry about acne, so I tend to use medicinal soap to wash my face.

example_sentences.japanese: この薬局に、薬用リップクリームはおいていますか？
example_sentences.english: Does this pharmacy have medicinal lip moisturizers?

example_sentences.japanese: 咳がひどいんですが、妊娠中に薬用せき止めドロップを服用しても大丈夫でしょうか？
example_sentences.english: I have a horrible cough, so is it okay for me to take medicated cough drops while I’m pregnant?

notes: "A small theory is some idea you have that you put on paper. Perhaps it's an idea about life, that you write in the form of a novel?" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: この小説マジで大好きだわ。これはホンモノだよ。
example_sentences.english: I seriously love this novel. This is legit.

example_sentences.japanese: お父さん、小説が売れて鼻高々だね。
example_sentences.english: Dad is glowing with pride because his novel is selling well, huh?

example_sentences.japanese: 「ほら、これでなみだと鼻をふきなよ」と言いながら、コウイチは読んでいた小説のページを一枚やぶって、クリステンにわたした。
example_sentences.english: “Here, wipe your tears and nose,” Koichi said, ripping off a page of the novel that he'd been reading and handing it to Kristen.

english: Open Seat, Empty Seat, Free Seat
notes: "A sky seat is a seat full of sky (aka nothing!). This is an empty seat or open seat." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: アメリカでクリスマスに映画を見に行ったら、ほとんど空席でびっくりしました。
example_sentences.english: I went to see a movie on Christmas day in the U.S. and I was surprised to see that the theater was nearly empty.

example_sentences.japanese: 空席の出そうなじゅ業があれば教えてもらえませんか？
example_sentences.english: Could you tell me if there are any lessons with free seats left?

example_sentences.japanese: まだ空席はたくさんありますか？できれば前の方の席がいいのですが。
example_sentences.english: Are there still many open seats left? If possible, I’d prefer to sit in the front.

notes: "A song drama. Ugh, I hate these. They sing so much and they're so dramatic. This is an opera." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: その歌劇の主人公は生粋のフランス人です。
example_sentences.english: This opera's main character is a natural-born Frenchman.

example_sentences.japanese: とある歌劇で、奴隷の役を演じました。
example_sentences.english: I played the role of a slave in an opera.

example_sentences.japanese: 歌劇のチケットの値段を2%値上げします。
example_sentences.english: We are going to increase our opera ticket prices by 2%.

notes: "The original thing you make is the original work. It's always better to have the original, rather than a copy, I think." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: マンガが原作の映画は、原作の良さを失ってしまうことが多いです。
example_sentences.english: Comic book movies often lose the flavor of the original work.

example_sentences.japanese: シェイクスピアを原作で読んだことはありますか？
example_sentences.english: Have you read Shakespeare's original works?

example_sentences.japanese: この漫画は、テレビアニメとドラマの原作です。
example_sentences.english: This manga was made into a TV anime and drama series.

hiragana: そとがわ, がいそく
notes: "The outside side is the outside." "This word uses the kun'yomi readings from the kanji. Since you learned the kun'yomi reading for 外 with the vocabulary, you should be just fine here."

example_sentences.japanese: 外側に開くと思ったら、内側に開くドアだったんだね。
example_sentences.english: I thought this door opened outward, but it actually opens inward, I guess.

example_sentences.japanese: いつもは外側のポケットにかぎを入れておくんですけど...おかしいなぁ。
example_sentences.english: I usually put the key in the outside pocket though....weird.

example_sentences.japanese: サーモンのフライを作ろうとしたんだけど、外側だけ焦げちゃって内側は血生臭いオレンジ色のままになっちゃった。油がちょっと熱すぎたのかも。
example_sentences.english: I tried to deep fry some salmon, but the outside got burnt and the inside stayed bloody and orange. I guess the oil might have been too hot.

notes: "They warn you and they guess when you've done something wrong (with evidence, of course!). They are the police." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 警察しょに入ると、梅酒のにおいが鼻をついた。
example_sentences.english: The smell of umeshu hit my nose as I entered the police station.

example_sentences.japanese: その警察は、ビエトの警告をあざ笑ったため、後からひどい目にあいました。
example_sentences.english: That police officer sneered at Viet's warning, so he later found himself in a miserable situation.

example_sentences.japanese: 警察署での出会いから一時間後、その警察官と泥棒はすっかり意気投合した。
example_sentences.english: One hour after meeting at the police station, the police officer and the robber had completely hit it off.

notes: "When your power is nothing you are powerless." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. You also can know that 力 uses its りょく reading because when you tried to pick up a tiny rock (りょく) you couldn't, because you were powerless."

example_sentences.japanese: 自分がどれだけちっぽけで無力な存ざいであるかを思い知らされました。
example_sentences.english: That made me realize how tiny and powerless I am.

example_sentences.japanese: 「無力の証明」というゆうぎ王カードを手に入れました。
example_sentences.english: "I got a Yu-Gi-Oh! trading card called ""Proof of Powerlessness."""

example_sentences.japanese: 警察はそのストーカーに対して無力で何をすることもできず、結局彼女は殺されてしまった。
example_sentences.english: The police were powerless to do anything about the stalker and in the end she was killed.

notes: "The right side is the right side." "The reading is all kun'yomi vocab reading. You should know the reading of the vocab word 右 by now. Also, the 側 reading happens to be the reading you learned with the kanji as well as with the word 側."

example_sentences.japanese: 日本の自動車のハンドルは通常右側にあります。
example_sentences.english: The steering wheels of Japanese cars are usually on the right side.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチのつくえの右側の引き出しには、塩がたくさん入っています。
example_sentences.english: There's a lot of salt in the right-hand drawer of Koichi's desk.

example_sentences.japanese: 心霊写真を撮っちゃったの。ほら。この写真の右側に、その場にはいなかった幼い女の子が写ってるのよ。分かる？
example_sentences.english: We took a picture of a ghost. Look. There is a little girl who wasn’t there on the right in the picture. Can you see her?

notes: "The actions around here are nothing. Absolutely nothing is going on. If nothing is going on, that means it is safe and sound for you." "One thing that's not safe and sound is the reading of the 無 in this word. Instead of む it's ぶ. Why? Because you thought it was safe and sound, but you were fooled. There are ghosts everywhere, all jumping out and screaming Boo! (ぶ) at you. Feel the surprise. You thought it was safe and sound!"

example_sentences.japanese: みなさんの無事をおいのりしています。
example_sentences.english: We are praying for the safety of you all.

example_sentences.japanese: 両親は、たいしょくして、平おん無事な生活を送っています。
example_sentences.english: My parents retired and live their lives safely and peacefully.

example_sentences.japanese: 本当に赤ん坊は私達の言葉が分からないと言い切れるんですか？もし私の双子ちゃんが、「お医者さんが今ママに、僕達がママの子宮から無事に出られるかどうかは、五分五分だって言ったみたいだね。」なんて話をしてたらどうするんですか？ああ、私の赤ちゃん、きっと先生の言葉に震え上がってるに違いないわ。
example_sentences.english: "Are you sure the baby doesn’t understand our language? What if my twins are talking right now like, ""The doctor told our mom that it’ll be a toss-up whether we would come out safe and sound from her uterus."" Aww... Doctor, they must have been frightened by what you said."

english: Salty Taste, Tastes Salty, Salty, Salty Flavor
notes: "The taste of salt is a salty taste (it's also when something tastes salty)." "The readings are the kun'yomi vocab readings. So, take the readings of 塩 (you learned the reading with the kanji) and 味 and you have yourself しおあじ."

example_sentences.japanese: もっと塩味を利かせてもよかったかもね。
example_sentences.english: Maybe I could've used more salt.

example_sentences.japanese: うす塩味のポテトチップスは、あまり人気がありません。
example_sentences.english: Lightly-salted potato chips aren't that popular.

example_sentences.japanese: 「ねぇねぇ！コウイチに塩味のジェロを作ってあげたら、テキストフグのアカウントが無料でもらえるって聞いたんだけど。」「信じないほうがいいよ。それって嘘だと思うよ。」
example_sentences.english: """Hey! I heard that if I make salty jello for Koichi, I’ll get a free TextFugu account."" ""It’s better if you don’t believe that. I think it’s a lie!"""

notes: "People who study about medicine are studying the study of pharmacy." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: どうしてコウイチは最近薬学の本をデスクにおいているの？
example_sentences.english: Why has Koichi been keeping that pharmacology book on his desk lately?

example_sentences.japanese: かれは、東京大学の薬学部の学生です。
example_sentences.english: He is a student of the pharmacy department at the University of Tokyo.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチが、薬学者の募集を検討しているって、本当ですか？
example_sentences.english: Is that true that Koichi is thinking of hiring a pharmacologist?

notes: "A drama location is where people do drama. This is a theater." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 劇場のロビーで待ち合わせしましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let's meet up in the theater's lobby.

example_sentences.japanese: それでは劇場のトイレで会いましょう。
example_sentences.english: I’ll see you at a bathroom in the theater then.

example_sentences.japanese: 劇場までの毎日の通勤に、片道二時間以上かかります。
example_sentences.english: My daily commute to the theater is over two hours each way.

notes: "A sad drama always ends in tragedy. That's what makes it sad." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: それが悲劇の始まりだった。
example_sentences.english: It was the beginning of my tragedy.

example_sentences.japanese: あんた、悲劇の主人公にでもなったつもり？いつまでもクヨクヨしてたって仕方ないでしょ？
example_sentences.english: Are you trying to act like the hero of some tragedy? Moping forever won't help anyone.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたには悲劇がお似合いよ。
example_sentences.english: Tragedy is suits you.

notes: "Something is not detailed at all. I don't know anything about it. No details whatsoever. It's a totally unknown entity." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日、年れい不詳な美人女性に出会ったんだ。
example_sentences.english: Yesterday, I met a beautiful woman of unknown age.

example_sentences.japanese: ワニカニは、性別不詳のモンスターです。
example_sentences.english: Wanikani is a monster whose sex is unknown.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼ってほんと職業不詳だよね。
example_sentences.english: His real job is unknown, isn’t it?

notes: "You have yourself a void of weakness. This means you are weak and feeble." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 虚弱な子どもを見ると、心配になります。
example_sentences.english: Whenever I see a weak child, I get worried.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はいちょうが虚弱なんです。
example_sentences.english: I have a weak stomach.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の息子は生まれつき虚弱体質で、運動はできません。
example_sentences.english: My son was born with a weak constitution, so he can’t exercise.

notes: "The West side of something is known as the West side. Sorry, I have no story to go along with your West side." "The readings are the kun'yomi vocab readings. You should know both of them, with 西 being にし and 側 being がわ (what you learned with the kanji)."

example_sentences.japanese: この町の西側のゆう便局で働いています。
example_sentences.english: I'm working at the post office on the west side of this town.

example_sentences.japanese: 西側しょ国とみなされるのはどの国ですか。
example_sentences.english: Which countries are considered Western countries?

example_sentences.japanese: 今年の二月三日に巻き寿司を食べるなら、西側を向いて食べなくてはいけませんよ。
example_sentences.english: If you eat makizushi on Feb 3rd of this year, you have to face the west bank.

notes: "If your brain is dead you have brain death." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 母が脳死じょうたいになった時、父は「何が起きるか分からない、それが人生だ」と自分に言い聞かせるように言いました。
example_sentences.english: "When my mom went brain dead, my dad said, ""You never know what will happen next—that's life,"" as if he was trying to tell himself."
