example_sentences.japanese: 脳内出血は、脳卒中につながり、最悪脳死を引き起こす可能性があります。
example_sentences.english: Brain hemorrhaging may lead to stroke and, finally, brain death.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨年イギリスで、脳死と判定された人のうち2~3人の人が息を吹き返し、さらに昏睡状態の間の会話を一部覚えていたという。
example_sentences.english: I heard a few people who were considered brain dead came back to life in the UK last year and they remembered parts of conversations from when they were unconscious.

notes: "A place that is peace and quiet is a very calm and serene place. Ahh, so nice!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 人類は自らぜつめつをまねくかもしれないと聞いて、平静ではいられなかった。
example_sentences.english: After I heard that the human race may cause its own extinction, I couldn't stay calm.

example_sentences.japanese: 今は自分でもびっくりするぐらい、平静な気持ちなんです。
example_sentences.english: I'm kinda surprised myself, but I actually feel amazingly serene now.

example_sentences.japanese: 便秘の時には、心の平静を失いやすくなる。
example_sentences.english: I easily lose my calm when I’m constipated.

notes: "Remember how 下品 is ""crude"" and ""vulgar"" - this is obviously the opposite. This is elegant." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 母は時々上品な仕草を見せる時があります。
example_sentences.english: Sometimes my mom reveals her elegant mannerisms.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の友達はミセスコンテストで上品な言葉づかいでスピーチした。
example_sentences.english: My friend gave a speech using elegant language at a Mrs. contest.

example_sentences.japanese: カナエはいつも上品にナイフとフォークを使うように両親からキツく言われている。
example_sentences.english: Kanae’s parents have always been very strict in telling her to use a knife and fork elegantly.

notes: "This is a single kanji with an い on the end, meaning you know it's probably an adjective. What's the adjective form of equal? It's equal (and also similar or equivalent). That ""similar"" one is a bit weird, because ""similar"" is not equal, though I'd lean more towards equal." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: What should be equal above all things? I think each person (ひと) should be equal!"

example_sentences.japanese: そんなに平等にこだわるなら、全社員の仕事りょうを等しくするべきです。
example_sentences.english: If you really care about equality, you should make all the workers' workloads equal.

example_sentences.japanese: 左の金玉と右の金玉の重さって等しいと思いますか？
example_sentences.english: Do you think the left and right balls are equal in weight?

example_sentences.japanese: オタクだけではなく他の人にとっても、ネット上で大文字を使うことは大声を出すことに等しいですよ。
example_sentences.english: Even for people who aren’t nerds, using uppercase letters on the internet is equivalent to shouting.

notes: "It doesn't matter what you say versus equal rights. If you really want things to be equal, you have to support equality." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは、社員達を対等の人間としてあつかってくれます。
example_sentences.english: Koichi treat workers as his equals.

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトは、コウイチと対等な共同けいえい者だと思っていました。
example_sentences.english: I thought Viet was a fifty-fifty partner with Koichi.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたとは対等に話をすることができません。
example_sentences.english: I can’t talk to you like an equal.

english: Far Away, Distant, At A Distance, Distant Place, By Far
notes: "This is the noun/no-adjective version of the kanji far, so it means far away or distant." "This uses the kun'yomi reading which you learned with 遠い. How convenient!"

example_sentences.japanese: 今はめがねをかけてないので、遠くの物がよく見えません。
example_sentences.english: I'm not wearing glasses right now, so I can't see far away objects very well.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は、家族から、遠くはなれて住んでいます。
example_sentences.english: I live far away from my family.

example_sentences.japanese: 遠くの方で銃声が響いた。
example_sentences.english: A gunshot went off in a far off direction.

english: First Class, First Rank, The Best
notes: "When you're equal to one you are the very top. You are first class and first rank. In fact, you are the best." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. いち gets shortened to いっ though, so watch out for that if you want to remain the best, yeah?"

example_sentences.japanese: 一等車に乗ってるとは、さすがコウイチだね。
example_sentences.english: You are in the first-class carriage, yeah? That's so like you, Koichi!

example_sentences.japanese: 銀座の一等地にオフィスをかまえるなんて、よっぽどもうけてるんだなぁ。
example_sentences.english: They must be making a ton of money if they have an office at the best location in Ginza.

example_sentences.japanese: このベーコンのキーホルダーは、私がベーコンのコスプレ大会で一等賞を取った時にもらったんです。
example_sentences.english: I won this bacon keychain when I took first prize in the bacon costume competition.

notes: "When you are higher than equal, you are above the very top, you are above everyone. You are high class." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: ずい分高等な技術を持っているんだね。
example_sentences.english: You have an extraordinarily high class technique like that, huh?

example_sentences.japanese: うちの息子はまだ小学生ですが、じゅくではすでに高等の数学を勉強しています。
example_sentences.english: My son is still an elementary school kid, but he is studying high grade mathematics at a cram school.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたの国の高等教育について教えて下さい。
example_sentences.english: Please tell me about higher education in your country.

notes: "It's not possible to lack. It is  indispensable and essential, so don't lack it!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ビーチに行く時は、日焼け止めが不可欠です。
example_sentences.english: When I go to the beach, sunscreen is essential.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語がペラペラになるのに不可欠なことは何だと思いますか？
example_sentences.english: What do you think would be essential to becoming fluent in Japanese?

example_sentences.japanese: 美味しいベーコンは、サクサク仕事を進めるのに不可欠です。
example_sentences.english: Tasty bacon is indispensable in promoting efficient work.

notes: "When something is not equal it suffers from inequality." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは、トーフグの利えきを不等に分配するのがいやなんだよ。
example_sentences.english: Koichi doesn't want to distribute Tofugu's profits unevenly.

example_sentences.japanese: 不等辺三角形の面せきを求める公式を知っていますか？
example_sentences.english: Do you know the formula to find the area of a scalene triangle?

example_sentences.japanese: 私は連立不等式が得意です。
example_sentences.english: I’m pretty good at simultaneous inequalities.

notes: "The ability is there, so it is possible... wait, there's enough ability to make this possible? Let's do it!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 今年の春から、むすめを保育園にあずけることが可能だと聞いて、胸のつかえが下りました。
example_sentences.english: Hearing that it would be possible for me to put my daughter in daycare this spring lifted a huge weight off my shoulders.

example_sentences.japanese: もう少し実げん可能なかい決さくをていあんしてください。
example_sentences.english: Please present a few more possible solutions.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は年間一億ドルを稼ぐことは実現可能だと思います。
example_sentences.english: I’d say earning a hundred million dollars a year is possible.

notes: "This is the な adjective form of quiet, which is kind of just like the noun, anyways. What is the adjective version of quiet? It's also quiet." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: You need to be quiet. She's (しず) being nice and quiet, unlike you!"

example_sentences.japanese: 静かな通りにある家の方がいいです。
example_sentences.english: We'd prefer a house on a quiet street.

example_sentences.japanese: 下りなのは分かりますが、もう少し静かにしていただけますか？
example_sentences.english: I know you have diarrhea, but could you keep it down a bit more, please?

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチとビエトが乗り込むと、そのタクシーは静かに動き出した。
example_sentences.english: When Koichi and Viet got in, the taxi quietly started to move.

notes: "A kind or type of person is when you categorize a person into different types. How do we do that? Well, you categorize by race of people (or more simply by race)." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: この町には、色々な人種の人がいます。
example_sentences.english: There's a wide variety of different races in this city.

example_sentences.japanese: 人種をネタにしたじょうだんは、あんまり好きじゃありません。
example_sentences.english: I don't really like racial jokes.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕のお父さんは人種差別主義者のくせに、僕には人種で人を判断してはいけないって言うんだ。
example_sentences.english: My father is a racist and yet he tells me that it’s wrong to judge people based on their race.

notes: "These people are kind of like a type of parents. Not quite parents, but kind of, in a pinch anyways. These are your relatives." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: まずは年配の親類に相談してみます。
example_sentences.english: I'll start by consulting elderly relatives.

example_sentences.japanese: 実は、コウイチとオバマ大とうりょうは遠い親類なんですよ。
example_sentences.english: Actually, President Obama is a distant relative of Koichi.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は全親類と縁を切った孤独な男だ。
example_sentences.english: He’s a really isolated guy who cut off all contact with his relatives.

notes: "A sit seat is probably going to be a seat." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: この座席のクッション、めっちゃいい感じ。
example_sentences.english: This seat's cushion is really comfy.

example_sentences.japanese: 座席の予約が必要だったとは、知りませんでした。
example_sentences.english: I didn't know that I had to make reservations for seats.

example_sentences.japanese: 車内で、サーモンが座席から身を乗り出してフグにキスをした瞬間、信号が青に変わった。
example_sentences.english: The moment Salmon leaned across the seat to kiss Fugu in the car, the traffic light turned green.

notes: "When you are able to acquire whatever you want, you start to see the benefits of everything around you and begin to profit from them. Aren't you so amazing?" "The reading for this is the same as with the kanji you learned. とく!"

example_sentences.japanese: お得なクーポン冊子はいかがですか？
example_sentences.english: Would you like a booklet of bargain coupons?

example_sentences.japanese: そんな事して、一体何の得があるっていうの？
example_sentences.english: What's there to gain from doing something like that?

example_sentences.japanese: ルックスがいい人は絶対に得だと思います。
example_sentences.english: I believe that having good looks is absolutely an advantage.

notes: "If you've had many busy days, then you're even more busy than you thought!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近多忙でつかれていて、よく舌がもつれるんです。
example_sentences.english: I've been tired because of how busy I've been lately, and it's been making me tongue tied.

example_sentences.japanese: 多忙な生活を送っています。
example_sentences.english: I lead a busy life.

example_sentences.japanese: ご多忙な所申し訳無いんですが、少しの間代わりに列の順番を取っておいてもらえませんか？
example_sentences.english: I know how busy you are, and I feel terrible asking this, but would you mind saving my place in line for a few minutes?

notes: "You put years in order of the period they come in and you're really putting them in chronological order." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: マイケルが、ビエトとヤクザの関係について、年代順に細かく説明してくれました。
example_sentences.english: Michael gave me a detailed explanation about the relationship between Viet and the yakuza in chronological order.

example_sentences.japanese: 記事の年代順リストとかってやっぱり作った方がいいのかな？
example_sentences.english: Should we make a list of our articles in chronological order?

example_sentences.japanese: 年代順の詳細な経過については、こちらの年表をご参照ください。
example_sentences.english: See this timetable for the detailed chronological accounts, please.

notes: "You have two flat objects that make up your tongue. What kind of tongue is made up of two of anything? That's a tongue that's split, that's a forked tongue." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Just remember that 舌 is read here as じた, and not した."

example_sentences.japanese: 政治家達の二枚舌の政さくにはもううんざりだよ。
example_sentences.english: I'm totally fed up with politicians' duplicitous policies.

example_sentences.japanese: あいつは二枚舌だから気をつけた方がいいよ。
example_sentences.english: He has a forked tongue, so you should be careful.

example_sentences.japanese: ○×クイズ: ビエトは等身大の初音ミク人形を買うお金を儲けるために、二枚舌を使ってコウイチを騙しました。○か×か？
example_sentences.english: True or False Quiz: In order to get the money for a life-sized Hatsune Miku doll, Viet used his forked tongue to cheat Koichi. True or false?

notes: "The continuation of history is history itself. This is the main word for ""history"" and you'll see it a lot if you're in school or something." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 歴史を勉強しておくと、しょう来得をするよ。
example_sentences.english: You'll benefit from studying history in the future.

example_sentences.japanese: そのころは、高校の歴史の先生になりたいと思っていたんです。
example_sentences.english: Around that time, I wanted to be a high school history teacher.

example_sentences.japanese: Tofuguの歴史について簡単に説明させてください。
example_sentences.english: Let me give you a brief explanation of Tofugu’s history.

notes: "You add and you subtract. This brings you back to zero. There was absolutely no point in doing those actions. Completely pointless. In fact, I'd say that was downright irresponsible of you. The extra いい is there to mean ""good,"" as in ""good, you've figured out how pointless that was, now stop.""" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: このサービスはいい加減すぎます。いい加減、改善をするべきですよ。
example_sentences.english: This service is clunky. It's about time for some improvements.

example_sentences.japanese: あんないい加減な人とけっこんして二十年もけっこん生活が続けられるなんて信じられない。
example_sentences.english: How have you stayed married to such an irresponsible man for twenty years? I can't believe it.

example_sentences.japanese: ねえ、お父さん。お母さんさぁ、近所の井戸端会議で仕入れたいい加減な情報に踊らされるの、いい加減に止めるべきだと思わない？
example_sentences.english: Hey, Dad. Don’t you think it’s time for mom to stop being manipulated by pointless gossip from idly chatting with the neighbors?

english: Nuclear Power, Nuclear Energy, Atomic Power, Atomic Energy
notes: "The power of the atom (原子) is nuclear power." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 今は原子力の是非について話をしているんだ。関係無い話を持ち出して頭を混乱させないでくれ。
example_sentences.english: We are talking about whether nuclear power is good or not right now. Don't try to confuse us with irrelevant facts.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の父は、以前は原子力発電所で仕事をしていました。
example_sentences.english: My dad used to work at a nuclear power plant.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチはゴジラと戦うために、原子力で稼働するTofuguロボットを作った。
example_sentences.english: Koichi made a nuclear-powered Tofugu robot to fight Godzilla.

notes: "A wealth clan is a group of people who do whatever they can to get their money. These are the plutocrats of the world, but you can also call them financial clique or even the Zaibatsu (sometimes brought up in English language history / economic books regarding Japan)." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はこの財閥のあと取りです。
example_sentences.english: He is the heir of this zaibatsu.

example_sentences.japanese: おそかれ早かれ、Tofuguは財閥として日本のビジネス界に君りんするでしょう。
example_sentences.english: Tofugu will reign over the business world in Japan as a zaibatsu sooner or later.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本には、第二次世界大戦前に三井財閥、三菱財閥、住友財閥、安田財閥などの財閥がありました。
example_sentences.english: In Japan, there were several financial cliques prior to World War II, including Mitsui Zaibatsu, Mitsubishi Zaibatsu, Sumitomo Zaibatsu and Yasuda Zaibatsu.

notes: "You know how 警察 is ""police""? Well, this is kind of like that. This time you have someone from the government trying to warn you about the bad things you do. This person, like 警察 is a police officer." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: その警官の名前は、舌をかみそうな名前だった。
example_sentences.english: That police officer's name was like a tongue twister.

example_sentences.japanese: 警官は、いい加減な返事をして言いのがれました。
example_sentences.english: The cop put me off with his vague answer.

example_sentences.japanese: 「昨夜、フグと別れたの。」「サーモン、何があったの？」「フグが、私が警官だってことを知って、それで、もう私とは会わないって言われたの。」「そんなに簡単に？」「ええ。あっけないものね。」
example_sentences.english: """I broke up with Fugu last night."" ""What happened, Salmon?"" ""Well, He found out that I’m a police officer and said he wouldn’t see me any more."" ""Just like that?"" ""Yeah. Just like that."""

notes: "The seasons season is the season. Who likes winter? It's my favorite 季節." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: このマーケットには、季節の野さいがたくさん売っています。
example_sentences.english: A lot of seasonal vegetables are sold in this market.

example_sentences.japanese: その服そうは、ちょっと季節外れじゃない？
example_sentences.english: Aren't your clothes a little out of season?

example_sentences.japanese: 心配しないで。季節の変わり目に風邪をひくのは、私の習慣のようなものなの。
example_sentences.english: Don’t worry. Catching a cold when the seasons change is kind of a habit of mine.

notes: "One who is junior in life is a student or pupil. It's kind of like how a 先生 is someone who came previous to you in life. Cool how that works, right? Okay 生徒, get back to work!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: その生徒は、先生に向かって舌打ちをしました。
example_sentences.english: That pupil tsk tsked the teacher.

example_sentences.japanese: 高校までは生徒のことを「生徒」とよぶけど、大学では学生のことを「生徒」とはよばないよ。
example_sentences.english: "We call students ""pupil"" up through high school, but we don't call university students ""pupils."""

example_sentences.japanese: 私の趣味は、教師と生徒の禁断の愛をテーマにした本を読むことです。
example_sentences.english: My hobby is reading books about the forbidden love between students and their teachers.

notes: "Know how 意識 is ""consciousness""? What about when this consciousness doesn't exist (aka it is nothing)? That's when it becomes unconsciousness." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. It will help to know how to read 意識, though."

example_sentences.japanese: 無意識のうちに、舌で虫歯の穴をさわってしまいます。
example_sentences.english: I can't help but unconsciously tongue the cavity in my tooth with the tip of my tongue.

example_sentences.japanese: その無意識につめをかむくせは直した方がいいよ。
example_sentences.english: That involuntary habit of biting your nails should be fixed.

example_sentences.japanese: 我々は素晴らしい。何故なら、無意識にクリエイティブになることができるからだ。
example_sentences.english: We’re awesome because we can be unconsciously creative.

notes: "A part of speech that represents moving is a part of speech that describes actions. That is a verb." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 英語は「主語ー動詞ー目的語」の言語です。
example_sentences.english: "English is a ""subject-verb-object"" language."

example_sentences.japanese: あなたの日本語で一番お気に入りの動詞は何？
example_sentences.english: What is your favorite verb in Japanese?

example_sentences.japanese: もし自分を表現するために動詞を一つだけ選ばなくてはいけないとしたら、どの動詞を選びますか？
example_sentences.english: If you had to choose one verb to describe yourself, which verb would it be?

notes: "A young someone is a young person." "The reading for this one is a pain. 若 is the same as what you learned with the kanji (わか), but 者 is もの, which isn't what you learned. Think of this: A young person does what they want. They don't follow tradition or do anything the way you'd want them to, just like the reading of this word. Also, their actions make you really want to moan (もの) because ugh, young people. Get off my lawn."

example_sentences.japanese: その若者は、公園でセミを細かくかんさつしていました。
example_sentences.english: That young person was observing cicadas very closely in the park.

example_sentences.japanese: この件には、あの若者の金が絡んでいるらしいよ。
example_sentences.english: Apparently that young person's money is involved in this matter.

example_sentences.japanese: この若者はすごいよ。大物になる前にサインをもらっておいた方がいいよ。
example_sentences.english: This young man is terrific. You should get his autograph before he becomes a big-shot.

notes: "A young young thing has youthfulness on their side. Oh to be youthful again!" The reading is the reading you learned with the kanji. Same goes for the repeater kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチっていつまでたっても若々しいよね。
example_sentences.english: Koichi's really had his youthful appearance forever.

example_sentences.japanese: そのファッション、ちょっと若々しすぎない？
example_sentences.english: Don't you think that type of fashion is a bit too young looking for you?

example_sentences.japanese: 私の祖母は九十代ですが、六十代の人よりも若く見えます。若さの秘訣は、若々しい気持ちでいることと、よく噛むことだそうです。
example_sentences.english: My Grandmother is in her nineties and she looks younger than some people in their sixties. She says that feeling young and chewing foods a lot are two big secrets to her youth.

notes: "It is correct and you're certain of it. When you've done this much checking and you're this sure, your measurements must be very accurate and precise." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチはワニカニの正確なユーザー数を知りません。
example_sentences.english: Koichi doesn't know the accurate number of WaniKani users.

example_sentences.japanese: マイケルはコウイチのランチリクエストを正確に記おくし、注文するというにんむを終えました。
example_sentences.english: Michael completed his mission to memorize Koichi's lunch request perfectly and order it.

example_sentences.japanese: 君って、ああ言えばこう言うし、しかも言うことがどれもいちいち正確なのが結構頭にくるんだけど。
example_sentences.english: Actually, I’m pretty annoyed at how you have a comeback for everything and how what you say is so accurate.

notes: "Even in the middle of your dream you're thinking about your body pillows. You're crazy about them, wrapped in absorption." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 穴をつくろうのに夢中な母のすがたを見て、うれしくなりました。
example_sentences.english: I was happy to see my mom so absorbed in patching holes.

example_sentences.japanese: 皿洗いの男に夢中のウェイトレスのことを好きになってしまったんだ。
example_sentences.english: I fell in love with a waitress who is mad about a dishwasher.

example_sentences.japanese: 「サーモン。あのさ、多分知らなかっただろうけど、高校生の頃、き、きみに夢中だったんだ。」「知ってたわよ。フグ。」
example_sentences.english: """Salmon, well, you probably don't know this, but back in high school, I was, um, crazy about you."" ""I knew, Fugu."""

notes: "You have crime and you have guilt. Sounds like you did the crime." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 犯罪にまきこまれて命を落としそうになりましたが、危機一ぱつの所で助かりました。
example_sentences.english: I was involved in a crime and almost got killed, but I was able to escape death by the skin of my teeth.

example_sentences.japanese: 通報を受けて、警察は犯罪の現場に飛んで行った。
example_sentences.english: The police raced to the crime scene after the phone call.

example_sentences.japanese: ああいう子供がそのまま大きくなるから、若者の犯罪が増えるんだよ。そう思わない？
example_sentences.english: The reason crime among youths is increasing is because kids like that get bigger but they don’t change. Don’t you think?

notes: "A dangerous machine is walking through your town, destroying everything. This is a huge crisis!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: できるだけ早い危機のこく服を期待しています。
example_sentences.english: I'm hoping they'll overcome this crisis soon.

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグは今、危機的じょうきょうにあります。
example_sentences.english: Tofugu is currently in a critical situation.

example_sentences.japanese: 2008年の世界的な金融危機では、Tofuguも経営難に陥ったのですか？
example_sentences.english: Did Tofugu run into trouble during the global financial crisis of 2008?

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "The reading for this word is pretty weird. It's different than the 嫌い word you will see in this level too. It is いや, so when you think of something you dislike, just think ""iyah, I dislike it."" Also, think about that eww feeling it gives you when you think of the thing you dislike most."

example_sentences.japanese: 嫌な仕事を嫌々するのは体に良くないよ。
example_sentences.english: Reluctantly doing a job you don't like isn't good for your health.

example_sentences.japanese: 嫌嫌嫌嫌嫌！無理無理無理無理無理！クモがいる！気持ち悪い！
example_sentences.english: Ewwwwwww!!!! Nooooooo!!!! There is a spider! Gross!

example_sentences.japanese: 「これ以上は安くできないよ。嫌ならやめて帰ってくれ。」 「分かったよ。買うことにするよ。」
example_sentences.english: """That’s my final offer. If you don’t like it stop coming back."" ""Alright, alright. I’ll take it."""

english: Do Not Enter, No Entry, Entry Prohibited, No Trespassing, Trespassing Prohibited
notes: "Standing and entering are both prohibited (禁止). If you see this sign, it's essentially saying do not enter or no entry." "The reading for this one is weird. 立 is たち and 入 is いり. It's like you're taking the words 立つ and 入れる and stuffing their hiragana parts back into the kanji (and changing it to いり in the case of 入れる). So, that's something you'll want to try to remember. 禁止 is normal, though, so at least you have that."

example_sentences.japanese: このドアには、関係者以外立入禁止って書かれているよ。
example_sentences.english: This door says Authorized Personnel Only.

example_sentences.japanese: スーパーのバックヤードは、たいていじゅう業員以外立入禁止です。
example_sentences.english: The backrooms of grocery stores are usually for staff only.

example_sentences.japanese: それは大胆だね！君が本当に立入禁止って書いてる場所に入ってションベンしたなんて信じられないよ！
example_sentences.english: "That is wild! I can’t believe you went into a place marked ""Do Not Enter"" and then peed in there!"

notes: "When you can exist all by yourself, then you can do things freely as you please." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは、自由自在な発想でいつもみんなをおどろかせてくれます。
example_sentences.english: Koichi always surprises people with his very flexible ideas.

example_sentences.japanese: しんしゅく自在の犬用リードを探しています。
example_sentences.english: I'm looking for an adjustable leash for dogs.

example_sentences.japanese: あの男は、他人の心を自在に操れる。
example_sentences.english: That man can manipulate minds at will.

notes: "Someone who have (has) guilt is someone who is guilty." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 犯人には、有罪かつ死けいのはん決が下りました。
example_sentences.english: The criminal was found guilty and sentenced to death.

example_sentences.japanese: 有罪の五名のうち二名は大しん院に上告した。
example_sentences.english: Two of the five guilty people appealed to the Supreme Court.

example_sentences.japanese: 飲酒運転で有罪になるのはご免なので、運転はできません。
example_sentences.english: I can’t drive because then I’d be guilty of drunk driving.

notes: "You're distressed and it's difficult. This is quite the hardship you're feeling." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: フグがちょうぼにあけた大穴を今年度中に埋めるのは困難でしょう。
example_sentences.english: It'll be hard to make up for the big losses Fugu made by the end of the year.

example_sentences.japanese: 困難な仕事に直面すると、ワクワクするんです。
example_sentences.english: When I face a hard task, I get excited.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の祖母は歩くのが困難なので、今日は買い物に行くのを手伝ってあげないといけません。
example_sentences.english: My grandmother has difficulty walking, so I have to help her go shopping today.

notes: "Psh, that guy's damage is nothing. He's what I'd call ""mostly harmless.""" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: マグニチュード6.2の地震がありましたが、無害でした。
example_sentences.english: There was an earthquake with a magnitude 6.2, but it was harmless.

example_sentences.japanese: 無害のツイートにまでいちいちつっかかってるやつ、なんなの？
example_sentences.english: What's with people who troll even harmless tweets?

example_sentences.japanese: 心配しなくていいよ。Tofuguに毒は無いから。彼は無害な河豚だよ。
example_sentences.english: Don’t worry. Tofugu doesn’t have any poison. He’s a harmless blowfish.

notes: "If something is not divisible (可分), then it is indivisible." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Will also help to know how to read the word 可分."

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトとコウイチは、不可分の関係にあるんですよ。
example_sentences.english: Viet and Koichi are inseparable from each other.

example_sentences.japanese: けい約では、それは不可分なさいむだったはずですよ。
example_sentences.english: I'm pretty sure it is an indivisible obligation on the contract.

example_sentences.japanese: ご存知のように、豆腐と河豚は不可分です。
example_sentences.english: As we all know, Tofu and Fugu are inseparable.

notes: "When you exist outside (outside of what? Japan, of course), you are overseas or abroad." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 在外し産はどのようにかん理していますか？
example_sentences.english: How do you manage your overseas assets?

example_sentences.japanese: 在外ほう人の安ぴはげん在確にん中です。
example_sentences.english: We are currently checking on the safety of Japanese residents abroad.

example_sentences.japanese: 在外投票をする前に、申し込み用紙を日本大使館か日本領事館に提出する必要があります。
example_sentences.english: Before casting an overseas ballot, you have to submit an application to the Japanese embassy or the Japanese consulate.

notes: "In terms of an individual person... well, that's personal, and depends on the individual. Whatever it is, an individual person has personal tastes, so make sure to think of that." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 私個人の意見ですが、ビエトにはいいおよめさんが見つかってほしいです。
example_sentences.english: This is my personal opinion, but I hope Viet finds a good wife.

example_sentences.japanese: アメリカ人の国民性なのか個人の問題なのかは分からないけど、コウイチはビールが大好きだよね。
example_sentences.english: I don't know if it's because he's American, or if it's just him, but Koichi really loves beer, right?

example_sentences.japanese: 個人主義と自分勝手の違いがよく分かりません。
example_sentences.english: I don’t really see the difference between being an individualist and simply being selfish.

notes:
"Public damage is something that affects everyone, the whole public. What is in the air and gets into everything no matter where you are? How about pollution?" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

"Suburbs on the outside of town are still suburbs. They're sometimes called the outskirts of town too." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本では1950~1960年代にかけて、公害が大きな社会問題になりました。
example_sentences.english: In Japan, pollution became a huge societal problem between 1950 and 1960.

example_sentences.japanese: 私達はみんな、公害の加害者ですよ。
example_sentences.english: We are all responsible for the pollution problems.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の息子は、公害による呼吸器疾患に苦しんでいます。
example_sentences.english: My son is suffering from a pollution-triggered respiratory illness.

example_sentences.japanese: 都心と郊外、どちらに住みたいですか。
example_sentences.english: Would you rather live in the city center or the suburbs?

notes: "One husband, many wives. Sounds a bit sketchy. This is polygamy." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Just note that the 一 gets changed to いっ and the 夫 gets changed to ぷ from ふう for some reason. You can imagine that this is because when you are the type that has many wives, you're probably the type who makes them clean up your poo for you as well."

example_sentences.japanese: 日本もかつては一夫多妻がみとめられていました。
example_sentences.english: Japan used to approve of polygamy too.

example_sentences.japanese: 「一夫多妻せいとか、ありえないよな」とビエトが非難するように言うと、「その非難、自分に向けた方がいいんじゃねぇか？」とコウイチが笑って言い返した。
example_sentences.english: """I can't believe polygamy exists,"" Viet said accusingly. ""You can turn that finger around,” Koichi retorted with a smile."

example_sentences.japanese: 全ての男性が一夫多妻制を支持する訳じゃない。
example_sentences.english: It’s not like all men support polygamy.

notes: "The remaining surplus is the remainder or residual left over." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 今月のさがく残余がくは現時点でいくらになっていますか？
example_sentences.english: What's this month's remainder as of now?

example_sentences.japanese: 残余のねん料では、地球まで引き返すことは難しいだろう。
example_sentences.english: It would be difficult to return to Earth with the remaining fuel.

example_sentences.japanese: 「残余リスクについてもちゃんと議論したんですか？」「まだです。みんな残余リスクの計算式を忘れてしまって、議論にならないんです。」
example_sentences.english: """Have you guys discussed the residual risks, too?"" ""Not yet. We all forgot the formula to calculate residual risk, so we can't have the discussion."""

notes: "If you have guilt then you have committed a sin or crime. Come here and confess to Father Koichi." "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it should use the kun'yomi reading. When learning the kanji, you didn't learn that reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you with this word: When you come to confess your sin to me, you start claiming it wasn't you. You say it was some other version of you! What? How could this be? Well, you say ""there are two mes (つみ) out there!"" One is doing the bad stuff, and the other is you, and you haven't done any sins!"

example_sentences.japanese: マミがコウイチのベーコンを食べた罪は思っている以上に重い。
example_sentences.english: Mami's crime of eating Koichi's bacon is more serious than she thinks.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の会社の社長は会計さぎの罪で有罪になった。
example_sentences.english: My company president has been found guilty of accounting fraud crimes.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは罪なき一般市民を殺害した人は雇わないと思うよ。
example_sentences.english: I don’t think Koichi would hire anyone who has committed the crime of murdering innocent civilians.

notes: "This is a single kanji with an い on the end, meaning you know it's probably an adjective. What's the adjective form of smoke? It's smoky." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: All this smokiness is from a terrible chemical (けむ) spill that happened nearby. It was acid, so it burned everything up real good, causing the air to get pretty smokey."

example_sentences.japanese: 山火事のせいで町中が煙くなっているんです。
example_sentences.english: The entire town is smoky now due to the wildfire.

example_sentences.japanese: 花火が煙くて、むせてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: The smoky fireworks made me cough.

example_sentences.japanese: 煙いなあ！一体いつになったら煙草やめるんだよ？本当に臭いんだけど。
example_sentences.english: It’s so smoky! When the heck are you going to quit smoking? This really smells awful.

notes: "When you're looking straight into the face of a collapse it means trouble and difficulty coming soon." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. The とう goes to どう, though. Agh, what a 面倒."

example_sentences.japanese: 面倒な仕事をおし付けられたと思ったことは、一度もありません。
example_sentences.english: I never once thought they'd given me troublesome tasks.

example_sentences.japanese: こりゃまた面倒な仕事を引き受けたもんだね。
example_sentences.english: You've taken on such a difficult job!

example_sentences.japanese: 今に見てなさい。あのフグ少年はきっと面倒を引き起こすわよ。
example_sentences.english: Mark my words. That Fugu boy is going to cause trouble.

notes: "You have such abundant luck! When you have abundant luck, most people probably would think you also have a lot of wealth, because lots of wealth equals lots of luck, right?" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 不けい気を尻目に、コウイチはどんどん裕福になっていった。
example_sentences.english: As if the depression was someone else's problem, Koichi became wealthier and wealthier.

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトって、裕福な家庭の出身だと思うんだよね。
example_sentences.english: I think Viet comes from a wealthy family.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕の両親はド金持ちって訳じゃないけど、比較的裕福な方ではあります。
example_sentences.english: My parents are not super rich but they are relatively wealthy.

notes: "This is not what you thought would happen during your deliberation. You thought it would be very normal. Instead, it's the opposite. It's full of wonder and mystery." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 休みの日の時間って、不思議と飛ぶようにすぎるよね。
example_sentences.english: It's a mystery how time flies on your day off.

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトの周りにいると不思議なことがよく起こるよね！この前も列の最後尾にならんでいたのになぜか前の人が次々とゆずってくれるし。
example_sentences.english: Marvelous things often happen when I am near Viet! The other day, for example, we were joining the end of a line but all of the people in front of us let us cut, one after the other.

example_sentences.japanese: 私達はコウイチをすごく頼りにしていますが、どうしていつもそんなに陽気にしてるのか不思議にも思っています。
example_sentences.english: We all depend on Koichi, but we also wonder why he seems so oddly cheerful all the time.

notes: "With the whole body. Do it as a whole instead of as a part, or something." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 我々は、お客様に総体的に満足して頂けるよう努力しています。
example_sentences.english: We are concentrating on the overall satisfaction of our customers.

notes: "When people evaluate and judge you at every turn, it means you have much fame and reputation. Wouldn't this be terrible if people evaluated and judged you 24/7? Having that kind of fame would be difficult." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. The はん changes to ばん, too, so be careful of that."

example_sentences.japanese: この地域は昔はスラム街でしたが、政府の戦略としての居住地域の高級化が功を奏し、住環境ががらっと変わったんですよ。今は評判もすこぶるいいです。
example_sentences.english: This area used to be a slum, but the governmental strategy of gentrification has changed the neighborhood and now it has a really good reputation.

notes: "The sect that stands the highest are those who are high class, splendid, and fine. 立派だ!" "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. The りつ shortens to りっ though, so keep an eye on that you splendid frood you. Oh and は changes to ぱ too. Because rendaku and all that."

example_sentences.japanese: 私の猫は立派な髯を生やしているので、「ヒゲ」と名付けました。
example_sentences.english: My cat grew very handsome whiskers, so I named him Hige.

notes: "People Rights are human rights." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 服装規定が人権侵害にあたることがあるという人もいますが、それについてどう思いますか？
example_sentences.english: Some people say that dress codes can violate human rights, what do you think about that?

notes: "You have an  occasion to check out another country. Wow, so international!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは国際会議でTofuguの開発成果について発表する予定です。
example_sentences.english: Koichi is going to announce the development of Tofugu at an international conference.

notes: "The element of enemy isn't something you should think of as bad. You have to have the ""enemy element"" if you are to have lovely, dreamy, and beautiful things too. This is a good word when you're talking about some dude you think is hawt. Doesn't work as well with girls." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. You haven't learned this reading for 素 yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you:Oh wow, you look really lovely in that suit (す). Yes, I can see you through the Internet, and I have to say, that suit is just dreamy! Don't ever take it off."

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の他の人を助けたいっていう熱意が、素敵だなって思うのよね。
example_sentences.english: I find him attractive because of his enthusiasm for helping others.

notes: "The material you use to make resources is still material." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: もしよろしければ、いくつか資料をお送りさせて頂けませんでしょうか？
example_sentences.english: If you don’t mind, would I be able to send you some data?

notes: "My righteousness task is my obligation to these people. I will go out and purge the world of evil, be righteous, and make things happen. It's my duty!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 家事をするのは、夫と子どもに対する妻の義務だと言う人が多くいますが、果たしてそれは本当でしょうか？
example_sentences.english: Many people say that doing housework is a wife’s obligation to her husband and children, but is that really true?

notes: "My idea of duty is that you don't really have to do it. It's optional, you know?" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 名前と住所は法律で答えなくてはいけないと決まっているものですか？それとも任意ですか？
example_sentences.english: Do I legally have to tell you my name and address, or is it optional?

notes: "A noun (名詞) that has hardness is a noun that can't be budged. It's a big noun, so big that you have to capitalize these kinds of nouns in English. It is a proper noun." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. It will help to know the word 名詞 as well."

example_sentences.japanese: しりとりに固有名詞は使えません。
example_sentences.english: You can’t use proper nouns in the game Shiritori.

notes: "It's public establishment. It is public." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: もし沖縄を旅行するなら、牧志公設市場に行った方がいいよ。
example_sentences.english: If you travel to Okinawa, you should go to Makishi Public Market.

english: Sense Of Duty, Social Obligation, In-Law
notes: "You have righteousness and then a reason behind it, at least in your own mind. This is your sense of duty. And it really is a ""sense"" in a way, too. You just feel it. It's not an actual thing that is tangible. It is your own personal reason for this righteousness.This word can also mean in-law like your mother-in-law, because they're your mother in the social obligation sense only, not by blood." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 義理の父に義理チョコを買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought an obligatory box of chocolates for my father in law.

notes: "This is a weird one. Just think about the sect of hands. They are always doing jazz hands and things like that, trying to be all showy and flashy. Ugh, what a dumb sect, you think." "The readings are the ones you learned with the kanji, though て goes to で."

example_sentences.japanese: ドレスが派手すぎるので、ブライズ・メイドには絶対なりたくありません。
example_sentences.english: I never want to be a bridesmaid because the dresses are too flashy.

notes: "You control every degree of this system. Think about a system. It's designed to create more control for you, degree by degree by degree. That's why they call it ""The system,"" after all." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: これは、新制度についての初心者向け案内書です。
example_sentences.english: This guidebook for the new system is intended for beginners.

english: Tax Free, No Tax, Duty Free
notes: "When the tax is nothing things are tax free." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: お酒が無税だったらいいのにな。
example_sentences.english: I wish alcohol was tax-free.

notes: "You have nothing when it comes to enemies. Why? It's not because you're super kind and everyone likes you. No, it's that you've defeated anyone who's tried. You are unrivaled and invincible." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: しりとりで、コウイチは無敵だ。
example_sentences.english: Koichi is invincible at Shiritori.

notes: "This is like your side part of speech, as in, you add it to the side of a verb because it's an adverb." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は昨日、日本語の時を表す副詞を学びました。
example_sentences.english: I learned Japanese adverbs that show time yesterday.

notes: "Your appearance has many degrees. You turn it up a dial, and you show off one attitude. Then you turn it down a degree and you have another attitude. So many attitudes to show off." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: あいつ、誰と話をしているかによって、態度を180度変えるからね。信じられないよ。
example_sentences.english: I can’t trust him because his attitude takes a 180 degree turn depending on who he’s talking to.

english: Bad Mood, Pout, Displeasure, Ill Humor, Ill Humour, Sullen
notes: "Remember how 機嫌 means mood? Well when you add not it becomes a bad mood. It's so bad it's like you have no mood at all." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 花江は今、不機嫌なのよ。
example_sentences.english: Hanae is in a bad mood right now.

notes: "To prevent crime is a good thing. To do this you use crime prevention techniques." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 本日参りました理由は、当社の最新防犯グッズをご紹介するためです。
example_sentences.english: The reason I’m here today is to introduce our latest crime prevention products.

notes: "You have a large force at your disposal. This large force is a group of people (just think about when this word was probably made up... a long time ago, and the biggest force you could have was a huge group of people). This group of people force is also known as a crowd." "The reading for 大 is the おお reading (like 大きい). Nothing you can do about that but remember it. Then, 勢 is rendaku'd to become ぜい. Also something you'll just have to remember. Say this word a few times in your head, then you'll be able to come up with an idea of what sounds right and what sounds wrong so that you can figure it out next time this word comes up."

example_sentences.japanese: 大勢の人の前で話す事に慣れていないので、今からもう手が震えています。
example_sentences.english: I’m not used to speaking in front of crowds, so my hands are already shaking.

notes: "This is my territory. This is my region. This is my domain!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 誰でも、前進するためには未知の領域に足を踏み入れなくてはいけない。
example_sentences.english: Everyone has to take a step into unknown territory to progress.

notes: "Each ground is its own ground. It is each area." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 父の仕事の都合で、私の家族は各地を転々としなくてはいけませんでした。
example_sentences.english: My family had to move from place to place because of my dad’s job.

notes: "The outside view of you is your external appearance." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: このアパートメントの外観が好きです。
example_sentences.english: I like the outward appearance of this apartment.

english: Hate, To Hate, To Really Hate
notes: "Remember how 嫌い is to dislike? When that dislike is big, you really dislike it. That means you hate (or really hate) it." "The reading is the reading for 大, and the reading for 嫌い is like the one you learned with 嫌い in level 20."

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチはあなたのことが大嫌いなので、彼に代わってビエトがお会いします。
example_sentences.english: Mr. Viet will meet with you instead of Mr. Koichi because Mr. Koichi really hates you.

english: Hurtful Words, Hurtful Speech, Sarcasm, Disagreeableness
notes: "You have a flavor of dislike. If someone gives you ""flavor"" and you dislike it, what might that ""flavor"" be? How about hurtful words." "The reading for 味 is the on'yomi you learned with the kanji, but the reading for 嫌 is the kun'yomi, いや. Just imagine someone saying words so hurtful that you have to scream, ""Iyaaaaa!"" いや."

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はちょっと頭が悪いよね。どうしてあれが嫌味だってことに気づかないのかしら。
example_sentences.english: He’s kind of an idiot, really. Why didn’t he realize that it was sarcastic?

notes: "You already know how 可能 means possible. So when you add not it becomes impossible." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. It will help to know how to read 可能 first as well."

example_sentences.japanese: あのポーカーのトーナメントで、悪い予感はしてたんだけど、捨てるのは不可能な手札を持っていたんだよ。
example_sentences.english: In the poker tournament, I had a bad feeling, but it wasn’t possible for me to fold my hand.

notes: "What will give birth to business? Well, some kind of industry, probably. Though heavy industry is pretty good too." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本で最も重要な産業は何ですか？
example_sentences.english: What is the most important industry in Japan?

notes: "Remember how 不足 is a physical shortage? Well, now you have a physical shortage of sleep. That's a lack of sleep." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. The ふ in 不 goes to ぶ, so hopefully you've been getting enough sleep."

example_sentences.japanese: 「今日も残業するつもりなの？」「えっと…ですね、今日は寝不足なのでどちらかというと早くあがりたいと思っています。」
example_sentences.english: """So are you going to work overtime again today?"" ""Well actually, I was kind of hoping to get off work early today because I’ve been missing out on a lot of sleep."""

notes:
"Anything that's privately managed is private and privately run." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

"Something that is managed by the city is run by the city / city run." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の両親は、私営の葱園を所有しています。
example_sentences.english: My parents own a private green onion garden.

example_sentences.japanese: 大阪市は、舞州にすごくユニークな市営のゴミ焼却炉を建設しました。
example_sentences.english: Osaka City built a very unique, city run incineration plant in Maeshima.

english: Run By The Prefecture, Prefecture Run
notes: "Prefecture managed things are run by the prefecture." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: フグは県営図書館でサーモンといちゃついていて、図書館司書さんに怒られた。
example_sentences.english: Fugu was scolded for making out with Salmon in the prefectural library by a librarian.

notes: "The soil that makes up your territory is your territory. Ain't nobody goin' set foot on my soil nuh'uh." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ブログでは、国家間の領土問題にはあまり触れたくありません。
example_sentences.english: We don’t want to touch on the territorial disputes between nations on our blog.

notes: "When you transmit something that unites the people, you are probably pulling on tradition. Tradition is what unites us all and transmits who we are to everyone else. What is your 伝統?" "The reading is でん for 伝, which you've seen a few times by now. For 統 it's just the reading you've learned."

example_sentences.japanese: あの日本の伝統衣装の名前って何だっけ？単語をすっかり忘れちゃったよ。
example_sentences.english: What was the name of that traditional Japanese costume we saw yesterday? I completely forget the word.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it probably uses the kun'yomi reading. You did not learn this reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you to remember: Okay, this is a great value. Wait, what is? A tie (あたい). Get a tie, and it will make you more professional which will help you to get a better job. Great value, right there, just for a tie."

example_sentences.japanese: その価には同意できないな。タダ同然じゃないか。
example_sentences.english: I can’t agree with this price. It’s just not right.

notes: "The value is the value, though it's also the price." "If you want to find out how much value a horse has, you just have to make it neigh. If the horse can't neigh, you know you can lower the price you were going to pay. This works with other things you want to buy too. Don't spend too much on a pair of socks or sunglasses if they can't neigh. #Lifehack"

example_sentences.japanese: 羽毛布団はやっぱり値が張るね。
example_sentences.english: A down quilt is expensive, as I expected.

notes: "A superior haiku requires someone really famous and well known to read it... it's just on that level. Who is super well known and who deserves to read this superior haiku? A great actor, perhaps?" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の恋人は、この芝居で馬の役を演じている俳優よ。
example_sentences.english: My boyfriend is the actor performing the part of the horse.

notes: "Swamps and mountains happen a lot in Japan. That's why we use this to mean many! Because there are many of them!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. This word is usually written in kana though, so keep that in mind when you're writing it to use kana and not these kanji!

example_sentences.japanese: 今月は沢山の金を手に入れた。
example_sentences.english: I got a lot of money this month.

notes: "A medicine expert is someone who knows a lot about medicine. Those people are (I hope) generally doctors." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ほんの短い時間だけでしたが、あの医師は二度テレビに出たことがあります。
example_sentences.english: That doctor appeared on TV twice, though just for short amounts of time.

notes: "経済 is economics. So, something that has to do with economics is the economic or financial situation." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. It will help to know 経済 as well."

example_sentences.japanese: 私は経済的に苦しい立場にあるため、週五日フルタイムの仕事をしているうえに、週六日パートタイムでも働いています。
example_sentences.english: I work full time five days a week and part time six days a week because I’m in a tough financial situation.

notes: "A luxury swamp. Really? You got yourself a luxury swamp? That's not even a thing, not to mention probably really expensive. You are being too extravagant." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 二十歳の誕生日だからって贅沢な事は何もしたくないわ。良い本が読めればそれでいいの。
example_sentences.english: I don’t want to do anything extravagant for my twentieth birthday. All I want to do is read a good book.

notes: "Though there's no law about two kanji with the same meaning producing the same meaning, a law law is probably a law." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: もし一ヶ月の間に全法律用語を覚えることができたら、百万ドルお支払いしてもいいですよ。
example_sentences.english: If you can memorize every legal term within one month, I will pay you a million dollars.

notes: "A car that halts at each station. These trains aren't the big and fast ones, they're the local trains, and you'll need to ride them to get to smaller stations." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: この各駅停車はちょうどトンネルを通り過ぎたところです。
example_sentences.english: The local train has just passed through a tunnel.

notes: "What is a milk neck? Think about where milk comes from. Now, think of what looks like a little neck on the thing that milk comes from. What is that thing? It's a nipple." "The reading for this one is an exception, at least for the 乳 part. It's read as ち, and 首 is read as くび. You can remember the reading of nipple by thinking of a very special ""nipple"" you have on your face. A bee has burrowed into your cheek, and it squirts out milk from its butt, which sticks out of your cheek. You can't get it out, so you've decided to call this little cheek bee nipple your cheek bee (ちくび). Buzz buzz *milk*"

example_sentences.japanese: あんたの乳首から血が噴き出しているのを見て、思わずパニクッちゃったよ！
example_sentences.english: When I saw all the blood spurting out of your nipples, I couldn’t help but panic!

notes: "Your employment business is your occupation. What is your employment business?" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女の職業はモデルなの？写真写りがとてもいいんね。
example_sentences.english: Is her occupation being a model? She comes out really well in photos.

notes: "The members of employment in your business are your personnel or staff. You employed them, so they're your personnel!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は教師ではありませんが、学校職員です。
example_sentences.english: I’m not a teacher, but I am part of the school staff.

notes: "Leather's fate is in the hands of a revolution. It's the leather revolution! Off with these normal clothes and on with leather ones!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 革命の後、情勢は好転した。
example_sentences.english: The situation changed for the better after the revolution.

notes: "Your present location is the scene of the crime! And you're on the scene to check out what's currently going on." The readings are the ones you learned with the kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: あの犯罪現場で実際に何が起きたのかがすぐに明るみに出ることを期待しよう。
example_sentences.english: Let’s hope that what actually happened at the scene of the crime will come to light soon.

notes:
"The foundation of your standard is where you place your standard. No more, no less. This foundation is where the standard is all based off of." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

"The standard of standards is the main standard we work off of." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 私達は、製品の品質において、業界基準を大きく上回っています。
example_sentences.english: The quality of our product is far above industry standards.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は世間の規準からはちょっと外れた、ユニークな人です。
example_sentences.english: He is a unique person who is slightly out of the ordinary.

notes: "Something that's superior will excel. It is superior in every way." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 優秀なシステム管理者は、ハッキングによるいかなる攻撃の可能性にも備えます。
example_sentences.english: Superior system administrators prepare for any possibility of hacking.

notes: "A teaching expert/teacher is a teacher." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: あの教師は歴史認識をころころ変えるからあまり好きじゃない。
example_sentences.english: I don’t like that teacher because he is always flip-flopping on historical facts.

notes: "When the status of your employment is ""nothing"" then you're probably experiencing unemployment." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は完璧な夫ですが、一つだけ問題があるんです。十年間ずっと無職なんです。
example_sentences.english: He would be the perfect husband, save for one thing - he has been unemployed for ten years.

notes: "The pipe that holds your blood is your blood vessels." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. The けつ goes to けっ."

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は血管が切れそうなぐらい怒っていた。
example_sentences.english: He was so angry that his veins were popping out.

notes: "Your parents don't want this to expand out into the community. Let's keep this confidential." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: もし「親展」と書かれている封書を勝手に開けたら、信書開封罪とみなされて一年以下の懲役又は二十万円以下の罰金に課せられるかもしれませんよ。
example_sentences.english: "If you opened a sealed envelope marked ""Confidential"" without permission, it could be considered as an unlawful opening of a letter and you could be punished with imprisonment with work detail for under one year, or a fine of up to 200,000 yen. "

notes: "The loop that makes up the boundary of this area holds in the environment, at least this particular one." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 環境保護の観点では、固形石けんの方が液体石けんよりも優れている。
example_sentences.english: From an environmental perspective, bar soap is usually better than the liquid kind.

notes: "The real quality of something is its essence, or its true nature. Whether it's good or bad is a different story." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: この男は、物事の本質を一瞬で見抜くことができる。
example_sentences.english: This man can see the true nature of anything instantly.

notes: "When you can look at far things, but not near things, you have farsightedness." The reading is the readings you learned with the kanji, which you'd know if it wasn't for your farsightedness (go get some glasses so you can read our lessons!).

example_sentences.japanese: 遠視が進んできたので、そろそろ老眼鏡を買わなきゃいけないかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: My farsightedness is progressing, so I may have to get a pair of reading glasses soon.

english: Fixed Amount, Fixed Sum, Flat Rate, Ration
notes: "A determined amount is an amount that is fixed, aka a fixed amount." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: あの〜、定額貯金の口座を開設したいんですが。
example_sentences.english: Well, I’d like to open up a fixed deposit saving account.

english: Fixed Quantity, Measurement, Fixed Amount, Set Quantity, Set Amount
notes: "A determined quantity is a fixed quantity." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: どうにかしてこのリスクを定量化する方法はないのかな。
example_sentences.english: Isn’t there any way to change the set amount of risks?

english: Good Quality, High Quality, Superior Quality
notes: "Good quality is always good quality. Don't skimp!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 良質のワインを飲む事が私の唯一の楽しみだ。
example_sentences.english: Drinking good quality wine is my only pleasure.

notes: "A tall value. If you paid for something that had a tall value, it would have a high price." This word uses the kun'yomi readings for both kanji, but you know them both now, so you should be able to read this too!

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチの秘密の日記が、オークションで歴代最高値で落札された。
example_sentences.english: Koichi’s secret diary fetched a record high price at the auction.

notes: "A celebrate day is a day you get off to celebrate something awesome. This is also known as a holiday. Festivus for the restivus!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは祝日はいつもかなり派手な格好をしている。
example_sentences.english: Koichi always wears the most showy clothes on holidays.

english: Homemade, Home Brewed, Made At Home
notes: "By my self at home I manufactured this. It is homemade." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 私がホテルで自家製ビールを楽しんでいる時に、警察が自宅へ襲撃を決行したようです。
example_sentences.english: While I was enjoying my home brewed beer in a hotel room last night, the police seem to have conducted a raid on my house.

notes: "A many amount is a large amount or large sum." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 最終的に会議はうまくいって、なんとか我々の科学調査への多額の寄付金を約束してもらうことができたよ。
example_sentences.english: The meeting ended smoothly and we managed to make them promise us a large donation for our scientific research.

notes: "A large quantity is a large quantity. Kind of like the amount of words you're learning here now." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 台所に蟻が大量発生しているのを見て、完全に取り乱してしまいました。
example_sentences.english: I totally freaked out when I saw the large amount of ants in the kitchen.

notes: "Long sleeves are long sleeves." This word uses the kun'yomi readings for both kanji. You've learned them both already, so you should be able to read this already!

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は、長袖着ていった方がいいかな？
example_sentences.english: Should I wear a long sleeve top today?

example_sentences.japanese: 長袖のパーカーを買いに行くのに、付き合ってくれない？
example_sentences.english: Can you help me shop for some long sleeve hoodies?

example_sentences.japanese: 私の彼氏は、タトゥー隠すため夏でも長袖を着ることがある。
example_sentences.english: Sometimes my boyfriend wears long sleeves in summer in order to hide his tattoos.

notes: "A cheap valued item comes at a low price. What a good deal!" This word uses the kun'yomi readings for both kanji, but you know them both now, so you should be able to read this too!

example_sentences.japanese: 私はこの長靴を驚くほどの安値で買いましたが、防水加工がされてませんでした。
example_sentences.english: I bought these rain boots at an unbelievably low price, but they aren’t waterproof.

hiragana: こっきょう, くにざかい
notes: "A country boundary is that country's national border. Be careful about crossing it if you're carrying bananas. The border police seem to hate when you tell them you're carrying a banana in your pants when they ask you if you're bringing any fruits back. No idea why." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. The こく gets shortened to a nice little こっ."

example_sentences.japanese: 国境警備隊の隊員がアメリカに不法入国した外国人を国境のそばの茂みで見つけることはよくあることです。
example_sentences.english: It’s common for a US Border Patrol Guard to find an illegal alien in the bushes right by the national border fence.

notes: "When you can look at things that are near well but you can't see things far away, you have nearsightedness. Good to get those eyes checked out occasionally." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は近視と乱視の両方があります。
example_sentences.english: I have both nearsightedness and an astigmatism.

notes: "The original model of something isn't usually very good. It's rough. It's a prototype." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 私たちはまず初めに、粘土で彫刻の原型を作るんです。
example_sentences.english: We usually sculpt a model out of clay at first.

notes: "Half sleeves is just another name for short sleeves." "This word uses the on'yomi reading for 半 and the kun'yomi reading for 袖. You've learned them both already, so you should be able to read this word."

example_sentences.japanese: 半袖で寒くない？
example_sentences.english: Aren't you cold in a short sleeve top?

example_sentences.japanese: コンマリの本を読んでから、半袖のシャツは一枚しか持っていない。
example_sentences.english: After reading Kon Mari's book, I only own one short sleeve shirt.

example_sentences.japanese: 今年のファッショントレンドは半袖の革ジャンです。
example_sentences.english: This year's trending fashion is short sleeve leather jackets.

notes: "主観 is subjectivity. So when something moves towards subjectivity it is becoming subjective." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. It will help if you know 主観."

example_sentences.japanese: これはとても主観的な見方かもしれないけど、僕にとっては君は働き過ぎだと思うんだよね。近々休みを取った方がいいよ。
example_sentences.english: This may be a very subjective view, but to me, you work too much and should take time off sometime soon.

notes:
"The versus phenomenon is what you're going up against. It's your target because you're heading towards this phenomenon you're versusing against." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.english: "I’m thinking of getting a short asymmetrical haircut called ""ashime."""

notes: "Remember how 男優 was ""actor""? Well, I bet you can extrapolate what this one means because it now has woman in it. This is an actress." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 「ホグワーツ魔法魔術学校にはもう行きたくない。女優になりたいの。」「もう、馬鹿なこと言わないで。ハーマイオニーったら。」
example_sentences.english: """I don’t want to go to Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry anymore. I want to be an actress."" ""Oh, don’t be ridiculous, Hermione."""

example_sentences.english: I heard swimming at the gym is the most effective way to lose weight.

If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

notes: "I've learned to be accustomed to this. It has become my custom and habit." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.english: """I thought you quit smoking."" ""Well, they say old habits die hard."""
