notes: "New and fresh is fresh (has to be new if you want it to be fresh, after all)." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 前の職場では、止めろと言われるまでいつも残業していたので、毎日五時に退社するのはとても新鮮です。
example_sentences.english: I always worked overtime at my last job until I was told to stop, so it’s very new to me to leave work at five o’clock every day.

english: Full House, No Vacancy, Sold Out
notes: "Full of members, so sorry, no more room. This place is a full house. That means there is no vacancy here." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎朝、新宿駅に着くまで、満員電車の中に立っていなくてはいけないのが苦痛です。
example_sentences.english: I hate that I have to stand in a packed train until I arrive at Shinjuku station every morning.

notes: "The full moon is a full moon." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日の夜は満月なんだって。曇らないといいね。
example_sentences.english: Tomorrow night will be a full moon. I hope it’s not cloudy.

notes: "The limit is nothing. What? No limit? That means it will never stop! It is infinite!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 今は絶好調のように思えるが、需要は無限には増加しないだろう？
example_sentences.english: The situation looks bright at the moment, but the demand won’t increase perpetually, right?

english: Irregularity, Unsteadiness, Disorderly, Irregular, Erratic, Inconsistent
notes: "You know that 規則 means ""rule"" or ""regulation."" So a not ""rule"" or ""regulation"" is an irregularity." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 不規則な生活で体調を崩してしまった。
example_sentences.english: My health was ruined by my disorderly life.

notes: "Full points are when you get a perfect score." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 満点をとったら、先生に花丸をもらえるの。
example_sentences.english: When I get a perfect score, my teacher draws a flower on the paper.

english: Plastic Model, Model, Dummy, Scale Model
notes: "An imitation model is obviously not the real thing. It's (usually) a plastic model or just a model figure or something." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 祖父は、最初は従業員一人の小売模型店からこのビジネスを始めました。
example_sentences.english: My grandfather started his business out as a small one person plastic model retail shop.

notes: "This is the same as the kanji 豊, making it plentiful (though can also be abundant)." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: Don't worry, these resources are plentiful. You take (ゆた) what you want."

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日満員電車にぎゅうぎゅう詰めになって乗り込む人がたくさんいる以上、日本の生活がとても豊かだと言う事はできないね。
example_sentences.english: As long as so many people have to squeeze onto the crowded train every day, I can’t say Japanese life is very satisfying.

notes: "Plentiful and full, you are. That's the nice way of saying it. Actually, you're a bit plump. Wait, you want me to be nice again? Sorry, you're full figured." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は豊満な胸をもっており、いつも美しい谷間を覗かせている。
example_sentences.english: She has full breasts and always has lovely cleavage.

notes: "A ""not condition"" is where nothing is going well. How are things going? Not well. The condition is bad. We're in a recession." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 不況時に金の価格は上昇しやすい。
example_sentences.english: The price of gold tends to rise during recessions.

notes: "Rhythm is 律動, but by adding a 的 in there we get the adjective version of that word, making it rhythmical or rhythmic." "The reading is the same as 律動. The 的 part you should also be able to read by now."

example_sentences.japanese: この音楽はとても律動的ですね。
example_sentences.english: This music is very rhythmic.

notes: "The scene's color is the scenery, scene, and landscape. Looking good, scenery!" "The reading for this one is a bit weird and pretty exceptional. If you have a good idea for a mnemonic for this one send it in, but until then do your best to just remember this word's reading the best you can!"

example_sentences.japanese: ちょっといつもと違った景色を見るために、今日は回り道をしてみない？
example_sentences.english: Do you want to make a detour to see some different scenery than usual today?

notes: "A time limit is a time limit." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

notes: "Alright, so it's not quite the same, but something that is fresh is also vivid and splendid. I know those are a couple things I'd associate with freshness. Try to make the connection here before moving on." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: This vivid and splendid fresh fish is MINE! You grab the other (あざ) one that's not as vivid and splendid. This one is mine."

example_sentences.english: The new personnel manager brilliantly solved the problem regarding mandatory overtime without pay.

notes: "A person created item is artificial, not ""real.""" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.english: The diplomat was stabbed by Android No.18.

notes: "Things that are of the beast type or animal type are within the beasts and animals category." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

notes: "Your energy is ... well ... different. That's the nice way to put it. You're crazy, actually.WARNING: We're teaching you this word because it's used quite a bit still (especially online) and we want you to be able to understand it if you see it. But please keep in mind that this is considered to be a discriminatory word against people with mental illnesses, so we strongly recommend you do not use or direct this word toward anyone. Think of it like a really inappropriate swear word that makes you really uncool if you say it. Please!" "The reading is 気 plus 違い."

notes: "I'm going to direct and adjoin the routes together. No more multiple stops. This is direct." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.english: I heard that you two ate my bacon directly from him.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it probably uses the kun'yomi reading. You did not learn this reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you remember: It is I! Due to my ego, I love the Wii and no other gaming device. I love playing all the Wii-ware (われ) that's available, and everything else sucks."

example_sentences.japanese: 我関せずって感じのアイツの態度、超嫌なんだけど。

notes: "After an interval of time it will adjoin, but not right away. That is because it was being indirect." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 寝室用の落ち着いた感じのロマンチックな間接照明を探しているんです。
example_sentences.english: I’m looking for soft, romantic, indirect lighting for our bedroom.

notes: "Lead poison is lead poisoning." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.english: He’s as obedient as a dog.

notes: "Somebody who is alone is single or unmarried." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は独身で、婚活中です。とりあえずそんな感じですが、何か他に聞きたいことがあれば、遠慮なくご連絡ください。
example_sentences.english: I’m single and looking for someone I can marry. That’s really it for now. But please do not hesitate to contact me if you need any further information about me.

english: Sweaty Smell, Smell Sweaty, Sweaty Stench
notes: "Your sweat is smelly (臭い). That is your sweaty smell." The readings are the ones you learned with the kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は彼の汗臭い枕が好きだった。
example_sentences.english: I liked his sweaty smelling pillow.

notes: "It is alone and special. Nothing is like it. It is very unique." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.english: These spices have a unique aroma.

english: Up To Now, So Far, Usual, Traditional
notes: "You've come and you've obeyed the whole way up to now. I guess it's time for you to know my secret.  So far I've really been a...*ahem*This word can also mean usual or traditional when it's modifying a noun or phrase with の. It makes sense if you try to think about it: a ""so far"" book is just a weird way of saying a ""traditional"" book." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.english: So far, first year employees are given zero paid holidays in this company.

notes: "One who does beast medicine is a veterinarian, taking care of all them animals." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.english: Going to that veterinarian has the best benefits. Of course he’s kind and intelligent, but not only that, you can split up your bill into separate payments.

notes: "A field beast/animal is one that lives outside and not under human care. It is a wild beast / wild animal." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: あのカップル、まさに「美女と野獣」って感じだね。
example_sentences.english: That couple is exactly like the Beauty and the Beast.

notes: "The extreme south is the extreme of south. It's about as south as you can go. That place is known as Antarctica." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の両親は、この夏に南極に行ってみることを決心しました。
example_sentences.english: My parents have decided to go to Antarctica this summer.

notes: "See this on the end of a word, and you know that it is a ______symptom. When you have a _____symptom, you have some kind of disease or sickness (otherwise why would you have a symptom of some kind?)." Since this is attached to things, it's treated like a jukugo word, so the on'yomi reading is used here.

example_sentences.japanese: 妻の神経性ヒステリー症について、医者に相談しなくてはいけません。
example_sentences.english: I should consult a doctor about my wife’s neurotic hysteria.

notes: "Remember how 効果 means ""effect""? Add ~like to that and it's effective!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 成果主義の給与制度は、良い社員を引き込む最も効果的で公平な方法である。
example_sentences.english: Performance based salaries are the most effective and fairest ways to attract good workers.

notes: "At the extreme edge, which is just the extreme." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 君は奇跡を起こすことができるかもしれない。でも、僕は君には極端なことは避けてもらいたいんだよ。
example_sentences.english: You may be able to perform miracles, but I want you to avoid doing extreme things.

notes: "Take the middle route, half on the edge. You don't do anything the full way. Just to the middle. Just to the half. Not to the edge. This was really half finished and half assed of you." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. The ぱ at the end is the only tricky part here since that isn't a common reading (or the one you learned before) for the kanji. Just watch out for that, and you'll be fine."

example_sentences.japanese: 俺は中途半端な生き方をしてきたかもしれないけど、マフィアに入りたいって思ったことは一度もないよ。
example_sentences.english: My life may be incomplete, but I would never dream of joining the mafia.

notes: "You're so healthy it puts you at ease. That's your health! So healthful, go you!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 会社側が負担する健康保険は、諸手当の中に含まれているのでしょうか。
example_sentences.english: Is company-paid health insurance included in the fringe benefits?

notes: "抜く is to extract. If you extract yourself for an interval of time from the world, you won't learn anything and become an idiot." "The readings come from the ま reading of 間 and from 抜く."

example_sentences.english: I don’t want him to think of me as a stupid country bumpkin.

notes: "Remember how 規模 is scale? Well, this is a big scale, which is on a large scale." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

notes: "Feeling drowsy and like I want to sleep. I just want to sleep so bad." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は、給与の良い管理職へ昇格したいがために、睡眠時間を削って一生懸命働いている。
example_sentences.english: He wants to be promoted to management for better pay so he works hard by cutting down on his sleep.

notes: "規模 is ""scale."" This is a small one, making this small scale." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 私達はみんな、啓介に小規模農場なんて始めない方がいいと警告したんです。
example_sentences.english: We all warned Keisuke against starting a small scale farm.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it probably uses the kun'yomi reading. example_sentences.japanese: 私達は空気洗浄機とか家電を販売してるんですが、お客さんがあまりこないので、お店では正直暇してます。
example_sentences.english: We sell home electronic appliances like air purifiers, but not many customers come in and honestly, I have a lot of free time at the store.

notes: "Led astray in what you believe by all these superstitions. These superstitions will lead you astray, don't believe them!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 年寄りは迷信を信じやすい。
example_sentences.english: Old people tend to be superstitious.

notes: "Your symptom condition is your symptoms that you have." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の症状について、一度同僚に相談しました。

notes: "The acid element is oxygen. In German it’s the same as in Japanese - it’s called “Sauerstoff”, including “sauer”, the word for “sour”. The word “oxygenium” in Greek/Latin literally means “acid maker”. Long ago chemists thought oxygen was a defining characteristic of acids, later they found out there are also acids without oxygen like hydrochloric/muriatic/salt acid and the defining characteristic actually is hydrogen. "This is a single kanji with an い on the end, meaning you know it's probably an adjective. What's the adjective form of valuable? It's valuable." You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: What is most valuable to you? Of course it's your toe toe (とうと). It's your big toe (the long とう) with another small toe growing out of it (short と). Imagine your toe toe, and then imagine how valuable it is to you. So valuable! You can also think about 尊い, a similar word which means ""revered."" It's a similar idea, and it has the same reading."

example_sentences.japanese: 息子に、「命ってどれくらい尊いの？」なんて聞かれちゃってさ。言葉に窮しちゃったよ。
example_sentences.english: "My son asked me something like, ""How precious is life?"" I had difficulty answering him."

example_sentences.japanese: 命ってのはベーコンと同じくらい貴いものなんだよ。
example_sentences.english: Life is as precious as bacon.

notes: "It has simplicity and is easy. Whatever it is, it is simple and easy." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: もしうちに泊まりたいなら、簡易ベッドがあるよ。
example_sentences.english: If you want to sleep over at our place, we have a cot.

notes: "Simplicity is simple, making this simple as well." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: iPadはノートパソコンよりも持ち運びが簡単です。
example_sentences.english: iPads are easier to carry around than laptops.

notes: "Something with not sugar is something that is sugar free or unsweetened." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: さっきも言ったけど、珈琲は無糖派なの。
example_sentences.english: As I told you earlier, I drink unsweetened coffee.

notes: "Something is dangling in front of you, so you fix it so it's straight and not moving. It becomes perfectly vertical, perpendicular to the floor." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: ロケットは垂直に発射した。
example_sentences.english: The rocket took off vertically.

notes: "To run alongside the line (referring to the train line) means along the train line. What's along the train line? All kinds of things if you look carefully." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の弟は、京王沿線に住んでいます。
example_sentences.english: My brother is living along the Keio Line.

notes: "The holy writing is the bible." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 聖書を半分ぐらい読み終わりました。
example_sentences.english: I’m halfway through the bible.

notes: "The run alongside coast basically just describes the coast." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 今度の日曜日にヨットで沿岸を一緒に帆走しないかって彼に誘われたんだ。
example_sentences.english: He asked me to sail along the coast in his yacht with him this Sunday.

notes: "A loss will give you a disadvantage and handicap. So, try not to get any losses... or you'll be at a disadvantage." "The reading comes from the kanji, so you aren't at a disadvantage... this time."

example_sentences.japanese: ポーカーで五百ドル損をした。
example_sentences.english: I had a loss of $500 in poker.

notes: "After you use it you throw away it, making whatever it is you used a disposable item." "The reading comes from 使う and 捨てる, combined into one."

example_sentences.japanese: 私にとって、使い捨てカイロは冬には無くてはならないものです。
example_sentences.english: For me, disposable pocket warmers are indispensable in winter.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it probably uses the kun'yomi reading. You did not learn this reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you to remember: Some dude... he did it two times. Yah, two (やつ) times.This can seem kind of derogatory, if you say it the wrong way. But as long as you're duding to your dude friends and not your no-dude boss, you should be a-okay to dude-bro it up!"

example_sentences.japanese: 宝くじが当たってから、奴は数週間最高の気分を味わったんだ。
example_sentences.english: After winning the lottery, that dude was on a high for weeks.

notes: "God is holy. Everything about a holy god is full of holiness." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 村人たちは、自然に対し神聖な敬意を持っています。
example_sentences.english: The villagers have a holy respect for nature.

notes: "Not pure things are impure." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は不純な動機から日本語を勉強し始めました。
example_sentences.english: I started studying Japanese out of impure motives.

notes: "Inside internal organs are your internal organs, though you'd think the second kanji would give a hint to that without the 内." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: ご近所さんのガレージで鹿の内臓を取り出すんです。
example_sentences.english: They take the internal organs out of deer in my neighbor’s garage.

notes: "A thin body type is called lean or slim. These days this is usually used in the context of slimming salons and massages you can get that may or may not work." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You've learned them already, so you should be able to read this on your own!

example_sentences.japanese: そのエステは痩身を専門にしているんだって。
example_sentences.english: I heard the beauty salon specializes in slimming.

example_sentences.japanese: 一年くらいマッサージに通ったんだけど、痩身の効果はなかったよ。
example_sentences.english: I kept getting massages for about a year, but I didn't have any slimming results.

example_sentences.japanese: 防犯カメラに写っていたのは、痩身の男性でした。
example_sentences.english: The person caught by security camera was a slim guy.

english: "Long Time No See, It's Been A While"
notes: "This is kind of a ""set phrase"" in Japanese, though we're going to treat it like a vocab word here (because it's so common and useful!). You know that 久 means ""long time"" - so now let's pay attention to the kana: しぶり. Just imagine that she buried you alive, then a few days later came back to dig you up. The first thing she says is ""LONG TIME NO SEE!""" "You learned this reading when you learned 久しい. It's the same one!"

example_sentences.japanese: 久しぶりですね！
example_sentences.english: Long time no see!

example_sentences.japanese: 久しぶりのビールは、なみだが出るほどおいしかった。
example_sentences.english: Beer after being sober for so long was so good it brought me to tears.

example_sentences.japanese: 久しぶり！とあったことのない人にいわれた。
example_sentences.english: "I was told ""long time no see"" by a person that I had never met before."

notes: "A magnet stone is a magnet. Magnets look like little stones, right?" "The 磁 reading makes sense. The しゃく reading for 石 is an exception. To remember this, just think how you are using a magnet to find this shack (しゃく) full of other magnets. It pulls you towards the shack, and when you find it and open it, all the magnets fly out and crush you because of magnety reasons."

example_sentences.japanese: お土産に可愛い磁石をいくつか買ったわよ。
example_sentences.english: I got some cute magnets for your souvenir.

notes: "Something that's valuable and heavy is extremely precious and probably even more valuable than your less heavy things." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You didn't learn this reading for 重 though, so here's a mnemonic to help you:Keep things precious to you very close, because the evil Mrs. Chou (ちょう) will come and steal it away if you don't. She'll take every valuable you have and destroy them."

example_sentences.japanese: 貴重なご意見を有難うございます。
example_sentences.english: Thank you for your valuable opinions.

notes: "A deep carve is very serious and grave. Just imagine getting cut with a sword. If the carve is deep, well, that's serious." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 甲状腺異常のある日本の子どもたちの数が増えているのは、深刻な問題です。
example_sentences.english: It’s a serious problem that the number of Japanese children with thyroid abnormalities have been increasing.

notes: "Simple and pure. This is simple." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語で単純な文章なら作れますが、難しいのはまだ無理です。
example_sentences.english: I can make up simple sentences in Japanese, but I can’t do complicated ones yet.

notes: "Some dude who is a slave is just a slave." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: そう取り乱すなよ。心配ないって。俺らはまだ奴隷だけど、そのうち何とかなるよ。
example_sentences.english: Don’t lose your cool. Don’t worry. We are still slaves now, but things will work out.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "You are stylish. If you're stylish, you always いきます (いき) to the clothing stores to buy more stylish clothes."

example_sentences.japanese: 自分で粋な会話をしてるって思ってるところがムカツクんだよね。
example_sentences.english: He believes that he carries on refined conversations, but they’re actually irritating.

notes: "People of a valuable tribe are part of the nobility. Unlike our tribes, they are valuable." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: ああ、もし私が貴族の家柄に生まれていたら、彼女と話をすることも可能だったかもしれないのに。
example_sentences.english: If I had been born to a noble family, I would have been able to talk to her.

english: Wirepuller, Mastermind, Black Curtain, Dick Cheney
notes: "Just imagine a black curtain off in the background. You don't know what's behind it, but you know what's in front of it. Thing is, the thing in front of the curtain is controlled by whoever is behind the black curtain. This person is the wirepuller or mastermind of the situation. Like the Wizard of Oz, or something." "The reading is the vocab readings for 黒 and 幕, though the vocab reading for 幕 is the same as the on'yomi reading, making things easy for you."

example_sentences.japanese: 結局、あんたが黒幕だったんだな。どうりてあの女を殺した時手慣れていたと思ったよ。
example_sentences.english: So, you are the mastermind, huh? No wonder you seemed so professional when you killed her.

notes: "A valuable formal name title. It's like saying something like ""the valuable great you""... or something. Anyways, this means you, but it isn't as nice as it sounds. Probably a lot of irony and sarcasm going into this word, because if you use きさま to say ""you"" to someone, you're probably not pleased with that person, or you're just trying to be rude." "The readings are the reading you learned with 貴 plus the vocab reading for 様."

example_sentences.japanese: 貴様がうるさかったせいで、昨日全然寝れなかったじゃねぇか。
example_sentences.english: I couldn’t sleep well because YOU were very noisy.

notes: "You mix, then you go mutual, then you mix, and then you go mutual. Alternately, you could go mix again?" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.english: She alternately licked two kinds of ice cream.

example_sentences.japanese: ねぇ、私、あなたと喋るだけで、いい気分になるわ。あなたって、私にとって本当に理想の彼氏だわ。
example_sentences.english: You know what, I get in a good mood just from talking to you. You really are my ideal boyfriend.

notes: "A rice paddy and a cottage. This is the image of the countryside to me. This is rural. Just cottages and rice paddies..." "The reading doesn't really make sense for the kanji, and is an exception for sure. Just think about how when you're in the countryside you're in 中 (いなか) of nowhere."

example_sentences.japanese: 田舎道で死にかけのフクロネズミを見ました。
example_sentences.english: I saw a dying possum on a country road.

notes: "蒸れる is ""to be humid."" So, if you have a humid hot, you have weather that is hot and humid (or you can just say humid, because that implies hotness too, usually). This is a useful word for summers in Japan, since you'll complain about this all the time." "The reading comes from 蒸れる and 暑い. Know those and you know this too."

example_sentences.japanese: 今年の夏は絶対去年よりも蒸し暑いよね。
example_sentences.english: This summer is definitely more humid than it was last year.

notes: "If you're inside prison you're in prison." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.english: How does your story about being in prison end?

example_sentences.english: My grandmother always tells me that eating bananas leads to a long life.

notes: "Mutual and mutual is mutual." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 相互リンクしてもらえませんか。
example_sentences.english: Could you set up a mutual link with me, please?

notes: "The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. It also means myself and I." "As for myself? I'm not Bob. oh no, Ray (おのれ), Ray is my name."

example_sentences.japanese: 俺は、みんな死ぬ前に己の墓は己で建てるべきだと思うけどね。
example_sentences.english: I think people should build their own graves before they die.

notes: "Your self oneself, is your oneself or self." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.english: "He was very proud of himself and said, ""I’m my own favorite singer,"" with a very self-satisfied smile."

notes: "The reality of the sword is that it will cut you right in half and kill you, easily. The fact that this is true is a very serious thing. Very serious." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.english: I’m seriously thinking about a way to raise prices without losing sales.

notes: "If you have an idea, it means you are important. You have significance. Those without ideas are just big jokes and can't do anything at all." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 卒論のための研究で、統計学的に有意な値を導けなかったんです。
example_sentences.english: The research for my graduation thesis wasn’t statistically significant.

notes: "This is he but plural, and includes ladies too. The ""ra"" makes it plural, making it ""they"" or ""them."" While this gennnnnnerally refers to a group of males, it can include ladies too." The reading is the same as the one you learned with the kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼らはみんな、電車の切符を買っていなかったため、無賃乗車者として捕まった。
example_sentences.english: None of them bought train tickets and they were caught for riding without paying.

english: Troublesome, Burdensome, Hard To Deal With, Trouble, Burden, Nuisance
notes: "The unlucky is just getting jammed in there. So much unluckiness leads to a very troublesome and burdensome time." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. The やく gets changed to やっ."

example_sentences.japanese: ビエットの顔に落書きなんてしたら、後々厄介なことになるよ。
example_sentences.english: If you draw on Viet’s face, you’re asking for trouble.

notes: "Something big in width is still big, in fact it's of a pretty substantial size." The readings for this word are both kun'yomi readings. You've learned both of these readings by now so you should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 会議の資料が大幅に変更されました。
example_sentences.english: The meeting’s documents were largely changed.

notes: "One generally does things... in general. It's more common this way." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. Just remember that the はん changes to ぱん for 般."

example_sentences.japanese: 私みたいな一般庶民には、そのパンプスはちょっと高すぎるかな。
example_sentences.english: Those pumps are a little too expensive for an ordinary citizen like me.

notes: "A horse deer is a stupid idea. You're an idiot for thinking about it, really. It's quite dumb." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: お前がそこまで馬鹿じゃなければ、お前がどれだけ馬鹿なのか説明することができるんだけどなあ。
example_sentences.english: If you weren’t so stupid, I could explain to you how stupid you are!

notes: "If we take along our alliance and move it forward to something better, we have a league or federation. It's like we're one group now!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: スケート選手たちは、日本スケート連盟について不平を漏らしています。
example_sentences.english: Figure skaters are complaining about the Japan Skating Federation.

notes: "A mouth deep red is a deep red you put on your mouth. This is lipstick." "The readings are the kun'yomi readings of both. 口 and 紅 vocab words combined into one."

example_sentences.japanese: 口紅をポケットに入れっぱなしにしてたみたいで、乾燥機の中で溶けちゃったのよね。
example_sentences.english: I left my lipstick in my pocket and it melted in the dryer.

notes: "A medicine can heal. This is medical treatment." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本で医者になりたいので、今は医療用語を勉強しています。
example_sentences.english: I want to be a doctor in Japan, so I’m studying medical terminology now.

notes: "The kanji and the word are the same. That means they share meanings as well. This word can also mean core because that's where the nucleus is in a cell, and nuclear because we like to blow ourselves up nowadays..." The reading is the same as the kanji reading you learned.

example_sentences.japanese: どうして核は細胞の中心部に位置するんですか？
example_sentences.english: Why is the nucleus located at the center of the cell?

example_sentences.japanese: 沖田君は小学生の時に原子核について興味を持ち、今ではこのチームの核として働いてくれています。
example_sentences.english: Okuta-kun became interested in atomic nuclei when he was an elementary school student, and now he's working as the nucleus of this team.

example_sentences.japanese: 核ミサイルの発射が、もう予定より三時間も遅れています。
example_sentences.english: The nuclear missile launch is three hours behind schedule now.

notes: "Something that is ultra natural (自然的) is supernatural. Too natural! Super!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: そういえば、私の超自然的な力についてお話したことってありましたっけ？
example_sentences.english: Have I ever told you about my supernatural power?

notes: "Your eyebrows interval is that place between your eyebrows called the brow. The technical term for this interval between your brows is the glabella, but I bet you never use that word. example_sentences.japanese: 社長は眉間にシワを寄せながら「この資料は誰が書いた？」と言った。
example_sentences.english: "The company president said, ""Who wrote these documents?"" while furrowing his brow."

example_sentences.japanese: 私のパグのチャームポイントはやはり眉間のシワです。
example_sentences.english: You know, my pug's most attractive feature is the lines on his brow after all.

example_sentences.japanese: 眉間を黒いマジックで塗りつぶしてください。
example_sentences.english: Please fill in your brow with black marker.

notes: "A fishing expert is a fisherman." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. The reading is the りょう reading, because you gotta get in your row boat to be a fisherman."

example_sentences.japanese: 私はその漁師を知っていますよ。私の義理の兄ですから。
example_sentences.english: I know that fisherman because he is my brother in law.

notes: "The fishing industry is the fishing industry or a fishery." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: ここは小さな漁村で、ここに住むほとんどの人は漁業に従事しています。
example_sentences.english: This is a small fishing village and most of the people living here are engaged in fishing.

notes: "A burial ceremony is a funeral." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.
