example_sentences.english: If anyone calls, say I’m at a funeral and will be back at three o’clock.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. The reading is the same as the kanji reading you learned.

example_sentences.japanese: 苺は旬ではありませんが、クリスマスケーキにたくさん使われます。
example_sentences.english: Although strawberries aren’t in season, they are used a lot for Christmas cake.

notes: "Some odd traces are left over here. We don't really understand what happened, because it was a miracle, but it certainly left some odd traces behind." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 奇跡でも起こらない限り、百人が同時におならをするのは不可能でしょう。
example_sentences.english: Unless there is a miracle, a hundred people won’t be able to fart at the same time.

notes: "A before omen is something that tells you about something that will happen before it happens. Really this is just an omen or sign." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: この雲と風は嵐の前兆です。
example_sentences.english: The clouds and wind are signs of a storm.

notes: "A punish penalty is a punishment." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 犯罪を根絶するには、火あぶりの刑みたいな残酷な刑罰を全部復活させるべきだと思うね。
example_sentences.english: In order to root out crime, I think we should restore all the brutal punishments, like burning people at the stake.

notes: "If you look to the sea, you are seaside or coastal." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本の学生の多くは、夏に臨海学校に行く事を経験します。
example_sentences.english: Many Japanese students experience going to seaside schools during the summer.

notes: "恥 is a ""disgrace."" If you 知らず then you don't know something. In this case, you don't know disgrace, and a person who doesn't know disgrace is a shameless person, because they don't care what disgraces them and what doesn't." "The reading is 恥 and 知る put together."

example_sentences.japanese: あの俺の兄貴は恥知らずの嘘つきだ。何の事だかサッパリ分からないなんて言ってたくせに、俺のベーコンを平らげたのはアイツだったんだよ。
example_sentences.english: My brother is such a shameless liar. He told me he had no idea what happened, but he was the one who ate all my bacon.

notes: "An omen for the climate of things is a sign or indication of change. If there's an omen, there's going to be a sign as well." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は、私に下痢の兆候がきたと告げるやいなや、トイレに駆け込んでいった。
example_sentences.english: She told me that she had symptoms of diarrhea and rushed into the bathroom.

notes: "The machine gulf isn't what you'd expect. In fact, looking at the reading will probably help the most first, since this word represents Taiwan." "The reading is たい for 台, which is a little different from what you learned, but not the end of the world (especially if you can get the meaning down). The わん is however what you learned, so even if you arrive to だいわん, you'll probably realize that this is たいわん."

example_sentences.japanese: 感染源を台湾のアヒルの群れだと突き止めました。
example_sentences.english: We’ve traced the source of the infection and it was a flock of ducks in Taiwan.

notes: "Look to time to see how much longer this will last. It's not forever, it's temporary, which is why we must look to time to figure out how much longer it'll be around." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: マミは、臨時のボーナスが出たので、さらにベーコンを購入した。
example_sentences.english: Mami got an extra bonus, so she bought more bacon.

notes: "Remember how you learned that 馬鹿 means ""idiot?"" Well put two idiots together and everything they say and do is absolutely absurd. Remember how ridiculous that ""Dumb and Dumber"" movie was? Yeah. Like that." "You already learned 馬鹿, so as long as you can remember it twice in a row, you should be able to read this too!"

example_sentences.japanese: 馬鹿馬鹿しいこと言わないでよ。
example_sentences.english: Don’t say stupid things.

notes: "馬鹿 is ""stupid"" so if you hear a rumor about something (らしい) that's stupid, you'll just respond by saying ""that's absurd.""" "The reading comes from 馬鹿."

example_sentences.japanese: 全く馬鹿らしいにもほどがある！！！
example_sentences.english: That’s completely absurd!!!

notes: "The day's edition is the daily edition." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. The にち goes to にっ."

example_sentences.japanese: アヤが描いたパグのイラストが、ある日刊紙のマスコットキャラクターに選ばれました。
example_sentences.english: Aya’s illustration of the cute pug was selected as a daily newspaper’s mascot character.

notes: "A round tray is a disk, though if it goes through the air it becomes a flying saucer." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: しばらくすると、ジェームズは円盤を脇に抱えて戻ってきて、UFOを見つけたんだと言いました。
example_sentences.english: After a while, James came back with a disk under his arm and told us he found a UFO.

notes:
"Go ahead and suspend fate, let's get this done before the time we are fated to do it. We are that eager to get started." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

"You're clever and bright so obviously you're going to make wise and sensible decisions. In fact, when you go to make these very wise choices and observations, your brain glows brightly." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 足が泥にはまって、一生懸命抜こうとしてみたんですが、できなかったんです。
example_sentences.english: My foot was stuck in the mud and I tried with all my might to get it out, but I couldn’t.

example_sentences.japanese: このビールを買うのは賢明なご決断ですよ。コクがあるだけでなく、喉ごしもとてもいいですからね。
example_sentences.english: Buying this beer is a wise decision. Not only does it have full-bodied flavor, but it also has such a pleasant, clean finish.

notes: "Do you fat al... is fatal!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 生徒とのスキャンダルは、彼の教師生命にとって致命的でした。
example_sentences.english: The scandal with his student was fatal to his teaching career.

notes: "All generalal! It's super general. It's general and overall and across the board. Nothing specific going on here." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 全般的に、犬は猫を怖がるものじゃないんですかね。
example_sentences.english: Dogs are generally scared of cats, aren’t they?

notes: "This is the na-adjective version of loose, so that means this word means loose or mild or gentle." The reading comes from what you learned with the kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: その小川が緩やかに東にカーブしているところがあるんだけど、そこが釣りの穴場なんだよ。
example_sentences.english: The stream curves gently towards the east and is a good fishing spot.

notes: "This is a single kanji with an い on the end, meaning you know it's probably an adjective. What's the adjective form of loose? It's loose." The reading is the one you learned with the kanji, so feel nice and loose and move on to the next item.

example_sentences.japanese: このシャツは首回りが緩いんですよね。
example_sentences.english: The neck of this shirt is pretty loose.

notes: "The moon edition is the monthly edition, since 月 also means ""month.""" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 月刊誌『ベーコン』は、エープリルフールのジョークとして、「ノーベルベーコン賞はマミに授与された。」と報じた。
example_sentences.english: "A monthly magazine named ""The Bacon"" reported that the Nobel prize for bacon was awarded to Mami as an April Fool’s joke."

notes: "If you are at an elderly age you are at an old age." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本の老齢年金の仕組みについてご説明してもらえませんでしょうか。
example_sentences.english: Could you please explain the structure of Japan’s old-age pension to me?

notes: "If 一般 is ""general""/""common"" then something that has 的 attached to it is ordinary or normal or common." "The reading comes from 一般 plus 的."

example_sentences.japanese: 大学卒業後も実家に住み続けることは、日本ではそこそこ一般的です。
example_sentences.english: Continuing to live in your parents’ home after graduating from college is pretty common in Japan.

notes: "A pregnant wife is a pregnant woman." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 妊婦さんのためのカウンセラーという、臨時の仕事が見つかりました。
example_sentences.english: I got a temporary job as a counselor for pregnant women.

hiragana: おくぶかい, おくふかい
notes: "If your interior is deep, then you're a really profound person." "The readings for this word are both kun'yomi readings. You learned おく when you learned the kanji, and ふかい from 深い, so you should be able to read this on your own. Most of the time the ふ is rendaku'd into ぶ, but it can be read the other way too."

example_sentences.japanese: 狩人とは非常に奥深い職業です。
example_sentences.english: A hunter is a very profound occupation.

notes: "We're inside together on this information. Just you and me, inside our knowledge. It is secret and confidential." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はICレコーダーで会話を内緒で録音します。
example_sentences.english: I secretly record conversations with my IC recorder.

notes: "You are one and together. If you're together as one, you are together." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. The 一 becomes いっ."

example_sentences.japanese: 「ご一緒してもよろしいですか？」「全然、構いませんよ。どうぞお座りください。」
example_sentences.english: """Do you mind if I join you?"" ""No, not at all. Please have a seat."""

notes: "原子 is atom and 爆弾 is bomb. What is an atom bomb? An atomic bomb." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の家は火災保険に入っていますが、もし誰かが原子爆弾を落として、それで家が燃えちゃった場合はどうなるんでしょうか。それでも保険金は降りるんでしょうか。
example_sentences.english: My house has fire insurance, but what if someone drops an atomic bomb and my house catches on fire? Would I still get the insurance money?

notes: "This is a single kanji with an い on the end, meaning you know it's probably an adjective. The adjective form of bitter is bitter, or more specifically, a bitter flavor." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: She gives you some food, and it's terribly bitter. You look at the lady who gave you this bitter food. You say, ""She boooo"" as in, she's no good, and she serves bitter food."

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチはDDOS攻撃に渋い顔をして、拳で机をバンバンと叩いた。
example_sentences.english: Koichi frowned at the DDOS attack and banged his fist on the table.

english: Broken Japanese, Broken English, Broken Language
notes: "One sided saying things means you don't know both sides of the language, making you have broken Japanese or broken language." "The reading is the reading you learned for 片 and the こと of 言葉."

example_sentences.japanese: 私は片言の日本語でなんとかパスポートの再発行をしてもらいました。
example_sentences.english: I managed to get my passport reissued with my broken Japanese.

notes: "Take along your home country to all the other spaces you want to add to your group. Put them together to form the commonwealth or federation." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: ちょっと待って。もしかして、連邦税と州税どっちも払わなきゃいけないの？
example_sentences.english: Wait a second. By any chance, do I have to pay both federal and state taxes?

notes: "Humility is heavy, so it's best nobody knows your secret. You should be discreet instead." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You just need to remember the alternative reading for 重. If you aren't discreet or careful, the evil Mrs. Chou (ちょう)will find you and kill you!"

example_sentences.japanese: どうしてそんなに慎重なんですか。
example_sentences.english: What makes you so careful?

notes: "The modesty void is that big pit you go into when you are showing modesty or humility." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: その謙虚な男性が実はマフィアの一員だったなんて、信じられません。
example_sentences.english: I can’t believe that humble man was actually a member of the mafia.

notes: "A one sided hand is one of your hands, that means you're doing something one handed." These readings are the ones you learned with both of these kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は重いお米の袋を片手でヒョイと持ち上げました。
example_sentences.english: He easily lifted up the heavy bag of rice with one hand.

notes: "A one sided street is for one way only, because everything just goes in one direction." "The readings are the kun'yomi readings. You learned the reading from 片 already, and 道 is the vocab reading みち."

example_sentences.japanese: 大阪から東京までの片道切符を二枚もらえますか。
example_sentences.english: Can I get two one-way tickets from Osaka to Tokyo?

notes: "Prosperity in piles is a lot of prosperity!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: アメリカで最も隆盛を極めて入る州は何州ですか。
example_sentences.english: Which state is the most prosperous in the U.S.?

notes: "The people who will review a problem are those who know more about the problems. They are the advisors." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は良いバスケ部の顧問だとの評判があります。
example_sentences.english: Rumor has it, he’s a good coach for the basketball club.

notes: "If you dilute feeling from someone, they have no feelings. They become cold hearted." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は薄情者だし、どっちの味方かサッパリ分からないよ。
example_sentences.english: He is cold hearted and I have no idea whose side he’s taking.

english: Cutting Edge, Up-And-Coming, State Of The Art, Freshly Picked
notes: "Something that is new and sharp (presumably because it's so new) is on the cutting edge. It's up-and-coming, the next big thing!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: その会社は最新鋭のパソコンを購入することを決定しました。
example_sentences.english: The company decided to buy the cutting edge computer.

notes: "Something that is superior and elegant has much elegance and grace." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は自称「優雅なマダム」です。
example_sentences.english: "She is a self-appointed ""elegant madam."""

notes: "If you go towards filial piety, you are going to be doing filial piety. Do this for your parents." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 女房が死ぬ前に、もっと孝行しておくんだったな。
example_sentences.english: I wish I devoted myself more to my wife before she passed away.

notes: "Something that is frequently overgrown is something that is super frequent. It never stops attacking, never stops coming, and is honestly getting incessant in how often it overgrows. Those darn [put plant name here]." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: お前は頻繁にくだらない事を気にし過ぎなんだって。
example_sentences.english: You frequently sweat the small stuff.

notes: "A famous honor is still an honor, but it is also a prestige to have, since you are famously honorable. So prestigious! " This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: あいつは名誉を得ることには興味がないなんて言ってるけど、俺は嘘だと思うね。
example_sentences.english: He says he has no interest in gaining prestige, but I think that’s a lie.

notes: "A medicine dose is medicine or drugs you're taking." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 薬剤を使い終わったら、必ず薬剤入れに戻してください。
example_sentences.english: Make sure you put the medicine away in the medicine case after you use it.

english: Neighbor, Next To, Next Door Neighbor
notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Remember the movie ""Tonari (となり) no Totoro""? That is the Tonari. "

example_sentences.japanese: 子育ては隣町でしてたんですが、子どもたちがみんな大きくなったので主人と私はこの町に越して来たんですよ。
example_sentences.english: We raised our children in a neighboring town, then my husband and I moved to this town after they grew up.

notes: "A neighbor person is a neighbor." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の隣人は、幸運を呼ぶお守りを持っていることで有名です。
example_sentences.english: My neighbor is famous for having a charm that brings good luck.

notes: "All the near neighbors are the people who live around you and near you. They're a part of the neighborhood." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチ大統領は、近隣諸国との関係をないがしろにはしなかった。
example_sentences.english: President Koichi never ignored relationships with neighboring countries.

notes: "A neighbor house is a neighboring house. That house is right next to ours!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 隣家ではどうやら窓は新聞紙で拭くようです。
example_sentences.english: It seems that the people in the neighboring house wipe their windows with newspapers.

notes: "You've surpassed what is normal alertness. You are too alert. You notice everything. This is oversensitivity." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 過敏性大腸症候群に苦しんでいます。
example_sentences.english: I’m suffering from irritable colon syndrome.

notes: "A machine alert is an alert that is timed by a machine, not by a human. That is pretty quick and clever. Machines can move and think so much faster than us, after all." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: ウェイトレスってのは機敏に動くものなのに、彼女はとんでもなく鈍いんだよ。
example_sentences.english: Waitresses are supposed to move quickly, but she is ridiculously slow.

notes: "If you have an alert feeling, you are sensitive to things going on around you. That means you have a lot of sensitivity!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 耳がすっごい敏感だから、コショコショ話はしないで。
example_sentences.english: Please don’t whisper because my ears are really sensitive.

notes: "Something that is sharp will benefit from its sharpness, since that's all it has, really." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 通り魔は、鋭利な刃物で私の全身を切りつけた。
example_sentences.english: The random attacker slashed at my body with a sharp knife.

notes: "Someone on sharp alert has a sharpness about them. They are quick witted and have a strong keenness to them." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: その犬の鋭敏な嗅覚は、何人もの麻薬密売人を捕らえました。
example_sentences.english: That dog’s keen nose caught so many drug dealers.

notes: "Something is diluted to the point of weakness. It has much weakness and feebleness." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: お兄さんに言われたわ。あなたは意志薄弱だから私と別れることができないけど、本当は別れたいんだって。
example_sentences.english: Your brother told me that you are too weak-willed to break up with me, but that you really want to.

notes: "Things of the charcoal element are made up of much carbon. Just look deep into the charcoal to see all the carbon in there." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 一酸化炭素と二酸化炭素の違いは何ですか？
example_sentences.english: What’s the difference between carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide?

notes: "A ceremony ceremony is a ceremony." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨夜我が家で生贄の儀式が行われた。
example_sentences.english: The sacrificial ritual was held in my house last night.

english: Extremely Gruesome, Extremely Fierce, Extremely Violent
notes: "Something really terrible causing mass extinction will be extremely gruesome. It will also probably be extremely violent, so don't look." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You've learned them already, so you should be able to read this on your own!

example_sentences.japanese: 殺人現場は凄絶だった。
example_sentences.english: The murder scene was extremely gruesome.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の祖母は戦争を経験し、凄絶な時代を生きました。
example_sentences.english: My grandmother experienced a war and lived in an extremely fierce era.

example_sentences.japanese: たった今、世界の凄絶さを目にした気がした。
example_sentences.english: I feel like I just saw the extreme violence of this world with my own eyes.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it probably uses the kun'yomi reading. You did not learn this reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you: It turns out she is a fake. Your niece (にせ) was a robot this whole time, just pretending to be your niece. What is wrong with this world, where your niece can be an imitation niece. A 偽niece, if you will."

example_sentences.japanese: どうして俺が偽札を偽札じゃないということが皆の為になるのさ？
example_sentences.english: What benefit is there to telling everyone this forged document isn’t a forged document?

notes: "Tear off a one-sided piece. It's only one part, not all the parts. It's a fragment." "The 破 reading is the one you learned, the 片 reading isn't one you've learned. Just think about how you're tearing off pieces of a hen (へん), one fragment at a time. Here little chicken, I want another feather from you please. *CAW*"

example_sentences.japanese: 地面はガラスの破片だらけなので、気をつけて下さい。
example_sentences.english: The ground is covered with glass fragments, so be careful.

notes: "If lies puke (吐く) out of your mouth, you're a liar." "This is a combination of the kun'yomi readings, one of which you haven't seen yet. You'll see this word without the 吐 kanji too, but for now let's learn its kanji reading! You can't just tell one lie, it always turns into two (つ). Kind of like a chip or pretzel, you can't just have one. With lies, you have to open your mouth for two more. And then two more.... and... well you get it."

example_sentences.japanese: ウソップは嘘吐きだ。
example_sentences.english: Usopp is a liar.

example_sentences.japanese: フグ子ちゃん、大嘘つきの彼氏がいて、よくケンカするんだって。
example_sentences.english: Apparently, Fuguko has a boyfriend who is a complete liar and they fight quite often.

example_sentences.japanese: その時代、嘘吐きは全員燃やされていた。
example_sentences.english: In that era, all liars were to be burned.

notes: "The kanji and the word are exactly the same. A lie is a lie!" Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it probably uses the kun'yomi reading. You learned with reading with the kanji, so you should be able to read it already!

example_sentences.japanese: 嘘ですよね？
example_sentences.english: It's not true, is it?

example_sentences.japanese: 「嘘をつかない」は私のモットーです。
example_sentences.english: "My motto is, ""I will not tell a lie."""

example_sentences.japanese: 宝くじで1億円当たったなんて、嘘の話みたいで信じられない！
example_sentences.english: Saying you won 100 million yen in the lottery sounds like a lie, I can't believe that!

notes: "I have sincerity about my loyalty. That shows loyalty, right?" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 今振り返ってみると、ハチ公は絶対的な忠誠心を持ったいい犬だったよな。
example_sentences.english: Looking back, Hachiko was a dog that had absolute loyalty.

notes: "You have sincerity and you have truth. You are so sincere and honest and faithful, good friend." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は僕の誠実な友人だから、心配する必要は無いよ。絶対に取引から手を引いたりなんかしないさ。
example_sentences.english: He is my faithful friend, so don’t worry. He will never back out of the deal.

notes: "If 意識 is consciously, then what exists concealed in your mind is your subconscious." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 夢ってのは、僕たちの潜在意識を反映しているとよく言われるよね。
example_sentences.english: Dreams are often said to reflect our subconscious.

notes: "If you have attained summer, that must mean you finished out with the previous season and are going into summer. This is the summer solstice." "You didn't learn the 夏 reading with the kanji, so we'll have to come up with a mnemonic to remember the reading of summer solstice, especially the first half. Just think about how cute little geckos (げ) start to come out into the open during the summer solstice. It's too cold for them to be out in the open before that, so if you look outside at the right time, you'll see geckos popping out of the ground all over the place!"

example_sentences.japanese: 父に夏至から11日目のことを何と呼ぶか知っているかと聞かれたので、得意気に「ハゲ症」って答えたんですけど、それって「ハゲ頭の症状」って意味になるみたいで。父は笑って、正しい答えは「半夏生」だよって教えてくれましたけどね。
example_sentences.english: "My dad asked me if I knew what to call the eleventh day after the summer solstice, so I said triumphantly ""hageshou,"" which literally means ""baldness-symptom"". He laughed and told me the correct answer was ""hangeshou."""

notes: "If you are about to attain winter, then it's the winter solstice. Happy winter, everyone!" "The reading for 冬 is the on'yomi reading, and one you haven't learned before. You're going to want to think about how you are celebrating the winter solstice in one particular place, that place being とうきょう (とう). See the Tokyo landmarks around you, think that you are there on the winter solstice, and also think about the things you are doing to celebrate, here in Tokyo. Also, watch out for the rendaku."

example_sentences.japanese: どうして日本では冬至の日にカボチャを食べると良いというのですか？
example_sentences.english: Why do people say it’s good to eat squash on the winter solstice in Japan?

notes: "The middle hinge is the center pivot point." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: どうしてそれが彼女の中枢神経系を刺激したの？
example_sentences.english: How could it stimulate her central nervous system?

notes: "If you're overcome with brightness, you'll be able to see all the little fine detailed things." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 十年前の旧正月のことは、克明に覚えていますよ。
example_sentences.english: I have detailed memories of the Chinese New Year from ten years ago.

notes: "Something that is round and slippery just moves around with no trouble at all. It is so effortless in how it slides around. It is also super smooth." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 英語で円滑なコミュニケーションを取るために、最も重要なことは何だと思いますか？
example_sentences.english: What do you think the most important things are to have a smooth conversation in English?

notes: "You know how 孝行 is ""filial piety,"" right? Well, this is basically the same thing. You're just showing said filial piety to your parents, which, of course, is what filial piety means. That makes this word mean filial piety." "The reading is 孝行 plus the kun'yomi of 親. Put them together and you'll become a good filial child."

example_sentences.japanese: 何か両親に親孝行してあげたいと思っています。
example_sentences.english: I think I want to do something to show my filial piety toward my parents.

notes: "The char point is the part you're looking at so hard it burns a little hole in it. Just imagine yourself looking at a single point so hard that it begins to smolder. This is the focal point or the focus." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生が顕微鏡の焦点の合わせ方について説明をしてくれていた時、私は上の空でした。
example_sentences.english: When our teacher explained how to focus the microscope, I was spacing out.

notes: "If you have the ol' liver flame then you probably have hepatitis. AUGH! MY LIVER IS ON FIRE." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: あのA型肝炎の患者は愛に飢えており、いつも医者や看護師の気を引こうとしている。
example_sentences.english: The hepatitis A patient is starving for love and always tries to get attention from the nurses and doctors.

english: Lack Of Filial Piety, Disobedience To Parents
notes: "You know that 不孝 means ""disobedience to parents. So, if you add parents to it, it just means the same thing. Just a longer version of the word, basically. This means lack of filial piety or disobedience to parents." "The reading for 不孝 is the one you learned. Then, add 親's reading (vocab) to it."

example_sentences.japanese: もう手遅れですが、私は本当に親不孝な息子でしたよ。
example_sentences.english: It’s already too late, but I was a really disobedient son.

notes: "Your lawn of life is just your lawn. Of course it's alive, otherwise it wouldn't be a very good lawn." "The reading for 芝 is the one you learned with the kanji. The reading for 生 is one you haven't seen before (exception). It's ふ, and you can remember it by thinking how you were such a fool (ふ) for putting all that poison on it. Now it's dying, and now it's becoming less of a lawn."

example_sentences.japanese: この公園では、芝生の上を歩くのは禁止されています。
example_sentences.english: Walking on the lawn in this park is prohibited.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it probably uses the kun'yomi reading. You did not learn this reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you: What's the first two letters of the word mourning? It's mo (も). You can use that to remember."

example_sentences.japanese: 大変申し訳ありませんが、喪に服しているため年賀状が送れないのです。
example_sentences.english: I’m very sorry but I’m afraid I can’t send a New Year’s card because I’m in mourning.

notes: "You know that 透明 is ""transparency"" or ""transparent"" - so, if something is not transparent, then it is opaque, making this word opacity." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 不透明な窓がある女子の更衣室です。
example_sentences.english: The girls’ locker room has opaque windows.

notes: "A person's pattern is the pattern of actions which they take to become who they are. What do they usually do? What is their pattern? This is the same as their personal character or personality." "The readings are both kun'yomi readings, combined. For 人 you'll just have to remember this. With 柄 that's the reading you learned anyways, so that makes things easier. Just keep it consistent!"

example_sentences.japanese: 本の内容を表紙で判断するみたいに、人の人柄を見た目で決めつけないでよ。
example_sentences.english: Don’t judge people’s personalities by their appearance like you’d judge a book by its cover.

english: Portable Phone, Cell Phone, Mobile Phone
notes: "You know that 携帯 means ""portable"" or ""cell phone"" or ""mobile phone."" And then 電話 means ""telephone."" This is basically just the longer version of simply saying 携帯, making this a portable phone or cell phone or mobile phone. It's sort of like the difference between saying ""my cell"" and ""my cell phone,"" you dig?" "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. Will help to know the readings of 携帯 and 電話 for this one."

example_sentences.japanese: 「あなたの携帯電話をお借りしてもいいですか？」「ええ、どうぞ。」
example_sentences.english: """May I use your cell phone?"" ""Sure, go ahead."""

notes: "A sick bed is a sickbed. If you're in that bed, you're probably sick." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は病床に臥してついにまた起ちません。
example_sentences.english: He laid down on his sickbed, never to rise again.

notes: "Someone built from a small pattern has a small build. I know lots of little old ladies that were built from these small patterns." The readings for this word are both kun'yomi readings. You've learned both of these readings by now so you should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: その店では、一人の小柄なおばあさんが買い物をしていた。
example_sentences.english: The short old woman did her shopping alone in the store.

english: State Of The Art, Cutting Edge
notes: "最新 is, as you can probably guess, ""the newest."" So, the newest sharp thing, is the cutting edge. It is state of the art." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: かつて、少し前までは、3Dプリンタは最新鋭の機械でした。
example_sentences.english: Once, a little while ago, 3D printers were cutting edge machines.

notes: "Temporarily determine something. That makes it tentative and temporary." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: こちらの料金設定は暫定的ですのでご留意下さいませ。
example_sentences.english: Please bear in mind that these prices are temporary.

notes: "This is the na-adjective version of bright. The word is bright or cheerful." "Of all the people who are bright and cheerful, one man comes to mind. The cheerful Hulk Hogan (ほが)."

example_sentences.japanese: 朗らかな声をした知らない人から国際電話がかかってきました。
example_sentences.english: I got an international call from someone I didn’t know with a melodious voice.

notes: "A bright bright is something that's bright." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はかつては明朗快活な青年だった。
example_sentences.english: He used to be a cheerful young man.

notes: "A fake thing is fake or counterfeit." You've learned both of these readings already. No fakes there.

example_sentences.japanese: あの男、俺に偽物のグッチの財布を自慢してきたんだぜ。
example_sentences.english: That guy bragged about his fake Gucci wallet to me.

notes: "I'm going to expose my bones for a second here and be blunt with you... this makes sense, because if you're exposing your bones at someone, you're not hiding anything. You're being frank and blunt." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女があまりに露骨にものを言うもので、少々面食らいました。
example_sentences.english: I was pretty surprised at how blunt she was.

notes: "Gentle and peace. These are signs of gentleness." "You didn't learn this reading of 柔 with the kanji, so let's remember it a different way. You have to provide a lot of gentleness if you want to touch something that's new (にゅう) to this world... a puppy, a kitty, a baby, etc. Anything new needs gentleness."

example_sentences.japanese: あそこで柔和な笑みを浮かべている理髪師は、実はこの辺りのポン引き男どもの親分なんだ。
example_sentences.english: That gentle looking barber over there is actually this area’s pimp boss.

notes: "An instant sit is immediate. It's also instantaneous. Just imagine yourself sitting instantly. No time passes between when you were standing and sitting. The instantaneous nature of your sit is definitely... troubling." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 即座の結果は期待しないでください。
example_sentences.english: Please don’t expect immediate results.

notes: "An instant interest in something you didn't have interest in before? Well, time for some improvisation, because you're going to have to pretend you have interest in it (since you don't actually)." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. Watch out for the shortening of そく."

example_sentences.japanese: みんなは彼が即興で作った詩をすごいねと褒めたが、口先だけなのは見え見えでした。
example_sentences.english: Everyone told him that his impromptu poem was great, but it was obviously just lip service.

notes: "The idea of being courteous leads you to have more feelings of intimacy and kindness toward people. The more courteous someone is toward you (and vice versa), the more the closeness between the two of you grows." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: その弁護士さんとはもう何十年も懇意にしていましてね。
example_sentences.english: I’ve been close to that lawyer for decades.

notes: "A bog earth place is a place where the earth is boggy. That's a marshland or wetland." The readings are the ones you learned with the respective kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: もしかしたら、彼らがこの沼地にはドラゴンがいると言ってたのは、本当のことだったのかも。
example_sentences.english: Maybe they were telling the truth that there is a dragon in these swamplands.

notes: "The mountain peaks are just the mountains. Just because you can only see the peaks doesn't mean the rest of the mountain doesn't exist." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: この山岳地帯では、少なくともあと三ヶ月は冬の季節が続くだろうね。
example_sentences.english: Winter will continue for at least three more months in this mountain district.

notes: "Nourishing and fostering. The thing that gives you this is nourishment." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 風邪を引いたら、大豆だとか林檎だとか、滋養のある物を食べなさい。
example_sentences.english: When you get a cold, eat nourishing food like soy beans or apples.

notes: "A pasture teacher is one who leads his flock around through life. This is a pastor, minister, or clergyman." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 牧師さんはもう今日は教会を出ちゃいましたか？
example_sentences.english: Has the pastor already left the church for the day?

notes: "Relax in peace. Wherever you are that's allowing you to do this, it is certainly peace. You feel security too." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: あの忌まわしい家族が未来永劫安泰でいられるなんて、誰が信じたいと思う？
example_sentences.english: Who would want to believe that horrible family would have eternal peace?

notes: "The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. You can add the meanings curious and strange to this word as well." "The reading for this kanji is the same as the one you learned with the kanji. That in itself isn't too rare, wouldn't you say?"

example_sentences.japanese: あなたの珍増税政策の理論的根拠を述べてくださいよ。
example_sentences.english: What is the rationale behind your strange policy for increasing taxes?

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. The reading is the same as the one you learned with the kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: 「彼女は誰かしら。」「名前を知らないの？クラスであなたの後ろに座っているよ！」
example_sentences.english: """I wonder who that girl is."" ""You don’t know her name? She sits behind you in class!"""

notes: "Gold hair is blonde hair. Makes sense!" "The reading for 髪 isn't the one you learned. It's actually はつ, but it's getting rendaku'd here. So, to remember the reading of it for this word, just think about how if you were blonde, you'd wear many hats (はつ) to hide it. I have no idea why you'd hide it, but you can come up with a compelling reason that makes sense to you."

example_sentences.japanese: 金髪になりたかったので、コカコーラで髪を脱色しました。
example_sentences.english: I wanted to be blonde so I bleached my hair with Coca-Cola.

notes: "The kanji is distract and the adjective version is confusing or misleading. " "You know who is particularly confusing? That maggie (まぎ) girl. She's confusing because she uses magic (まぎ). Think of a Maggie you know, if possible."

example_sentences.japanese: 結局それはバスケットボールだったんですが、とても紛らわしかったです。私は完全に妊婦さんの大きなお腹だと思っていました。
example_sentences.english: It was a basketball after all, but it was really misleading. I thought it looked exactly like a pregnant woman’s stomach.

notes: "Having good luck is a good omen to have. Good luck means more good luck, right?" "This word uses the きち reading you learned with the kanji."

example_sentences.japanese: みんな、結婚式の日に吉日を選びたいのよ。
example_sentences.english: Everyone wants to choose a lucky day for their wedding.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. The reading is the same as the one you learned with the kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: やあ、コウイチ！俺、久しぶりにお前に会ったから、話したいことが山ほどあるよ。
example_sentences.english: Hey Koichi, we’ve got a lot to catch up on.

notes: "The left wing is the left wing, as in the ""left wing party"" or ""left wing politics"" or something like that." "The reading for 左 is the on'yomi reading, さ. You can remember this because the left wing uses saws (さ) to cut down their right wing enemies. Imagine left wing hippies sawing down old right wing conservatives. BBrrrrbbbbbbzzzzz!"

example_sentences.japanese: 取材であの左翼支持者の方とお会いできるのがとても楽しみです。
example_sentences.english: I am so excited that I get to meet with the left wing movement supporter for an interview.

english: Ominous, Sinister, Bad Luck, Ill Omen
notes: "Something that is not good luck is ominous and sinister. It's also bad luck and an ill omen." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: すごく不吉な夢を見たもんで、あんたのことが心配になってこうして電話をした訳さ。
example_sentences.english: I had such an ominous dream that it made me really worried about you, and that’s why I called.

notes: "A peach color is a peach color." The readings come from the vocab readings (and kanji readings, actually) of the two kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: 桃色のバンで母親が迎えにきた時は、恥ずかしかったですね。
example_sentences.english: I was embarrassed when my mom came to pick me up in the peach colored van.

notes: "The right wing is the right wing. As in, ""right wing politics"" or ""right wing beliefs.""" "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You haven't learned this reading for 右, so here's a mnemonic to help you:Those in the right wing love eating uni (う), not because they like the taste, but because uni is expensive. Picture some right-wing people in your mind right now and watch as they try really hard to pretend they like eating uni as they shovel buckets of it down their throats."

example_sentences.japanese: 自分は、極端な右翼思想を持って生まれたように感じます。
example_sentences.english: I feel that I was born with extreme right-wing ideas.

notes: "You know that 堅い is ""solid"" or ""tough."" When your hand is solid and tough, it's solid and steady. If your hand is shaky, it's the opposite, or something." "The reading is the two words 手 and 堅い combined together. Watch out for the rendaku."

example_sentences.japanese: 中々手堅い仕事みたいだから、葬儀屋になるための勉強をしようかなって思ってるんだよね。
example_sentences.english: I’m thinking of learning how to become an undertaker because it looks like a pretty secure job.

notes: "A wild wave will make for some stormy seas or raging waves. Don't go out in these kinds of waves." "The readings come from the kun'yomi readings of the kanji, 荒 (the secondary reading you learned with this kanji) and 波 (just the vocab version)."

example_sentences.japanese: アイツはまだ社会の荒波に揉まれた事のないただの若造だよ。
example_sentences.english: He is just a young boy who hasn’t been tossed in the stormy seas of life yet.

notes: "A dragon scroll is a dragon that's shaped kind of like a scroll, spinning around. This is a tornado." "The reading is the kun'yomi readings of the kanji. For 竜 just think about how it's a standing (立つ) dragon, because it would have to be if it's a tornado. Your まき reading comes from 巻く, but the kana is pushed into the kanji."

example_sentences.japanese: 昨夜、竜巻警報が出て、停電にもなりました。
example_sentences.english: There was a tornado warning and a power outage last night.

notes: "If something has a nothing edge, it's probably unrelated to what you're doing. There's no edge, your stuff always has edges." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: この田舎道は、渋滞とは無縁です。
example_sentences.english: This country road is free from traffic jams.

notes: "I with a ら on it makes it plural. It's less formal than 俺たち (if you've seen that word yet), but has the same meaning. It's we." The reading is the same as the kanji's reading.

example_sentences.japanese: ごめん。 俺らがこの会話をするのは明らかにすごく早すぎたよな。でも、ただ、俺はお前と結婚したいと思ってるってこと、言いたかったんだ。
example_sentences.english: I’m sorry. It’s obviously way too early for us to be having this conversation, but I just wanted to tell you that I want to marry you.

notes: "荒い is rough. Double that to 荒々しい and you have the same thing: wild or rough." "The reading comes from 荒い. Since you already know that 々 means it repeats, you already know this reading!"

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は荒々しい声で、寝ている時に奥さんが毎晩顔に小便を掛けてくることに怒り心頭していることを公言しました。
example_sentences.english: "He in a wild voice he proclaimed that he was totally “pissed off” at his wife for ""pissing"" on his face every night while he was sleeping."

notes: "A villain who is bad is the most atrocious and fiendish villain of them all." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 誰もが、その凶悪犯が刑務所で大人しく刑期を務めるのは無理だろうと思っていました。
example_sentences.english: Everyone believed that the atrocious criminal would not fare well in prison.

notes: "Your 趣味 is your hobby. It's the thing you do on habit. A bad hobby is a habit that you do all the time that's no good. This is a bad habit." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 母は、父が悪趣味な人形を集めることを禁止しました。
example_sentences.english: My mom forbade my dad from collecting tasteless dolls.

english: Completely Nude, Totally Nude, Completely Naked, Totally Naked
notes: "You're all naked, which makes you completely nude or totally nude." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 一度しかない人生だろ！なぁ！一緒に全裸でスカイダイビングしに行こうぜ。すんげぇいい経験になると思うんだよね。
example_sentences.english: You only live once! Come on. You should go skydiving nude with me. It would be a great experience for us.

notes: "An eating table is a dining table." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 私がお皿を洗うから、あなたは食卓を綺麗にしてくれる？いいかしら？
example_sentences.english: I’ll wash the dishes and you can set the table for me. Is that okay?

notes: "Skin color is flesh colored or skin colored." "The readings are the vocab kun'yomi readings of each kanji, 肌 and 色 combined into one."

example_sentences.japanese: その男は強引な押し売りで私に肌色のクレヨンを一箱売りつけました。
example_sentences.english: The guy used high pressure sales tactics to sell me a box of skin colored crayons.

notes: "A shade energy is a shady feeling. It's a feeling of gloom and melancholy." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: アイツのYoutubeビデオを見るまでは、てっきり陰気な男だと思っていたよ。
example_sentences.english: I was certain he was a melancholy guy until I saw his Youtube videos.

notes: "A far distance detachment is a distance that is far. It is long distance. Also remember that 距離 is a ""distance"" so a far distance is a long distance." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

notes: "Red diarrhea means there's blood in there and you're probably dying of dysentery! Have you been playing too much Oregon Trail? Either way, get to a doctor!" "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You haven't learned this reading for 赤 yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you:You know what dysentery isn't? Sexy (せき). That's right. If anyone tries to seduce you by saying they have dysentery and they'd like to share it with you, tell them how NOT sexy that is and get the heck away from them!"

example_sentences.japanese: 男女計5人から細菌性の赤痢が検出されました。
example_sentences.english: The dysentery bacteria was detected in five men and women total.

notes: "The lake shore is the lake shore!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 夏は、静かな湖畔のロッジで読書をしています。
example_sentences.english: In summer I read in a quiet lake shore lodge.

notes: "Buy something at bargain value and you'll be getting it at a really low price. Good for you!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 廉価版のゲームのパッケージって安物感丸出しだよな。
example_sentences.english: The game’s popular edition packaging feels cheap, doesn’t it?

notes: "Barbarians who live in fields, not even in huts or houses or anything, are called savage by people who DO live in huts and houses. They think if you live out in a field you're really uncivilized. But that's all a matter of opinion, I guess." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: そんな野蛮な人たちと付き合ってはいけません。
example_sentences.english: You must not associate with such savage people.

notes: "Tell a widow to shut up and she'll be silent for the rest of the day. That wasn't very nice. You're a mean person." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 寡黙で読書好きな男性がタイプです。
example_sentences.english: My type is a guy who likes reading in silence.

notes: "Sulfur that's yellow is still sulfur. It smells like rotten eggs, which are also kinda yellow." "The reading for this word is an exception. Here's a mnemonic to help you remember it:This sulfur smells like an eagle's OOHHH (いおう)!! Oh no. Sulfur smells... it smells... like an eagle's... OH.. Oh eww no."

example_sentences.japanese: この温泉には硫黄が含まれています。
example_sentences.english: There’s sulfur in this hot spring.

notes: "Someone who is ugly and mean can't hide their ugliness or meanness from the rest of us! If you're really mean, it shows on your face." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 老婆の幽霊が、醜悪な顔でこちらを睨んでいた。
example_sentences.english: The old woman’s ghost glared at me with her ugly face from over there.

notes: "This is a single kanji with an い on the end, meaning you know it's probably an adjective. What's the adjective form of ugly? It's ugly still!" "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: The most ugly thing you've ever seen was a mini cookie (みにく). Why would any one want a tiny cookie? Cookies should be huge, and enough to fill you up. The more you look at the mini cookie it seems to become uglier and uglier to you."

example_sentences.japanese: あの女は、顔は美しいが心は醜い。
example_sentences.english: That woman’s face is beautiful but her heart is ugly.
